row.title: Finite spacelike slab and normal flux charge

items.title: Finite coordinate boxes and their faces are compact Jordan sets
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ and let
$$Q=\prod_{j=1}^{m}[a_j,b_j]\subseteq\mathbb R^m, \qquad a_j<b_j.$$
Then $Q$ is compact and Jordan measurable, and its boundary has Jordan
content zero. For any product $R=\prod_{j=1}^m I_j$ where each $I_j$ is one
of $[a_j,b_j]$, $(a_j,b_j)$, $[a_j,b_j)$ or $(a_j,b_j]$, the set $R$ is a
bounded Jordan set with closure contained in $Q$. Every continuous
$f:Q\to\mathbb R$ is Riemann integrable over $R$. When $m\ge2$, each closed
coordinate face of $Q$ is compact and Jordan measurable in its own
$(m-1)$-dimensional coordinate space; the same endpoint-variant and
integrability conclusions hold for products in that face.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, §10.5.1 'Volume and Jordan measurable sets', Proposition 10.5.1
references.locator: Section 10.5.1 states and proves that a bounded set is Jordan measurable exactly when its boundary has measure zero. The thin-cover proof for coordinate-box faces is supplied locally.

items.title: Metric divergence density identity for a C¹ current
items.statement:
Assume the Countable Choice convention $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]] used by the smooth tangent-bundle structure in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth
Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-selected
connection $\nabla$, and let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart. Write
$w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$. Let $J$ be a $C^1$ vector field on $U$; the
connection derivative on such a field is defined by its usual chart formula
$$\nabla_bJ^a:=\partial_bJ^a+\Gamma^a{}_{cb}J^c,$$
whose coefficients are continuous. Then, throughout $U$,
$$\nabla_aJ^a=w^{-1}\partial_a(wJ^a).$$
The right-hand side is the chart expression of the scalar divergence
$\nabla_aJ^a$; no higher regularity of $J$ than $C^1$ is required.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III General Relativity, University of Cambridge lecture notes, 12 October 2022, §8.7 and §9.1, printed pp. 109–111 (PDF pp. 110–112)
references.locator: §8.7 relates current-form Stokes flux to metric divergence; §9.1 uses the metric divergence theorem. The C¹ extension is proved locally from the stated smooth-metric density identities.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos lecture notes, Michaelmas Term 2019, §3.2.4, printed pp. 110–112 (PDF pp. 117–119)
references.locator: The section states the curved-space divergence formula and the trace of the Christoffel symbols. Its displayed matrix-log derivation is not used for a Lorentzian metric with negative determinant; the local proof uses the exact cofactor-based published density lemma.

items.title: Finite spacelike slab and normal flux charge
items.statement:
Use a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ and an independent orientation, with the exact meanings in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The tangent-bundle smooth
structure follows the stated Countable Choice convention
[[def-countable-choice]]. Let $(U,x)$ be a positively oriented chart with
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and $x(U)=V\subseteq\mathbb R^4$. Coordinates here are
mathematical real coordinates; no physical units are assigned.

Choose real numbers $t_0<t_1$ and $a_i<b_i$ for $i=1,2,3$, and let
$$\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(a_i,b_i),\qquad \overline\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3[a_i,b_i],\qquad K=[t_0,t_1]\times\Omega,\qquad \overline K=[t_0,t_1]\times\overline\Omega\subset V.$$
The finite integration slab $K$ is a bounded Jordan set and its closure
$\overline K$ is a compact coordinate box. Assume $\overline K$ has an open
neighborhood in $V$ on which the spatial metric block
$h_{ij}:=g_{ij}$ is positive definite and the inverse-metric component
$g^{00}$ is negative. Thus each slice
$\Sigma_t=\{x^{-1}(t,x^1,x^2,x^3):(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\Omega\}$ is spacelike.
Assume also that the future unit normal defined below is future-directed in the
given time orientation. The closure $\overline K$, its closed coordinate
faces, the open spatial rectangle $\Omega$, the mixed-endpoint slab $K$, and
the corresponding mixed-endpoint side-face rectangles are Jordan sets by
[[lem-tgr-coordinate-boxes-are-compact-jordan]].

Write $g^{ab}$ for the inverse matrix to $g_{ab}$ and put
$$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|},\qquad \alpha:=(-g^{00})^{-1/2},\qquad n^a:=-\alpha g^{a0},\qquad n_a:=-\alpha\,\delta_a^0.$$
Then $n$ is the future unit normal to every $\Sigma_t$; its unit and normal
properties follow from $g^{ab}n_an_b=-1$ and
$g_{ab}n^b=n_a$. Let $dV_h:=\sqrt{\det(h_{ij})}\,dx^1dx^2dx^3$ be the
Riemannian volume element of the induced positive-definite slice metric.
In this positively oriented chart the metric volume form is
$\mathrm{vol}_g=w\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ by
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a).

A **current** here is a $C^1$ vector field $J=J^a\partial_a$ on an open
neighborhood of $x^{-1}(\overline K)$; equivalently, its coordinate components $J^a$
are $C^1$. Its current three-form is the pointwise contraction
$\omega_J:=\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g$, where
$(\iota_J\mathrm{vol}_g)(X_1,X_2,X_3):=
\mathrm{vol}_g(J,X_1,X_2,X_3)$. In coordinates,
$$\omega_J=w\bigl(J^0dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3 -J^1dx^0\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3 +J^2dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^3 -J^3dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\bigr).$$
The slice orientation is chosen so that the future unit normal precedes a
positive slice basis. Since $n^0=1/\alpha>0$ and the spacetime chart is
positive, this slice orientation is $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$; the
pullback of $\omega_J$ to $\Sigma_t$ is $wJ^0dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.
Define its signed **slice charge** (the normal flux through the spacelike
slice) by
$$Q_J(t):=\int_\Omega -g(J,n)\,dV_h.$$
Every displayed integral is the Riemann integral over the indicated bounded
Jordan set, as defined in
[[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]. The current and metric extend
continuously to the compact coordinate closure, and
[[lem-tgr-coordinate-boxes-are-compact-jordan]] proves that the open spatial
and mixed-endpoint rectangles are Jordan measurable and that these continuous
densities are Riemann integrable there.

Let $B$ denote the union of the six side faces of $K$, with outward boundary
orientation; each face is integrated over its relative interior, a bounded
Jordan rectangle whose closure is compact. The upper $x^i$ face has induced orientation
$(-1)^i dx^0\wedge\cdots\widehat{dx^i}\cdots\wedge dx^3$; the lower face
has its opposite. Thus the $i$th current-three-form pullback integrates to
the upper-minus-lower $wJ^i$ coordinate expression below. Define the
**net outward side flux** $\Phi_J(B)$ as the sum over
the three spatial coordinate directions of upper-face flux minus lower-face
flux. More explicitly, for $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $\Omega_i$ be the product
Jordan rectangle in the three coordinates other than $x^i$, with endpoint
convention $x^0\in[t_0,t_1]$ and $x^j\in(a_j,b_j)$ for $j\ne i$; then
$$\Phi_J(B):=\sum_{i=1}^3\int_{\Omega_i} \left. wJ^i\right|_{x^i=b_i}-\left. wJ^i\right|_{x^i=a_i}\,d^3x_{\widehat i}.$$
The integrals use the standard increasing-coordinate order on each face. For
a $C^1$ current the three-form coefficients are continuous, so the displayed
rectangular integrals exist. This extends the smooth-current flux convention
of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (b) to the present
finite coordinate faces. No unit normal to a side face is part of this
definition; in particular the flux form remains defined if a side face is
null. The term “charge” names this mathematical flux integral only; it does
not assert a physical conservation law or an entropy interpretation.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III General Relativity, University of Cambridge lecture notes, 12 October 2022, §§8.6–8.7, printed pp. 108–110 (PDF pp. 109–111)
references.locator: §8.6 gives integration of the metric volume form; §8.7 defines hypersurface integration by pullback and states Stokes' theorem and the non-null normal-flux formula. The local coordinate-box definition here supplies its own C¹-current convention.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos lecture notes, Michaelmas Term 2019, §§2.4.4–2.4.5 and §3.2.4, printed pp. 87–89 and 110–112 (PDF pp. 94–96 and 117–119)
references.locator: The notes define integration of forms and state Stokes' theorem, then give the curved-space divergence theorem. The local definition keeps side flux as a three-form/coordinate-face integral and does not require a unit normal on a null face.

items.title: Normal slice charge equals its coordinate density integral
items.statement:
Assume the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention and the spacelike slab data of
[[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]. For every slice $\Sigma_t$ and every
$C^1$ current $J$ in that definition, its normal flux charge is
$$Q_J(t)=\int_\Omega wJ^0\,d^3x,$$
where $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ is the metric density in the supplied chart.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III General Relativity, University of Cambridge lecture notes, 12 October 2022, §8.7, printed pp. 109–111 (PDF pp. 110–112)
references.locator: The non-null face flux formula identifies current flux with its unit-normal component times the induced metric volume density. The local block-matrix calculation here supplies the spacelike coordinate-slice specialization.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos lecture notes, Michaelmas Term 2019, §3.2.4, printed pp. 110–112 (PDF pp. 117–119)
references.locator: The divergence-theorem boundary expression uses the induced hypersurface metric density and unit normal. The exact coordinate lapse relation is proved locally here.

items.title: Complete finite-slab production and outward-flux balance
items.statement:
Assume the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ background of
[[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]. Let $K$, $\Sigma_t$, the $C^1$ current
$J$, its slice charge $Q_J(t)$ and its net outward side flux $\Phi_J(B)$ be
as in [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]. Use the oriented metric volume form
of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] clause (a). Put
$\Pi:=\nabla_aJ^a$, using the $C^1$ divergence of
[[lem-tgr-c1-current-density-divergence]]. Then the exact finite-slab balance
is
$$Q_J(t_1)-Q_J(t_0)+\Phi_J(B)=\int_K\Pi\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$
Here the four-volume integral is the Riemann integral on the bounded Jordan
slab $K$, whose compact closure is the supplied coordinate box. If
$\Pi\ge0$ everywhere on $K$, then
$Q_J(t_1)+\Phi_J(B)\ge Q_J(t_0)$. In particular, nonnegative local
production implies $Q_J(t_1)\ge Q_J(t_0)$ when the **net outward side flux**
is zero. If $\Pi=0$, the identity instead reads
$Q_J(t_1)-Q_J(t_0)=-\Phi_J(B)$, so zero production alone does not imply
constant slice charge.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III General Relativity, University of Cambridge lecture notes, 12 October 2022, §§8.6–8.7, printed pp. 108–110 (PDF pp. 109–111)
references.locator: §8.7 states Stokes' flux balance and the metric divergence theorem for non-null boundaries. The present proof is restricted to a finite coordinate box and proves the C¹ case directly.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos lecture notes, Michaelmas Term 2019, §3.2.4 and §4.5.5, printed pp. 110–112 and 187–189 (PDF pp. 117–119 and 194–196)
references.locator: §4.5.5 gives the current charge change plus boundary flux and requires no side outflow for equal slice charges. §3.2.4 states the smooth metric divergence theorem for purely spacelike or timelike boundaries. The coordinate-box proof here also allows null side faces because it uses the flux form/coordinate face integrals.

items.title: Zero divergence with decreasing slice charge in an open region
items.statement:
The following universal assertion is false: for every slab and current of
[[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]], pointwise nonnegative production
$\nabla_aJ^a\ge0$ implies nondecreasing slice charge
$Q_J(t_1)\ge Q_J(t_0)$ even when outward side flux is unrestricted.

references.title: Harvey Reall, Part III General Relativity, University of Cambridge lecture notes, 12 October 2022, §§8.6–8.7, printed pp. 108–110 (PDF pp. 109–111)
references.locator: Background for finite-slab current flux and the boundary term; the explicit vector field and all values in this counterexample are constructed and verified locally.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos lecture notes, Michaelmas Term 2019, §§3.2.4 and 4.5.5, printed pp. 110–112 and 187–189 (PDF pp. 117–119 and 194–196)
references.locator: Background for the curved-space divergence theorem, slice charge and outward side flux. The counterexample is a new mathematical construction, not a reported physical solution or observation.

row.title: Classical first-law product leaves entropy-temperature calibration free

items.title: Classical first-law product leaves entropy-temperature calibration free
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected smooth manifold, let $E,A,\kappa\in C^\infty(X,\mathbb R)$, and let $C>0$ be a constant with $\kappa(x)>0$ for every $x\in X$. Here $dE$ and $dA$ are the differential one-forms of the indicated functions, and equality of one-forms means pointwise equality on $X$. Assume the classical first-law product identity
$$dE=C\kappa\,dA.$$
For every constant $b>0$ and offset $s_*\in\mathbb R$, set $T_b:=b\kappa$ and $S_{b,s_*}:=(C/b)A+s_*$. Then $T_b dS_{b,s_*}=dE$. Distinct positive $b$ give distinct functions $T_b$, and changing $s_*$ changes $S_{b,s_*}$ without changing its differential. Thus this product identity alone does not determine the temperature scale or the absolute entropy offset.

The names $T_b$ and $S_{b,s_*}$ denote real-valued functions here; no operational temperature or physical entropy is assumed. If the symbols carry dimensions, consistency requires $[T]=[b][\kappa]$, $[S]=[C][A]/[b]$, and $[E]=[T][S]$. No particular unit system is used.

references.title: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Introduction to black hole thermodynamics, 78-page lecture notes, §§1.3 and 2.1, arXiv:2512.24929v1
Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, Living Reviews in Relativity 4 (2001), 6, §§2–3, arXiv:gr-qc/9912119v2

row.title: Classical first-law product leaves entropy-temperature calibration free — Examples

items.title: Two entropy-temperature calibrations preserve the same energy differential
items.statement: Use the abstract state family $X=(0,\infty)$ with coordinate $r$, and define $E(r)=r$, $A(r)=r$, $\kappa(r)=1$, and $C=1$. These are formal real-valued functions with no physical units assigned. Then $dE=C\kappa\,dA=dr$. The choices $b=1$ and $b=2$, with offset $s_*=0$, give $(T_1,S_{1,0})=(1,r)$ and $(T_2,S_{2,0})=(2,r/2)$.

references.title: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Introduction to black hole thermodynamics, 78-page lecture notes, §§1.3 and 2.1, arXiv:2512.24929v1
Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, Living Reviews in Relativity 4 (2001), 6, §§2–3, arXiv:gr-qc/9912119v2

items.title: A fixed scalar label and zero energy do not determine finite spectral entropy
items.statement:
On the complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$, a density matrix means a positive semidefinite $2\times2$ matrix $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Let the Hamiltonian be the zero self-adjoint matrix $H=0$, define its energy by $E_H(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho H)$, fix one positive real scalar label $a>0$, and fix a positive scalar $k_B>0$. Define the finite spectral entropy by
$$S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\rho)}\lambda\log\lambda,$$
where eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity, $\log$ is the natural logarithm, and $0\log0:=0$. The statement that the fixed data $(a,E_H(\rho))=(a,0)$ determine one value of $S(\rho)$ for every density matrix $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$ is false.

The scalar $a$ is held fixed as a mathematical label; $H$ is only the displayed finite matrix. No physical units, dynamics, horizon state, or coupling to geometry is part of this construction.

row.title: Finite Killing energy current and reference normalization

items.title: Finite Killing energy current and reference normalization
items.design_state: Finite Killing current, balance conditional on the present draft MI01 theorem, static proper-energy expression, covector unit distinctions, positive-generator rescaling, and conditional horizon-parameter rescaling.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike vector field selecting the future cone, as in clause (c) of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be an open chart domain and let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be a positively oriented smooth chart on $U$ whose image contains a neighborhood of the compact closure $\overline K=[x_0^-,x_0^+]\times\overline\Omega$ of the slab $K=[x_0^-,x_0^+]\times\Omega$, where $x_0^-<x_0^+$, $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(a_i,b_i)$ and $\overline\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3[a_i,b_i]$ with $a_i<b_i$. The chart orients $U$, which inherits the time orientation from $N$. Let $T^{ab}$ be a smooth symmetric contravariant rank-two tensor on $U$ satisfying $\nabla_aT^{ab}=0$, and let $\xi$ be a smooth Killing field on $U$. Use the induced Levi-Civita derivative on all tensor fields. With the inverse metric and index conventions of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] and [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]], set $\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ and $T_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$. Define the Killing current by
$$j_\xi^a:=-T^{ab}\xi_b .$$
On an open neighborhood of $\overline K$, write $h_{ij}:=g_{ij}$, assume $h$ is positive definite and $g^{00}<0$, and choose the time orientation so that $n^a=-\alpha g^{a0}$ is future-directed, where $\alpha:=(-g^{00})^{-1/2}$; the future unit normal is $n_a=-\alpha\delta_a^0$. Put $w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, and let $dV_h:=\sqrt{\det h}\,d^3x$ be the induced positive spatial volume element. For $x^0=s\in[x_0^-,x_0^+]$, define the finite slice charge
$$H_\xi(s):=\int_\Omega [-g(j_\xi,n)]\,dV_h=\int_\Omega T_{ab}n^a\xi^b\,dV_h .$$
Let $B$ be the union of the six side faces of $K$, and let $\Phi_J(B)$ be the net outward side flux defined in [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; explicitly it is the sum of the three upper-minus-lower face integrals of $wJ^i$ over the remaining coordinate variables. Conditional on the exact finite-slab balance stated in [[thm-tgr-finite-current-production-balance]],
$$H_\xi(x_0^+)-H_\xi(x_0^-)+\Phi_{j_\xi}(B)=0 .$$
Thus the endpoint charges are equal exactly when the net outward side flux is zero; divergence-free current alone does not imply that equality. The balance uses precisely the open spatial rectangle and compact-closure convention of that theorem.

In the static subcase on $U$, assume $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ is future timelike and orthogonal to these coordinate slices, so $g_{0i}=0$ and the future unit normal is $u^a=n^a=\xi^a/\mathcal N_\xi$, where $\mathcal N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$. Define $\epsilon:=T_{ab}u^au^b$. Then the same finite charge is the redshifted energy functional
$$H_\xi(s)=\int_\Omega \mathcal N_\xi\,\epsilon\,\sqrt{\det h}\,d^3x .$$
This is a matter-current charge on the specified finite slice, not a general gravitational energy.

For every constant $a>0$, replacing $\xi$ by $\widetilde{\xi}=a\xi$ preserves the Killing equation and gives $\widetilde j=a j$ and $\widetilde H=aH$. In the static subcase it also gives $\widetilde{\mathcal N}_\xi=a\mathcal N_\xi$ and the same normalized field $u=\xi/\mathcal N_\xi$. In the SI convention below, $a$ is dimensionless. If a function $\vartheta:U\to(0,\infty)$ is supplied and interpreted as the local temperature assigned to the observer field $u$, with SI unit kelvins, define $\mathcal T_\xi(q):=\mathcal N_\xi(q)\vartheta(q)$ for $q\in U$. No regularity of $\vartheta$ is needed for this pointwise definition. Then $\mathcal T_{a\xi}=a\mathcal T_\xi$; no equilibrium or constancy of $\mathcal T_\xi$ is asserted.

For the SI reading, take length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and spatial coordinates $x^i$ in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the metric components are dimensionless, and $\xi$ is normalized so that its flow parameter has units of length, hence its components are dimensionless. At any $q\in U$, let $p,k,\pi\in T_q^*U$ be covectors whose components have units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and $\mathrm J$, respectively, interpreted as mechanical momentum, wave, and energy-valued covectors. These labels assign physical interpretations and units only; no motion law or identification between $p,k,\pi$ is assumed. Let $\hbar$ be a supplied constant with SI unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$. These are pointwise pairings, so no regularity beyond the stated covectors is needed. If $T_{ab}$ has components in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, then $H_\xi$ is in joules. At each $q\in U$, the mechanical pairing $E_\xi(p;q):=-c\,p_a\xi^a(q)$ has units of joules. The wave pairing $E_\xi(k;q):=-\hbar c\,k_a\xi^a(q)$ also has units of joules, while the energy-valued covector pairs as $E_\xi(\pi;q):=-\pi_a\xi^a(q)$ with no extra factor of $c$. The rescaled covector $p^\pi_a:=\pi_a/c$ has mechanical momentum units. Each pairing scales linearly with $\xi$.

For an additional horizon clause, let $\mathcal H\subset U$ be a smooth embedded codimension-one submanifold whose induced metric is degenerate at every point (the null-hypersurface condition). Assume $\xi$ is nonzero and tangent to $\mathcal H$, and suppose a function $\kappa_\xi:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R$ is defined there by $\nabla_\xi\xi=\kappa_\xi\xi$ along $\mathcal H$. Then the rescaled generator satisfies $\kappa_{a\xi}=a\kappa_\xi$. In geometric units where the flow parameter has length, $\kappa_\xi$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; the associated acceleration normalization is $c^2\kappa_\xi$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. No existence or constancy of a horizon surface gravity, or temperature law, is asserted.

items.title: Zero Killing contraction makes the sourced Killing current divergence-free
items.design_state: Sourced stress with zero Killing contraction; its local divergence argument is complete and its finite-slab conclusion is conditional on the present draft MI01 balance theorem.
items.statement: Use the time-oriented Lorentzian open set, smooth metric, metric-selected connection, Killing field, positively oriented finite coordinate slab with compact closure, and finite-slab conventions of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]], including its definitions of $h_{ij},n_a,w,j_\xi,H_\xi$ and the net outward side flux $\Phi_{j_\xi}(B)$. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by its connection construction. Let $T^{ab}$ be smooth and symmetric and let $f^b$ be a smooth vector field such that $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$; this replaces the conserved-stress hypothesis for this corollary. If $f^b\xi_b=0$, then $\nabla_a j_\xi^a=0$, and, conditional on the finite-slab balance theorem [[thm-tgr-finite-current-production-balance]] at its actual interface, the finite slice charges satisfy $H_\xi(x_0^+)-H_\xi(x_0^-)+\Phi_{j_\xi}(B)=0$. Thus the endpoint charges are equal exactly when the net side flux is zero. In the static subcase, assume $\xi=\mathcal N_\xi u$ with $\mathcal N_\xi>0$; the algebraic zero-work condition $u_bf^b=0$ then implies $f^b\xi_b=0$. No infinite-domain or exhaustion limit is asserted.

items.title: Reference-wall normalization preserves proper thermal and particle ratios
items.design_state: Finite static cavity reference point sets the selected Killing lapse to one and rescales finite charge while preserving proper-temperature and proper-particle-energy ratios; inputs remain draft.
items.statement:
Use the static subcase, finite coordinate slab, and open chart domain $U$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. Adopt that lemma's SI convention: $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$, the spatial coordinates $x^i$ are in metres, $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and the metric components and length-normalized Killing field are dimensionless. Let $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ be future timelike and orthogonal to the coordinate slices, and put $\mathcal N_\xi(q):=\sqrt{-g_q(\xi_q,\xi_q)}>0$ and $u_q:=\xi_q/\mathcal N_\xi(q)$ for $q\in U$. Let $W\subset U$ be a specified smooth embedded codimension-one submanifold whose induced metric has signature $(-,+,+)$ (a timelike cavity wall), and choose a reference event $q_{\rm ref}\in W$ in the static region. Put $\mathcal N_{\rm ref}:=\mathcal N_\xi(q_{\rm ref})>0$, which is dimensionless in this convention. No asymptotically flat end is assumed. Supply a function $\vartheta:U\to(0,\infty)$ assigned units kelvins and interpreted as the local proper temperature measured by observer field $u$, and a covector field $p$ on $U$ whose components have units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. When a particle-energy interpretation is used, supply a vector field $P$ on $U$ that is future-directed and causal and satisfies $p_q=g_q(P_q,\cdot)$ at each $q\in U$; its components then have the same units as $p$ because the metric is dimensionless. Define, pointwise on $U$, $\mathcal T_\xi(q):=\mathcal N_\xi(q)\vartheta(q)$ and $E_\xi(p;q):=-c\,p_q(\xi_q)=-c\,p_a(q)\xi^a(q)$. Rescale the generator by $\widehat\xi:=\xi/\mathcal N_{\rm ref}$. The reference lapse is then $\widehat{\mathcal N}_\xi(q_{\rm ref})=1$, while the normalized temperature and particle-energy ratios at every $q\in U$ are unchanged:
$$\frac{\mathcal T_{\widehat\xi}(x)}{\widehat{\mathcal N}_\xi(x)}=\frac{\mathcal T_\xi(x)}{\mathcal N_\xi(x)}=\vartheta(x),\qquad \frac{E_{\widehat\xi}(p;x)}{\widehat{\mathcal N}_\xi(x)}=\frac{E_\xi(p;x)}{\mathcal N_\xi(x)}=-c\,p_a(x)u^a(x).$$
For each slice charge defined in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]], $H_{\widehat\xi}=H_\xi/\mathcal N_{\rm ref}$. This choice is meaningful in a finite cavity without an asymptotic normalization; it does not make $\vartheta$ spatially constant or assert that distinct reference-wall choices produce equal local temperatures.

row.title: Rest fluid state,frame and geometric current definitions

items.title: Rest fluid state, frame and geometric current definitions
items.statement:
Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

items.title: Local Gibbs, Euler, parcel first law and response identities
items.statement:
Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be nonempty and open, let $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$, and define
$$Y:=\{(n,s)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R:(1/n,s/n)\in X\},\qquad \varepsilon(n,s):=n\,e(1/n,s/n).$$
For $(n,s)\in Y$, put $v=1/n$, $\sigma_p=s/n$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, $H=e+pv$, $h=\varepsilon+p=nH$, and $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Then the following identities hold as equalities of differentials on $Y$:
$$d\varepsilon=T\,ds+\mu\,dn,\qquad \varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n,\qquad dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu.$$

For parcel totals $\mathsf S\in\mathbb R$ (entropy), $\mathsf V>0$ (proper volume), and $\mathsf N>0$ (marker count) with $(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X$, define
$$E(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):=\mathsf N\,e(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N).$$
Then $E$ is $C^2$, is positively homogeneous of degree one, and satisfies
$$dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N,\qquad E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N.$$
If $E$ is viewed on its open domain in $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, its Hessian annihilates the radial vector $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$.

The local response statements are conditional. At a state with $T>0$ and $e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}>0$, temperature is a valid local coordinate at fixed $v$, and the per-marker heat capacity
$$c_v:=\left(\frac{\partial e}{\partial T}\right)_v=\frac{T}{e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$, the isentropic compressibility
$$\kappa_{\sigma_p}:=-\frac1v\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial p}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac1{v e_{vv}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$ and $h>0$, the local pressure-energy response
$$\alpha_{\sigma_p}:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\varepsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n h}$$
is positive. If $X$ is convex and $e$ is convex on $X$, then $D^2e$ is positive semidefinite. Positivity of the displayed diagonal responses is not asserted to imply convexity, a sound cone, or an evolution theorem.

items.title: Observer projections, pointwise Eckart vector and local C¹ Landau field
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal V$ be a four-dimensional real vector space and let $g:\mathcal V\times\mathcal V\to\mathbb R$ be a symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, meaning that in some basis its matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. A vector $X$ is timelike when $g(X,X)<0$, and null when $X\ne0$ and $g(X,X)=0$. Choose one connected component $C^+$ of the timelike set $\{X:g(X,X)<0\}$ as the future cone; a timelike vector is future-directed when it belongs to $C^+$. Components and connectedness use the basis-independent finite-dimensional real vector-space topology. Lower indices with $g$ and raise them with its inverse, summing repeated upper/lower indices over $0,1,2,3$. Let $u\in C^+$ be unit timelike, $g(u,u)=-1$, and define $\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b$ as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. For every vector $J\in\mathcal V$ and symmetric contravariant rank-two tensor $\mathsf T$ on $\mathcal V$, the following statements hold.

1. The operator $\Delta$ is the $g$-orthogonal projection onto $u^\perp$, and
$$J^a=\nu_u u^a+V^a,\qquad \nu_u=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b,$$
is the unique decomposition with $V\in u^\perp$.

2. With
$$\varepsilon_u=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\quad Q^a=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\quad P^{ab}=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
one has the unique decomposition
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon_u u^a u^b+u^aQ^b+Q^a u^b+P^{ab}.$$
The scalar $p_{\mathrm{mech}}=\tfrac13g_{ab}P^{ab}$ and tensor $\pi^{ab}=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}$ satisfy $u_aQ^a=u_aP^{ab}=0$, $u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Also, $Q=0$ if and only if $u$ is a timelike eigenvector of $\mathsf T^a{}_b$.

3. If $J$ is future timelike, then
$$u_E:=\frac{J}{\sqrt{-g(J,J)}}$$
is the unique future unit timelike observer vector for which the spatial number current vanishes, $\Delta_{u_E}J=0$, where $\Delta_{u_E}{}^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u_E^a(u_E)_b$ is the clause-1 projection computed using $u_E$. Call $u_E$ the pointwise Eckart observer vector associated with $J$; it is a vector, not a chart or a tetrad.

4. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $O\subset M$ be open, and let $\mathsf T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field on $O$. At $x_0\in O$, choose an open neighborhood $O_0\subset O$ and a smooth future tetrad $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ on $O_0$ as supplied by [[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]], and put $u_0:=E_0(x_0)$ and $\Delta_0{}^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u_0^a(u_0)_b$. Define $\mathbb B^3:=\{w\in\mathbb R^3:\sum_{i=1}^3(w^i)^2<1\}$ and, for $x\in O_0$ and $w\in\mathbb B^3$, define
$$u(x,w):=(1-|w|^2)^{-1/2}\left(E_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^3w^iE_i(x)\right)\in T_xM.$$
The tetrad equations make $u(x,w)$ future unit timelike. If
$$\mathsf T^{ab}(x_0)=\varepsilon_0 u_0^a u_0^b+p_0\Delta_0^{ab},\qquad h_0:=\varepsilon_0+p_0>0,$$
then there are a neighborhood $U\subset O_0$ of $x_0$ and an open neighborhood $W\subset\mathbb B^3$ of $0$ such that there is a unique $C^1$ map $w_L:U\to W$ for which $u_L(x):=u(x,w_L(x))$ satisfies $Q_{u_L(x)}(x)=0$ for every $x\in U$. Thus $u_L$ is a $C^1$ observer field, meaning a $C^1$ vector field whose values are future unit timelike; it is distinct from the chosen tetrad field and from any coordinate chart. This is a local result; no far-from-equilibrium or global Landau-field existence is asserted.

5. In a Lorentz vector space, for every nonzero null vector $\ell$ and $\rho>0$, the pointwise tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}=\rho\ell^a\ell^b$ has no timelike eigenvector. Hence no future unit timelike observer vector has $Q=0$ for this tensor, so no pointwise Landau observer vector exists.

row.title: Rest fluid state,frame and geometric current definitions — Examples

items.title: Parcel derivatives and rest-energy shift
items.statement:
Let $e_0\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$ be any specified single-marker state function on a nonempty open state domain $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$. Fix a mass per marker $m\ge0$ with units $\mathrm{kg\,marker^{-1}}$ and $c>0$ with units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and define
$$e_m(v,\sigma_p):=e_0(v,\sigma_p)+mc^2.$$
Then $e_m\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. The derived temperature and pressure are unchanged, while $H_m=H_0+mc^2$, $\mu_m=\mu_0+mc^2$, $\varepsilon_m=\varepsilon_0+nmc^2$, and $h_m=h_0+nmc^2$. For parcel totals, $E_m(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)=E_0(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)+\mathsf Nmc^2$. This is a mathematical change of the state function by a constant rest-energy offset, not an empirical statement about a material.

Nicolas Borghini, Elements of Hydrodynamics, University of Bielefeld lecture notes (2015), §§IX.2 and Appendix A

row.title: Thermodynamics-GR fields, currents, reference normalization and units

items.title: Thermodynamics-GR fields, currents, reference normalization and units
items.statement:
Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, as defined in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. A chart is a smooth coordinate map; an observer congruence is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$; its integral curves, an adapted chart, and a tetrad field are distinct objects. The exact regularity and rest-space conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and the chart/congruence distinction of [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] apply. An orthogonal family of rest slices is not available for every congruence.

For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The roles of these quantities as primitive model inputs are framework-specific. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. Define the lapse $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and unit observer $u_\xi:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a supplied proper-temperature scalar $T>0$ in kelvins, define the Killing-normalized temperature field $T_\xi:=N_\xi T$. It is not assumed constant; if a separate equilibrium argument proves constancy on its stated domain, denote that value by $T_K$. The finite matter charge and its side-flux convention are those in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]] and [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; their charge-balance clause retains its explicitly conditional finite-slab hypotheses. This charge is not a general gravitational energy.

Keep covector types separate. A mechanical momentum covector $p_a$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$; its Killing energy is $E_\xi(p):=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ in joules. An energy-valued covector $\pi_a$ already has units joules and pairs as $E_\xi(\pi):=-\pi_a\xi^a$, without another factor of $c$. An inverse-length wave covector $k_a$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and pairs as $E_\xi(k):=-\hbar c\,k_a\xi^a$. For a specified charged stationary gauge, charge $q$ has coulombs and a potential covector $A_a$ in length coordinates has units $\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$; when a global stationary potential is actually defined, $\Phi_\xi:=-cA_a\xi^a$ has volts and $q\Phi_\xi$ has joules. A charged energy or chemical-potential convention requires its stated gauge and reference; no global potential, electrochemical equilibrium, or constancy is asserted here.

When $T_K>0$ is supplied, distinguish the inverse-temperature vector $\beta^a:=u_\xi^a/(k_BT)=\xi^a/(k_BT_K)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, from the scalar $\beta_K:=1/(k_BT_K)$, also in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a quantum statistical model, let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra: an associative complex algebra with nonzero identity $1$, a complete norm satisfying $\|AB\|\leq\|A\|\,\|B\|$, and a conjugate-linear involution $A\mapsto A^*$ satisfying $(A^*)^*=A$, $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$, and $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$. Its elements represent bounded observables. Let $\{\alpha_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ be bijective complex-linear maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserving multiplication and involution, with $\alpha_t(1)=1$, $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}$, and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$; require $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ to be norm-continuous for every $A\in\mathcal A$. A state is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\geq0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. For $b>0$ in the chosen flow-parameter units, define $S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq b\}$. The state $\omega$ satisfies the KMS condition at width $b$ when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ with $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$, continuous on $S_b$ and complex-differentiable at every point of its interior, such that

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

This all-observable boundary-value definition uses no separately declared analytic subalgebra. With the quantum statistical calibration $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$, a physical-time parameter $t$ in seconds has KMS width $b_t=\hbar\beta_K$ seconds. If the flow parameter is length $\lambda=ct$, use the reparameterized group $\widetilde\alpha_\lambda:=\alpha_{\lambda/c}$; its KMS width is $b_\lambda=c\hbar\beta_K$ metres. These are unit and parameter-convention assignments only. This definition introduces no Hilbert-space operator $H_K$ and does not identify the abstract automorphism flow or its strip width with the finite matter charge $H_\xi$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. This item asserts neither the existence of an observable algebra or flow for a given thermodynamic-gravity model nor the existence of a KMS state or equilibrium.

On a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H\subset M$,
write $i:\mathcal H\hookrightarrow M$ for the inclusion. A generator $\chi$
here is a smooth section of $i^*TM$ with $\chi_p\in T_p\mathcal H$
nonzero and null at each $p\in\mathcal H$. For a smooth tangent field $X$
on $\mathcal H$ and a smooth vector field $V$ along it, define
$\nabla_XV:=(i^*\nabla)_XV$ by [[def-pullback-connection]], applied to the
ambient tangent bundle and its metric-selected connection. The prescription
is independent of frames by
[[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. In particular,
$\nabla_\chi\chi$ is a vector field along $\mathcal H$ and needs no chosen
ambient extension. If $\chi$ is the restriction of a smooth ambient field
$\widetilde\chi$, the same theorem gives
$\nabla_\chi\chi=(\nabla_{\widetilde\chi}\widetilde\chi)|_{\mathcal H}$;
thus this convention also covers the supplied ambient Killing generators.
The generator may admit a scalar $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ defined by
$\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa_{\rm geom}\chi$. When the flow parameter has length units, $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; the corresponding acceleration-unit quantity $\kappa_{\rm acc}:=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. This definition does not assert a horizon exists, that $\kappa$ is constant, or that a temperature law follows. The formula $T_K=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}/(2\pi k_B)$ requires a specified quantum/semiclassical model, and an area-entropy formula requires a separate thermodynamic identification. In particular, equal units do not identify local material entropy, finite statistical entropy, and area entropy, and no generalized second law is asserted here.

items.title: Restricted local equilibrium parcel with adopted material state function
items.statement:
For a selected fixed-composition, single-material branch, adopt a local-equilibrium description on an open state domain $D\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ with a supplied function $e\in C^2(D,\mathbb R)$ and $T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e>0$. Here $v$ is the rest volume per selected material marker, $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, and $e$ is energy per marker, including the rest-energy contribution; their types and SI units are those in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Here “comoving” means that local state values are referred to the observer-congruence rest spaces of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]; no orthogonal rest-slice foliation or finite-region volume integral is presupposed. For an admissible local continuum parcel, let $N_p>0$ be its real marker amount, $V>0$ its supplied proper-volume parameter, and $S\in\mathbb R$ its supplied total entropy, with $(V/N_p,S/N_p)\in D$. The quantities $V/N_p$ and $S/N_p$ have the per-marker state meanings and units of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. This model assigns energy $E=N_p e(V/N_p,S/N_p)$. Treating the real marker amount as a particle count is part of the fixed-composition continuum model, not a claim about discrete microscopic transitions or a consequence of the mathematical marker definition.

This is an adopted constitutive/local-equilibrium premise for the stated material and regime. It does not derive $e$ microscopically, assert a measured equation of state, impose a spacetime conservation equation, imply a universal gas law, or make the local parcel energy additive with the energy of an arbitrary self-gravitating region. Rest energy belongs in $e$; if a rest mass $m$ is specified, its contribution is $mc^2$, not $m$ in SI units. No entropy-maximization, quantum Gibbs representation, or global gravitating thermodynamic limit is assumed.

items.title: Local entropy-current admissibility in a separately defined model
items.statement:
On an open region of the smooth spacetime of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], take a separately specified material/current model in its declared smooth regime. Its entropy current is a supplied $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ of the type and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Adopt the local admissibility condition

$$\nabla_aS^a\geq 0$$

throughout that region. This inequality is a physical restriction on the chosen model and current; it is not a construction of an undefined constitutive current. Each application must state its current, regime, boundary/exchange data, and any source or sink terms it includes.

The inequality is not deduced from Lorentzian geometry, the local state function, or finite data. It does not assert statistical thermalization, a universal microscopic $H$-theorem, entropy-area identification, or a generalized second law. Romatschke's cited calculation is restricted to a specified conformal-fluid model and itself records the absence of experimental verification known to that author; that source limitation does not turn this postulate into an observed law. No experimental observation or uncertainty is supplied by this item.

items.title: Conditional finite entropy balance with explicit boundary flux
items.statement:
Use the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry, positively oriented chart and product slab $K=[x^0_-,x^0_+]\times\Omega$ with open spatial rectangle $\Omega$ and compact closure $\overline K$ of [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]], with nonempty rectangular factors, spacelike slices, future unit normal $n$, induced volume $dV_h$, and a $C^1$ current defined on a neighborhood of $\overline K$. Let $S^a$ be the entropy current selected by [[post-tgr-local-entropy-admissibility]] and put $\Pi:=\nabla_aS^a\geq0$ on $K$. Define the proper slice entropy

$$Q_S(x^0):=\int_\Omega[-g(S,n)]\,dV_h$$

and let $\Phi_S(B)$ be the net outward flux through the union $B$ of the six spatial side faces, with the sign convention of [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]. Conditional on the exact current statement and hypotheses of the **draft** mathematical theorem [[thm-tgr-finite-current-production-balance]],

$$Q_S(x^0_+)-Q_S(x^0_-)+\Phi_S(B)=\int_K\Pi\,\mathrm{vol}_g\geq0.$$

Every term has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ in the length-coordinate convention of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. If the net outward side flux is zero, then the endpoint charges satisfy $Q_S(x^0_+)\geq Q_S(x^0_-)$. This is a deduction conditional on both the adopted local inequality and the actual draft supplier interface; it is not an observation, a proof approval of that mathematical supplier, or a generalized second law.

items.statement:
Take the finite chart slab, current and local-admissibility assumptions of [[pthm-tgr-finite-entropy-balance]]. Call the side boundary entropy-impermeable in this setup when the pullback of the entropy-current flux three-form vanishes on every side face; this implies $\Phi_S(B)=0$. Then, conditional on the current draft supplier chain recorded by [[pthm-tgr-finite-entropy-balance]],

$$Q_S(x^0_+)-Q_S(x^0_-)=\int_K\Pi\,\mathrm{vol}_g\geq0.$$

If $\Pi=0$ throughout the slab, the endpoint charges are equal. This is an idealized model prediction, not a reported experiment. It does not identify this finite material entropy with horizon area or exterior quantum entropy, and does not assert a global generalized second law.

row.title: Perfect stress and particle balances with entropy identity

items.title: Perfect stress and particle balances with entropy identity
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, let $\nabla$ be its metric-compatible torsion-free connection, and
let $u$ be a smooth future-directed vector field with $g(u,u)=-1$. Put
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$,
$a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and $\Delta^b{}_a=\delta^b{}_a+u^bu_a$.
Take a smooth fixed-composition state from [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] with
$n>0$, $T>0$, $s=n\sigma_p$, and $h=\epsilon+p=Ts+\mu n$ as in
[[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. Define the perfect stress tensor and particle
current by

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^a u^b+p\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a.$$

For any smooth vector field $f^b$, the balance equation $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$
is equivalent to the pair

$$D\epsilon+h\theta=-u_bf^b,\qquad ha^c+\Delta^{ca}\nabla_a p=\Delta^c{}_bf^b,$$

and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ is equivalent to $Dn+n\theta=0$. Whenever both balances
hold, the exact entropy identities are

$$T\nabla_a(su^a)=-u_bf^b,\qquad nT D\sigma_p=-u_bf^b.$$

In particular, when $f=0$, the entropy current $su$ is divergence-free and
specific entropy is advected, $D\sigma_p=0$. These are conditional identities
for supplied smooth fields; they assert no solution existence or physical
applicability beyond the stated model data.

items.title: Enthalpy vorticity and restricted material circulation
items.statement:
Use the state, signature, connection, and perfect-fluid data of
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]], with
$f=0$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. On their common open domain $O$, assume both
isolated balance equations

$$\nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,\qquad T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+p\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Put $v=1/n$, $H=(\epsilon+p)/n=e+pv$, and let
$c>0$ be the fixed speed-of-light normalization in the convention $x^0=ct$.
For the momentum one-form $P=(H/c)u^\flat$, consider a smooth closed curve
$\gamma_0:[0,1]\to O$ with equal endpoint values and a local flow
$\Phi_\lambda$ of $u$ in $O$ defined on a neighborhood of its compact image. Write
$\gamma_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda\circ\gamma_0$ and
$\mathcal C(\lambda)=\int_{\gamma_\lambda}P$. Then

$$\iota_u d(Hu^\flat)=T\,d\sigma_p,\qquad \frac{d\mathcal C}{d\lambda}=\frac1c\int_{\gamma_\lambda}T\,d\sigma_p.$$

Consequently, circulation is conserved if $\sigma_p$ is constant on the
region swept out by the loop. The local identity does not assert circulation
conservation merely from $D\sigma_p=0$, nor does it assume a global flow,
complete spacetime, or shock solution.

items.title: Frame-qualified dissipative entropy cancellation
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$, $u$, $\nabla$, and the fixed-composition state be as in
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]], with
$g(u,u)=-1$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. Define
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $\Delta_{ab}=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$\Delta_a{}^b=\delta_a{}^b+u_au^b$, and $D=u^a\nabla_a$,
$\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and the spatial symmetric
trace-free shear

$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)} -\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$

where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Suppose smooth fields
$\Pi$, $Q^a$, $V^a$, and $\pi^{ab}$ obey $u_aQ^a=u_aV^a=0$,
$u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $\pi^{ab}$ is symmetric with $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Set

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab} +u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a+V^a.$$

If $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$ and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$, the vector field

$$S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T}$$

satisfies the exact identity

$$\nabla_aS^a=-\frac{\Pi\theta+\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T} -\frac{Q^a(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)}{T^2} -V^a\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\mu}{T}\right)-\frac{u_bf^b}{T}.$$

This identity applies to the stated smooth fields and conventions; it does not
select a constitutive law or assert that any such fields solve an evolution
problem.

items.title: Positive first-order residual and actual instability/tail counterexamples
items.statement:
Use the smooth state, frame, and dissipative stress/particle decomposition of
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]].
Assume the stress and particle balances $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$ and
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$. Let $c>0$, $T>0$, and let $\eta,\zeta,\kappa,L\ge0$. Impose

$$\Pi=-\zeta c\theta,\quad \pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab},\quad Q^a=-\frac{\kappa}{c}\Delta^{ab}(\nabla_bT+Ta_b),\quad V^a=-L\Delta^{ab}\nabla_b(\mu/T).$$

On any branch with no rest-frame work, $u_bf^b=0$ (including the isolated case
$f^b=0$), the entropy identity reduces to

$$\nabla_aS^a= \frac{\zeta c\theta^2+2\eta c\,\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T} +\frac{\kappa}{cT^2}\Delta^{ab}(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)(\nabla_bT+Ta_b) +L\Delta^{ab}\nabla_a(\mu/T)\nabla_b(\mu/T)\ge0.$$

This sign condition alone implies neither finite propagation nor linear
stability, as the following two conditional model calculations show.

1. **Supported fixed-rest Fourier branch.** Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ have Minkowski
metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, choose $N=(1,0,0,0)$ as time
orientation, and write $x^0=ct$. On the positive-time field domain
$O=\{(x^0,\mathbf x):x^0>0,\ \mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3\}$ set
$u=(1,0,0,0)$. Set $V=\Pi=\pi=0$ and $\eta=\zeta=L=0$, and maintain the
fixed rest field with external support
$f^0=0$, $f^i=\partial_i p+c^{-1}\partial_tQ^i$, hence $u_bf^b=0$ even if
$f^i$ is nonzero. On a fixed-volume state slice
$v=v_0$, let $T=T_0+\vartheta$ and
$\epsilon=\epsilon_0+C\vartheta$, where $T_0,C>0$ are constant and the
temperature coordinate is valid on an interval $[T_0,T_0+\delta]$ contained in
the material-state domain for some $\delta>0$. With constant $\kappa>0$, set
$q=cQ=-\kappa\nabla\vartheta$. For any
$\vartheta_0\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfying
$0\le\vartheta_0\le\delta$ and $\vartheta_0\not\equiv0$, the heat solution
$\vartheta(\mathbf x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma(\mathbf x-\mathbf y,\kappa t/C)
\vartheta_0(\mathbf y)\,d\mathbf y$ for $t>0$ has initial boundary trace
$\vartheta_0$ locally uniformly as $t\downarrow0^+$ and is strictly positive
at every $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$ for every $t>0$. Hence no finite speed $v$ satisfies
$\operatorname{supp}\vartheta(\cdot,t)\subseteq
\operatorname{supp}\vartheta_0+\overline B_{vt}(0)$ for all $t>0$.

2. **Homogeneous Eckart linearization.** On the same Minkowski spacetime take
$f=0$ and a homogeneous rest state with $n_0,T_0>0$,
$h_0=\epsilon_0+p_0>0$, and $\kappa>0$. Set the density and temperature
perturbations to zero, $\delta n=\delta T=0$, take $V=0$, and impose no spatial
gradients. Let $\mathbf w:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^3$ be the first-order spatial
perturbation of $u$. The linearized first-order heat and momentum equations are
$Q^i=-(\kappa T_0/c^2)\dot w^i$ and
$h_0\dot{\mathbf w}+\dot{\mathbf Q}=0$. Hence for
$\lambda=h_0c^2/(\kappa T_0)>0$, every nonzero constant vector $\mathbf w_*$ gives
the growing linearized mode $\mathbf w(t)=\mathbf w_*e^{\lambda t}$.
This is a statement about the linearized equations, not a nonlinear solution
claim.

The results are conditional mathematical deductions from the displayed model
equations. They do not establish a constitutive law for nature, a nonlinear
existence theorem, or a general instability theorem.

items.title: An explicit null-dust tensor without a timelike Landau frame
items.statement:
Take $M=\mathbb R^4$ with Minkowski metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and choose the time orientation
$N=(1,0,0,0)$. By [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], a nonzero causal vector
$v$ is future-directed exactly when $g(v,N)<0$, which here is equivalent to
$v^0>0$. Let $\ell=(1,1,0,0)$, so $g(\ell,\ell)=0$ and
$g(\ell,N)=-1<0$; thus $\ell$ is future-directed null. Let $\rho>0$ and
define the symmetric tensor $T^{ab}=\rho\,\ell^a\ell^b$. A **Landau frame** for this
tensor means a future unit timelike vector $u$ for which the projected energy
flux $Q^a=-\Delta^a{}_cT^{cd}u_d$ vanishes. The current frame convention of
[[lem-tgr-fluid-frame-projection]] gives the unique stress decomposition; when
$Q=0$, contracting it with $u_b$ gives
$$T^a{}_bu^b=-\epsilon_u u^a,\qquad \epsilon_u=T^{ab}u_a u_b.$$
This explicit tensor has no Landau frame.

row.title: Complete symmetrized constant-coefficient evolution

items.title: Complete symmetrized constant-coefficient evolution
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$, and let $A_1,A_2,A_3,B,M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be constant matrices. Assume $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite, each $MA_j$ is symmetric, and $S:=(MB+B^{\mathsf T}M)/2$ is positive semidefinite. Consider

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_{x_j}U+BU=0.$$

Use [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]: for $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^3$, the scalar seminorm is $p_{\alpha\beta}(f):=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^3}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$, and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ consists of functions for which all these seminorms are finite. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ means maps $U=(U_1,\ldots,U_m)$ with real-valued components such that each component, viewed as complex-valued with zero imaginary part, belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$; its vector seminorms are $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}(U):=\max_{1\leq\ell\leq m}p_{\alpha\beta}(U_\ell)$. For $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ there is a unique global smooth solution, Schwartz in $x$ at each time and continuous in every $p_{\alpha\beta}^{(m)}$ on compact time intervals. With the negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, put $\widehat U(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}U(x)\,dx$ and define, for $s\ge0$,

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M}^2:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|\xi|^2)^s\widehat U(\xi)^*M\widehat U(\xi)\,d\xi.$$

For $t\ge0$, $\|U(t)\|_{H^s_M}\le\|U_0\|_{H^s_M}$ for every $s\ge0$; hence the solution depends continuously on the data in each such norm. The same conclusions hold for smooth periodic data on the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, $L>0$, with Fourier coefficients $\widehat U_k=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}U(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x/L}\,dx$ and

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k/L|^2)^s\widehat U_k^*M\widehat U_k.$$

For periodic data, $\|U(t)\|_\infty\le C_{s,L,M}\|U_0\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}$ for each integer $s>3/2$.

For a unit vector $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, write $A(\nu)=\sum_j\nu_jA_j$ and $\widetilde A(\nu)=M^{1/2}A(\nu)M^{-1/2}$. The finite speed

$$v_*:=\sup_{|\nu|=1}\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde A(\nu))\}$$

is finite. If $v_*>0$, $R>v_*t$, and $U_0$ vanishes on $B_R(x_0)$, then $U(t)$ vanishes on $B_{R-v_*t}(x_0)$ for $0\le t<R/v_*$. The same assertion holds on $\mathbb T_L^3$ using its geodesic distance. If $v_*=0$, every $A_j=0$ and the system is a pointwise linear ODE, so spatial support does not move. These are conclusions for the displayed linear systems; no variable-coefficient or nonlinear existence claim is included.

items.title: Perfect sound characteristic and actual stable causal linear branch
items.statement:
Fix $c>0$ and take $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future causal cone $\{V\in\mathbb R^4:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$. For $V=(V^0,\mathbf V)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $V^0>0$, define its coordinate velocity by $\mathbf v(V):=c\mathbf V/V^0$. Since $\eta(V,V)=(V^0)^2(|\mathbf v(V)|^2/c^2-1)$, membership in this cone is equivalent to $|\mathbf v(V)|\leq c$, with equality on its nonzero null boundary. The zero vector belongs to the cone but has no coordinate velocity under this definition. The constant rest observer is $\bar u=(1,0,0,0)$.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, let $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and fix $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv}>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$. A first variation is defined by a family of state maps $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda}):M\to X$ and fields $u_\lambda:M\to\mathbb R^4$, jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, with the displayed reference state and $\bar u$ as their constant $\lambda=0$ values and with $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$, $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, write $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$; put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and impose the adiabatic first-variation condition $\delta\sigma_p=0$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of the no-force balances $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$ and $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, with $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+p_\lambda\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$, and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear balances. Differentiating $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ gives $\delta u^0=0$.

The local Gibbs identity of [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] gives

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})}{n_0h_0},$$

and assume additionally $a_s\le1$. In the adopted units, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $r$ and $h_0$ have units Pa, and $w$ and $a_s$ are dimensionless. Since $x^0=ct$ and $\bar u=\partial_{x^0}$, the first variations of the no-force perfect-fluid projection equations of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] are

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0.$$

For initial data $U_0=(r_0,w_0)$ whose real components belong componentwise to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ as defined by [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or for smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, these equations have the unique global smooth solution supplied by [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]]. The positive quadratic energy density $\mathcal E=\tfrac12[(a_s/h_0)r^2+h_0|w|^2]$ has flux $c a_s r w$, and the solution is contractive in the corresponding weighted $L^2$ and Sobolev norms. Its characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$; for positive $a_s$, this propagation cone lies inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s\le1$. These are statements about this frozen linear system only; they do not assert a nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution theorem.

For the formal coefficient comparison in [A3], if the same linear equations are assigned $a_s>1$, their plane-wave speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}>c$. If they are assigned $a_s<0$, smooth periodic modes grow as $e^{c\sqrt{-a_s}|k|t}$ at arbitrarily large wave numbers. The case $a_s=0$ is degenerate: the displayed positive energy matrix is no longer positive definite, so the stability proof above does not apply.

items.title: Corrected bulk relaxation and exact extended entropy
items.statement:
Use the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian data, local state, and conventions of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]], with $n>0$, $T>0$, $c>0$, $x^0=ct$, and smooth future unit $u$. On the nonempty open spacetime domain $O$ of those suppliers, let $\zeta,\tau\in C^1(O;(0,\infty))$ be scalar coefficient fields, set $\beta:=\tau/\zeta\in C^1(O;(0,\infty))$, and let $\Pi:O\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. In the bulk-only branch take

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_au^a$, and $a^b_{\rm acc}=Du^b$. Adopt the corrected relaxation law

$$\beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right)$$

and the extended entropy current $S^a=[s-\beta\Pi^2/(2T)]u^a$. Then the stress and particle equations imply

$$D\epsilon+(h+\Pi)\theta=0,\qquad (h+\Pi)a^b_{\rm acc}+\Delta^{ba}\nabla_a(p+\Pi)=0,\qquad Dn+n\theta=0,$$

and every actual smooth solution of the stated corrected law satisfies

$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\ge0.$$

Here $\beta$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, $\Pi,\epsilon,p,h$ have units Pa, $D,\theta,a_{\rm acc}$ have inverse-length components, and the correction $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has the units of entropy density. The law is an explicit model assumption; dropping its derivative term does not yield the stated sign identity in general.

There is an exact homogeneous solution on the explicitly specified Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$; its Levi-Civita derivative is ordinary coordinate differentiation. Fix a state point $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplied local state domain with $v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and take the constant state map $(v,\sigma_p)(x)=(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, so $n_0=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ are constant. For constant positive coefficients $\zeta_0,\tau_0$, let $u=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, $T=T_0$, and define the smooth scalar field $\Pi(x)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0}$ on all of $M$, where $t=x^0/c$. The stress and particle balances and the corrected law hold, with strict entropy production wherever $\Pi(x)\ne0$. This mathematical witness is not a general nonlinear existence theorem or a claim of physical applicability in any separately selected near-equilibrium regime.

items.title: Bulk linear relaxation energy, stability and causal speed
items.statement:
Use $\mathcal M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, future direction $\partial_{x^0}$, and reference causal cone $\{V\in\mathbb R^4:V^0\geq0,\ \eta_{ab}V^aV^b\leq0\}$. For $V=(V^0,\mathbf V)$ with $V^0>0$, define $\mathbf v(V):=c\mathbf V/V^0$; then $\eta(V,V)=(V^0)^2(|\mathbf v(V)|^2/c^2-1)$, so cone membership is equivalent to $|\mathbf v(V)|\leq c$, with equality on its nonzero null boundary. The zero vector belongs to the cone but has no coordinate velocity under this definition. Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be open, $e\in C^2(X;\mathbb R)$, and $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})\in X$. Define $n_0:=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0:=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0:=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0:=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$. The background fields are this constant state, $u_0=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, and $\Pi_0=0$. Assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv},c>0$, with $e_{vv}$ evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$.

A first variation is defined by a family $(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda},u_\lambda,\Pi_\lambda)$ jointly smooth in dimensionless $\lambda$ near $0$ and in $x$, through the displayed background, with $u_\lambda$ future unit, meaning $\eta(u_\lambda,u_\lambda)=-1$ and $u_\lambda^0>0$. For any such field $f_\lambda$, set $\delta f:=\left.\partial_\lambda f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$. At each $\lambda$, set $n_\lambda=1/v_\lambda$, $\epsilon_\lambda=n_\lambda e(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $p_\lambda=-e_v(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $T_\lambda=e_{\sigma_p}(v_\lambda,\sigma_{p,\lambda})$, $\Delta_\lambda^{ab}=\eta^{ab}+u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b$, $D_\lambda=u_\lambda^a\partial_a$, and $\theta_\lambda=\partial_a u_\lambda^a$. The bulk stress and current are $T_\lambda^{ab}=\epsilon_\lambda u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b+(p_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda)\Delta_\lambda^{ab}$ and $J_\lambda^a=n_\lambda u_\lambda^a$, and the corrected law of [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] is $\beta D_\lambda\Pi_\lambda+\Pi_\lambda/(\zeta c)=-\theta_\lambda-(T_\lambda\Pi_\lambda/2)\partial_a(\beta u_\lambda^a/T_\lambda)$, where $\beta=\tau/\zeta$. The linearized equations mean the first variations at $\lambda=0$ of $\partial_aT_\lambda^{ab}=0$, $\partial_aJ_\lambda^a=0$, and this corrected law, set equal to zero; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve the nonlinear system. Impose $\delta\sigma_p=0$, put $r:=\delta\epsilon$, $w:=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and denote $\delta\Pi$ by $\Pi$ in the linearized system below. Take constant coefficients $\zeta,\tau>0$.

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n_0h_0}>0$$

as supplied by [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. The resulting linearized system is

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau\Pi_t+\Pi=-\zeta c\operatorname{div}w.$$

Its positive quadratic energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2+\frac{\tau}{\zeta}\Pi^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\Pi)w]=-\Pi^2/\zeta$. The normal characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm v_{\rm bulk}$, where

$$v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{a_s+\frac{\zeta}{\tau h_0}}.$$

By [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]], initial data $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^5)$ with the componentwise real convention of [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], or smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, have unique global smooth solutions, contractive in the corresponding energy and Sobolev norms, with finite propagation at $v_{\rm bulk}$. The branch is inside the Minkowski reference cone exactly when $a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0)\le1$. Constant density and transverse velocity modes can persist, so contraction does not mean every mode decays. No nonlinear or variable-coefficient existence theorem is claimed.

items.title: Positive relaxation parameters can give superluminal characteristic speed
items.statement:
Choose $n_0,T_0,h_0,\tau,c>0$ and $\sigma_{p0}\in\mathbb R$, put $v_0=1/n_0$, and on an open neighborhood $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ of $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ define the $C^2$ local energy per marker

$$e(v,\sigma_p)=\frac{h_0}{n_0}+T_0(\sigma_p-\sigma_{p0})+\frac{n_0h_0}{6}(v-v_0)^2.$$

Choose $X$ small enough that $v>0$ and the local enthalpy density $h:=\epsilon+p$, with $n=1/v$, $\epsilon=ne$, and $p=-e_v$, remains positive. At the reference state, $T=e_{\sigma_p}=T_0>0$, $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=h_0$, and $e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})=n_0h_0/3$. The local Gibbs response in [[lem-tgr-bulk-linear-causality]] therefore realizes $a_s=e_{vv}/(n_0h_0)=1/3$. Now set $\zeta=\tau h_0$. All positivity hypotheses of that bulk linear branch hold, but its exact normal characteristic speed is $v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{1/3+1}=2c/\sqrt3>c$. With SI units, $h_0$ is in Pa and $\tau$ in s, so $\zeta$ is in Pa s. This is a parameterized mathematical model example, not a measurement or an estimate for a material.

items.title: Separate entropy-only radiation state maps
items.statement:
Fix a real parameter $a_R>0$ and let the temperature coordinate range over the open interval $T\in(0,\infty)$. Define the entropy-only radiation state maps

$$\varepsilon_T(T):=a_RT^4,\qquad p_T(T):=\frac13a_RT^4,\qquad s_T(T):=\frac43a_RT^3.$$

Here $\varepsilon_T$ and $p_T$ are scalar-valued maps on $(0,\infty)$, and $s_T$ is the entropy coordinate as a scalar-valued map on the same interval. Put $h_T(T):=\varepsilon_T(T)+p_T(T)$. No particle-number coordinate, particle-number current, or chemical-potential coordinate is part of this state space.

Also define maps on the positive entropy-coordinate interval by

$$\tau(s):=\left(\frac{3s}{4a_R}\right)^{1/3},\qquad \varepsilon_s(s):=a_R\tau(s)^4,\qquad p_s(s):=\frac13\varepsilon_s(s),\qquad s\in(0,\infty).$$

The displayed formulas define functions on the stated domains. In the conventional SI physical reading, $T$ is measured in K, $a_R$ in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-4}$, $\varepsilon_T,p_T$ in J m$^{-3}$, and $s_T$ in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$. These units do not assign an empirical value to $a_R$. In particular, this definition does not derive a quantum blackbody coefficient or assert that any physical system realizes these maps.
