items.title: Radiation Gibbs and perfect linear sound deduction
items.statement:
Fix $a_R>0$ and the maps of [[def-tgr-entropy-only-radiation-state]]. First, their temperature and entropy coordinates are inverse, $d\varepsilon_T=T\,ds_T$, $h_T=T s_T$, and $dp_T/d\varepsilon_T=1/3$ on $T>0$.

Next, assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth symmetric nondegenerate covariant $2$-tensor field of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Write $g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components and $u_b:=g_{bc}u^c$. Use the Levi-Civita connection supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $c>0$, let $u$ be a smooth vector field with $g_{ab}u^au^b=-c^2$, and let $T:M\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth. Put $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_T(T)$, $p=p_T(T)$, $s=s_T(T)$, and $h=\varepsilon+p$. Define the symmetric tensor field

$$\mathsf T^{ab}:=\frac{h}{c^2}u^au^b+p g^{ab}.$$

If $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$, then $\nabla_a(su^a)=0$. This is a conditional mathematical identity for the specified tensor and state maps; it assumes no particle-number current.

Finally, on $\mathbb R^4$ with Minkowski coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x)$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, specify the linearization as follows. For some $\epsilon>0$, let $\lambda\mapsto(T_\lambda,u_\lambda)$ be jointly smooth on $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times\mathbb R^4$, with $T_\lambda(x)>0$, $T_{0}(x)=T_*$, $u_{0}=(c,0,0,0)$, and $\eta_{ab}u_\lambda^au_\lambda^b=-c^2$. Form $\mathsf T_\lambda^{ab}$ by the same stress formula above with $(T,u,g)$ replaced by $(T_\lambda,u_\lambda,\eta)$, using $\varepsilon_\lambda:=\varepsilon_T(T_\lambda)$ and $p_\lambda:=p_T(T_\lambda)$. Write $\delta f:=\left.\frac{d}{d\lambda}f_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}$; the linearized equation means $\delta(\partial_a\mathsf T_\lambda^{ab})=0$. Put $h_*:=\varepsilon_T(T_*)+p_T(T_*)$, $r:=\delta\varepsilon$, and $w^i:=\delta u^i/c$. Its resulting constant-coefficient linear system is

$$r_t+c h_*\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{3h_*}\nabla r=0,$$

where $\nabla$ and $\operatorname{div}$ are the Euclidean spatial gradient and divergence. With $U=(r,w)$, write this system as $U_t+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_jU=0$, where

$$A_j:=c\begin{pmatrix}0&h_*e_j^{\mathsf T}\\(1/(3h_*))e_j&0_{3\times3}\end{pmatrix},\qquad e_j\text{ is the }j\text{th standard basis vector of }\mathbb R^3.$$

The matrix $M_*:=\operatorname{diag}(1/(3h_*),h_* I_3)$ is a positive symmetrizer in the explicit sense that it is symmetric positive definite and $M_*A_j$ is symmetric for each $j$. For each unit spatial vector $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, define the directional coefficient matrix $A(\nu):=\sum_{j=1}^3\nu_jA_j$; its eigenvalues are $0$ (multiplicity two) and $\pm c/\sqrt3$. For Schwartz initial perturbations on $\mathbb R^3$ or smooth periodic initial perturbations on $\mathbb T_L^3$ with $L>0$, where Schwartz means each component belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$ as defined in [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], the global smooth evolution, weighted Sobolev contraction, and finite-propagation conclusions are conditional on the exact symmetrized-system interface of [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]] stated in [A1]. That current carrier is draft, so this item does not record those conclusions as independently accepted.

items.title: Fixed-coefficient Cattaneo entropy and propagation
items.statement:
Let $C,\kappa,\tau,T_0,L>0$. Let $\Omega$ be either $\mathbb R^3$ or the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$. Consider real smooth fields $\theta:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $q:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying

$$C\theta_t+\operatorname{div}q=0,\qquad \tau q_t+q=-\kappa\nabla\theta.$$

The derivatives are ordinary derivatives of the Euclidean spatial coordinates; on the torus they are defined using periodic lifts. Write $U=(\theta,q)$ and let $e_j$ be the $j$th standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^3$. Define

$$A_j:=\begin{pmatrix}0&e_j^{\mathsf T}/C\\(\kappa/\tau)e_j&0_{3\times3}\end{pmatrix},\qquad B:=\operatorname{diag}(0,(1/\tau)I_3),\qquad M:=\operatorname{diag}(C,(\tau/\kappa)I_3).$$

Then the displayed system is $U_t+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_jU+BU=0$. The matrix $M$ is a positive symmetrizer, meaning $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite and $MA_j$ is symmetric for each $j$. For a unit direction $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, define the principal matrix $A(\nu):=\sum_{j=1}^3\nu_jA_j$; its eigenvalues are $0$ (multiplicity two) and $\pm v_h$, where $v_h:=\sqrt{\kappa/(C\tau)}>0$. For a fixed comparison speed $c_*>0$, $v_h\le c_*$ if and only if $\kappa\le C\tau c_*^2$.

For every such solution and every $s_0\in\mathbb R$, define the specified quadratic effective entropy density and flux by

$$s_{\rm eff}:=s_0+\frac{C\theta}{T_0}-\frac{C\theta^2}{2T_0^2}-\frac{\tau|q|^2}{2\kappa T_0^2},\qquad j_s:=\frac{q}{T_0}-\frac{\theta q}{T_0^2}.$$

Every smooth solution satisfies the exact identities

$$\partial_t s_{\rm eff}+\operatorname{div}j_s=\frac{|q|^2}{\kappa T_0^2}\ge0,\qquad \partial_t e_L+\operatorname{div}(\theta q)=-\frac{|q|^2}{\kappa},\qquad e_L:=\frac12\left(C\theta^2+\frac{\tau}{\kappa}|q|^2\right).$$

For every unit direction $\nu$, its quadratic flux satisfies $|\theta q\cdot\nu|\le v_h e_L$. The density $e_L$ is a positive quadratic Lyapunov density, not a physical energy density. The entropy identity asserts nonnegative production for this specified quadratic effective current; it does not assert positivity of $s_{\rm eff}$ for arbitrary data or a nonlinear material entropy law. These equations define the mathematical subsystem considered here; the sources give model context and do not establish a material-specific realization.

Use the exact global-solution, Fourier-coefficient, and weighted-norm conventions in [F1]. For initial data $U_0=(\theta_0,q_0)\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^4)$ or $C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^4)$, the unique global smooth evolution, its weighted Sobolev contraction, and finite propagation at speed $v_h$ follow conditionally from [F1] after checking the matrices below. On $\mathbb T_L^3$, for every integer $r>3/2$, set

$$K_{r,L,C}:=C^{-1/2}\left(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k/L|^2)^{-r}\right)^{1/2}<\infty,$$

where $C>0$ is the heat-capacity coefficient and $\|\cdot\|_{H^r_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}$ is the norm in [F1]. The periodic global solution supplied conditionally by [F1] obeys $T_0+\theta(t,x)>0$ for all $t\ge0$ whenever $K_{r,L,C}\|U_0\|_{H^r_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}<T_0$. The constant uses only the temperature component $C|\widehat\theta_k|^2$ of the supplied quadratic norm, so it does not compare heat-flux and temperature coordinates by a least eigenvalue. Although [F1] states a generic periodic supremum bound with unspecified constant $C_{s,L,M}$, the explicit $K_{r,L,C}$ bound here is derived directly from Fourier reconstruction and the stated norm contraction.

If the symbols receive their conventional SI thermal interpretation, take $\theta,T_0$ in K, $C$ in J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$, $\kappa$ in W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, $\tau$ in s, $L$ in m, $q$ in W m$^{-2}$, and the comparison speed $c_*$ in m s$^{-1}$. Use the spatial coordinates in the inherited Fourier norms as their numerical values in metres, so the unit-frequency term in $1+|k/L|^2$ uses the reference length $1$ m. Then $s_0$ and $s_{\rm eff}$ have entropy-density units J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$, $j_s$ has entropy-flux units J m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, and $e_L$ has units J K m$^{-3}$ rather than energy-density units. The norm $\|U\|_{H^r_M}$ has units $\sqrt{\mathrm{J\,K\,m^{-3}}}$ and $K_{r,L,C}$ has units $\sqrt{\mathrm{m^3\,K/J}}$, so their product has temperature units. These unit labels do not assert a physical realization of the linear subsystem.

items.title: Damped Cattaneo Fourier mode
items.statement:
Choose $C,\kappa,\tau,T_0,L>0$ and an integer $n\ge1$. Set $k:=2\pi n/L$ and assume $k^2>C/(4\tau\kappa)$. Let $\Theta\in\mathbb R$ with $0<|\Theta|<T_0$ and

$$\omega:=\sqrt{\frac{\kappa k^2}{C\tau}-\frac{1}{4\tau^2}},\qquad \phi(t):=\Theta e^{-t/(2\tau)}\cos(\omega t).$$

On $\mathbb T_L^3$, let $e_1=(1,0,0)$ be the first standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^3$ and define

$$\theta(t,x):=\phi(t)\cos(kx_1),\qquad q(t,x):=-\frac{C}{k}\phi'(t)\sin(kx_1)e_1.$$

This is a nonzero, smooth, spatially periodic solution for every $t\in\mathbb R$ of the linear Cattaneo subsystem

$$C\theta_t+\operatorname{div}q=0,\qquad \tau q_t+q=-\kappa\nabla\theta.$$

Under the conventional SI interpretation of [F1], $L$ is measured in m, $k$ in m$^{-1}$, $\omega$ in s$^{-1}$, and $\Theta,\phi,\theta,T_0$ in K; the units of $C,\kappa,\tau,q$ are those stated in [F1]. These unit labels do not assert a material realization.

For $t\ge0$, the proxy field $T_0+\theta$ remains positive, and its oscillation envelope decays as $e^{-t/(2\tau)}$. The physical-temperature interpretation is limited to the interval where $T_0+\theta>0$.

items.title: Smooth perfect local material balance model
items.statement:
Let $O$ be an open region of a smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with its metric-compatible torsion-free connection $\nabla$. Use the local material-state and unit conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]]: a smooth future-directed unit timelike observer-congruence field $u$ has $g(u,u)=-1$; a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$ takes values in a nonempty open $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$; and a supplied $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$ defines $n=1/v>0$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\varepsilon=ne$, $T=\partial_{\sigma_p}e$, and $p=-\partial_v e$. Adopt the selected fixed-composition material branch of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]], including its stipulated local-equilibrium regime and $T>0$.

For this branch, adopt the perfect-fluid matter model
$$J^a:=n u^a,\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}:=\varepsilon u^a u^b+p\Delta^{ab},\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ab}+u^a u^b,$$
with local balances $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$ on $O$. Here $J^a$ is the selected material-marker current and $\mathsf T^{ab}$ is the symmetric stress-energy tensor; the perfect branch adopts zero spatial marker diffusion and isotropic rest-space stress. The balances are physical model assumptions in the stated smooth regime, not conclusions from the state function or from geometry. They may be used on a prescribed background or together with an explicitly specified coupled Einstein model; this postulate does not assert a solution exists for arbitrary initial data or an arbitrary equation of state.

The marker receives its material-particle interpretation from the fixed-composition premise. No microscopic equation of state, universal material applicability, nonzero external force, dissipative flux, global self-gravitating energy additivity, or empirical observation is asserted.

items.title: Local Gibbs and parcel first law in the adopted material
items.statement:
In the adopted fixed-composition local-equilibrium material model of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]], let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be its open state domain, let $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$ include the rest-energy contribution, and set $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, $\varepsilon=ne$, and $\mu=e+pv-T\sigma_p$, with $n=1/v$ and $s=n\sigma_p$ as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. The model's local state identities are
$$d\varepsilon=T\,ds+\mu\,dn,\qquad \varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n,\qquad dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu.$$
For a local continuum parcel with real extensive marker variable $\mathsf N>0$, proper volume $\mathsf V>0$, entropy $\mathsf S\in\mathbb R$, and $(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X$, its adopted energy is $E=\mathsf N e(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)$. On this open parcel domain it obeys
$$dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N,\qquad E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N.$$
The count variable is treated continuously as part of the local-equilibrium continuum model; these differentials are not claims about discrete microscopic transitions. The result is conditional model calculus and does not establish that a chosen state function describes a particular material.

items.title: Perfect entropy advection and restricted circulation
items.statement:
Assume the smooth isolated perfect material model of [[post-tgr-perfect-fluid-model]] on an open region $O$ of a time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Thus $u$ is a smooth future-directed unit timelike observer-congruence field, $g(u,u)=-1$, the local state is the $C^2$ state of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] with $n>0$ and $T>0$, $J^a=nu^a$, $\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+p(g^{ab}+u^a u^b)$, and $
abla_aJ^a=0$, $
abla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$. Write $D=u^a
abla_a$ and $u^ lat=g(u,\cdot)$. For every smooth closed curve $\gamma_0:[0,1]	o O$ whose image is compact and for which a local flow $\Phi_\lambda$ of $u$ is defined on a neighborhood of that image for $\lambda$ in an interval about $0$, set $\gamma_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda\circ\gamma_0$, $H=(\varepsilon+p)/n$, $P=(H/c)u^ lat$, and $\mathcal C(\lambda)=\int_{\gamma_\lambda}P$, with $c$ and the length-coordinate convention of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Conditional on the exact current mathematical supplier interfaces, the entropy identities and loop law are
$$
abla_a(su^a)=0,\qquad D\sigma_p=0,\qquad  rac{d\mathcal C}{d\lambda}= rac1c\int_{\gamma_\lambda}T\,d\sigma_p.$$
In particular, $\mathcal C$ is locally constant if $\sigma_p$ is constant on the whole region swept out by the loop. Material advection alone, $D\sigma_p=0$, does not imply $d\sigma_p=0$ or circulation conservation. These are conditional model deductions, not an existence theorem or empirical claim.

items.title: Uniform prescribed-background perfect material
items.statement:
Choose Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb R^4$ with length coordinates $x^0=ct$, metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and its standard future cone. On a material state domain $X$, fix $(v_0,\sigma_0)\in X$ with the adopted state function $e$ and its derived constants $n_0=1/v_0$, $\varepsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_0)$, $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_0)$, and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_0)>0$. Let $u=(1,0,0,0)$ be the constant future unit observer field and adopt the perfect model of [[post-tgr-perfect-fluid-model]] on this prescribed background. Then the resulting homogeneous material is an exact solution of the local particle and stress balances.

For the constant future unit observer field $w=\gamma(1,\boldsymbol\beta)$, parameterize its boost relative to $u$ in this global Cartesian chart by the dimensionless vector $\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$, and put $\gamma=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$. The observer-projected energy density is
$$\varepsilon_{(w)}:=\mathsf T^{ab}w_aw_b=(\varepsilon_0+p_0)\gamma^2-p_0.$$
At zero boost this equals $\varepsilon_0$. The nonzero-boost value is a frame-dependent stress-energy prediction within the model, not an observation. Prescribing Minkowski geometry here does not make this nonzero-stress configuration a solution of the coupled Einstein equations.

row.title: Restricted gradient constitutive dissipative model

items.title: Restricted gradient constitutive dissipative model
items.statement:
Use the time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, Levi-Civita connection, smooth future unit observer congruence, and length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Here a **frame** means this smooth observer field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$ and its pointwise rest spaces; it does not mean a coordinate chart or a tetrad. On a nonempty open region $O$, take a $C^2$ fixed-composition state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$ with $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, state function $e\in C^2(X)$, and $T=\partial_{\sigma_p}e>0$ as adopted by [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]]. The mathematical state maps are $n=v^{-1}$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\varepsilon=ne$, and $p=-\partial_v e$; their meanings and units are those in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]].

Write $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the rest-space projector, derivative along the observer congruence, expansion, acceleration, and spatial symmetric trace-free shear by
$$\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^a u^b,\qquad D=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad \theta=\nabla_a u^a,\qquad a_b=u^c\nabla_c u_b,$$
$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$
where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Put $Y_b=\nabla_bT+Ta_b$ and $Z_b=\nabla_b(\mu/T)$, using the chemical potential $\mu$ from [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. The number current, stress tensor and entropy current in the selected branch are
$$J^a=nu^a+V^a,\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab}+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T},$$
with $u_aV^a=u_aQ^a=u_a\pi^{ab}=0$ and $\pi^{ab}$ symmetric and trace-free. Adopt the source-free balances $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$ together with the first-order gradient closures
$$\Pi=-\zeta c\theta,\qquad \pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab},\qquad Q^a=-\frac{\kappa}{c}\Delta^{ab}Y_b,\qquad V^a=-L\Delta^{ab}Z_b.$$

Here $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; $\theta$, $a_b$ and $\sigma_{ab}$ have inverse-length components; $\Pi$, $\pi^{ab}$ and $Q^a$ have units Pa; $\zeta,\eta\in C^1(O)$ have units Pa s; $\kappa\in C^1(O)$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$; and $L\in C^1(O)$ has formal units $\mathrm{marker^2\,K\,J^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. The temperature and chemical-potential gradients have units K m$^{-1}$ and J marker$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ m$^{-1}$, respectively. The coefficient fields satisfy $\zeta,\eta,\kappa,L\geq0$. All displayed constitutive fields, currents and stress data are required to have enough regularity that the balances and entropy-current divergence hold classically.

Each application declares a nonempty open regime of the pointwise state values and first covariant derivatives of $u,T,\mu/T$ (with the listed algebraic constraints) on which the constitutive model is used. The regime separately requires $J$ to be future timelike. Since $u_aV^a=0$, this condition is $n>0$ and $g_{ab}V^aV^b<n^2$, as follows from $g(J,J)=-n^2+g(V,V)$ and $-u_aJ^a=n$. It is an additional applicability restriction, not a consequence of the gradient closures.

This is an adopted constitutive model for one declared material regime. The closures are not derived from geometry, measurements, or the second law; they do not assert that a solution exists, that the model applies to every material, or that the branch is causal, stable, or globally entropy-increasing. No empirical observation is supplied.

items.title: Specified bulk extended entropy and relaxation law
items.statement:
Use the fixed-composition local-equilibrium state, smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, smooth future unit observer congruence $u$, and length coordinates $x^0=ct$ from [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] and [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. In particular, $n>0$, $T>0$, $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, and $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$ have those suppliers' meanings. In a selected bulk-only branch, adopt the stress, number current, and source-free balances
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$
where $\Pi$ is a smooth scalar bulk pressure. Let $\zeta,\tau\in C^1(O)$ be positive coefficient fields with SI units Pa s and s, respectively, and define $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, with units Pa$^{-1}$. Adopt the extended entropy current and derivative-corrected relaxation law
$$S^a=\left(s-\frac{\beta\Pi^2}{2T}\right)u^a,\qquad \beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right).$$
Here $\Pi$ has units Pa, $D$ and $\theta$ have inverse-length units, and each side of the relaxation law has units m$^{-1}$; $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has entropy-density units J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$.

For each application, specify a nonempty open near-equilibrium regime in the pointwise state and first-derivative data around $\Pi=0$, based at constant zero-gradient reference data, and use the current and law only while the fields remain in that declared regime. Require enough field regularity for the balances and entropy divergence to hold classically. The mathematical result [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] supplies the exact matching conditional entropy identity and one homogeneous witness; its actual statement and proof are conditional on the listed mathematical inputs and assume exactly countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). It motivates this selection and is used by the downstream deductions, but it does not derive the adopted physical postulate.

This is a restricted constitutive assumption for the selected material. It does not derive the equation of state, assert universal validity, or adopt existence of a general nonlinear solution. It makes no causal or stability claim; positive relaxation time alone supplies neither. No empirical observation is supplied.

items.title: Exact entropy identity in the selected bulk branch
items.statement:
On a nonempty open region of the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian model of [[post-tgr-bulk-relaxation-model]], assume an actual solution of its source-free stress and particle balances and corrected relaxation law. Use the state maps and units of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]], with smooth future unit observer congruence $u$ (the frame, not a chart or tetrad), $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $n,T,c>0$, positive $C^1$ coefficient fields $\zeta,\tau$, and $\beta=\tau/\zeta$. Require enough regularity that all displayed balances and the entropy-current divergence are classical. The solution remains in the application's declared open near-equilibrium regime. With
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad S^a=\left(s-\frac{\beta\Pi^2}{2T}\right)u^a,$$
the exact pointwise identity is
$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\geq0.$$
This is conditional on an actual solution and does not assert general solution existence.

There is also an explicit homogeneous solution under the additional application condition that the declared open regime contains constant zero-gradient reference data with $\Pi=0$. Let the selected material's state domain contain $(v_0,\sigma_0)$ with $n_0=1/v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_0)>0$, and let the regime contain those constant state data. On $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, Minkowski metric $g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$, choose constant positive $\zeta_0,\tau_0$ and set $u=\partial_{x^0}$. For some $\delta>0$ seconds take the open region $O=(-c\delta,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3$, put $t=x^0/c$, and define
$$\Pi(t)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0},\qquad t> -\delta.$$
Choose $\Pi_0$ sufficiently small that the full field and first-derivative data stay in the declared regime throughout $O$. Then the source-free balances and corrected law hold, and the entropy production is strictly positive at every finite $t\geq0$ when $\Pi_0\ne0$, and zero when $\Pi_0=0$.

The argument is a conditional model deduction, not an observation or a general nonlinear existence, causality, or stability theorem. No empirical premise is used.

items.title: Actual homogeneous bulk relaxation entropy production
items.statement:
Take a state point $(v_0,\sigma_0)$ of the selected model's supplied material domain with $v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_0)>0$. Its state map is constant, with $n_0=1/v_0$, $s_0=n_0\sigma_0$, $\varepsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_0)$, and $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_0)$ as in the state conventions of [[pthm-tgr-bulk-extended-entropy]]. Let $\zeta_0,\tau_0>0$ be constant coefficients with units Pa s and s, and take $\Pi_0$ in Pa. On $M=\mathbb R^4$ use global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, Minkowski metric $g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$. The frame is the observer congruence $u=\partial_{x^0}$ in that chart. For some $\delta>0$ seconds, take the open region $O=(-c\delta,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3$, put $t=x^0/c$, and define
$$\Pi(t)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0},\qquad t> -\delta.$$
Assume the application's open near-equilibrium regime contains these constant zero-gradient reference data at $\Pi=0$; choose $\Pi_0$ small enough that the field and first-derivative data remain in that regime throughout $O$. Then the source-free bulk balances and the corrected relaxation law hold. For every finite $t\geq0$ the entropy production is
$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi_0^2e^{-2t/\tau_0}}{\zeta_0cT_0}.$$
It vanishes when $\Pi_0=0$ and is strictly positive when $\Pi_0\ne0$. This is a constructed model solution, not a reported experiment.

items.title: Specified small-perturbation material dynamics
items.statement:
Use the selected local material state, perfect stress branch, bulk-only relaxation branch, and unit conventions of [[post-tgr-perfect-fluid-model]], [[post-tgr-bulk-relaxation-model]], and [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. For this effective model take prescribed Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb R^4$ with coordinates $(x^0,\mathbf x)=(ct,\mathbf x)$, $t\in\mathbb R$, $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$ measured in metres, and metric $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. The reference material is a constant state $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplier's open state domain, with supplied $e\in C^2$, $u_0=(1,0,0,0)$, $\Pi_0=0$, $n_0=1/v_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and enthalpy density $h_0=\varepsilon_0+p_0>0$. The local Gibbs supplier [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] gives the dimensionless adiabatic response

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\varepsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})}{n_0h_0};$$

restrict this pair of effective branches to $a_s>0$. Here $e_{vv}$ is the second derivative of the supplied $C^2$ state function with respect to $v$ at fixed $\sigma_p$. The equality between the derivative and the state-function ratio is the exact interface stated by [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]] under the reference-state hypotheses above. The derivative is the local fixed-composition response at the reference state; the equation does not assign a universal value to $a_s$.

For this postulate, a first variation means the derivative at $\lambda=0$ of a smooth one-parameter family of field configurations through the reference state, with dimensionless $\lambda$; no member with $\lambda\ne0$ is required to solve a nonlinear equation. The fields $r,\widehat\Pi:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ and $w:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ are smooth. Write $r=\delta\varepsilon$, $w=(\delta u^1,\delta u^2,\delta u^3)$, and, in the bulk branch, $\widehat\Pi=\delta\Pi$. The adiabatic sector means $\delta\sigma_p=0$. These first variations have $r$ and $\widehat\Pi$ in Pa and $w$ and $a_s$ dimensionless. Let $\zeta_0>0$ and $\tau_0>0$ be the bulk viscosity and relaxation time evaluated at the reference state, with units Pa s and s. Spatial derivatives have units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Adopt the following two constant-coefficient effective systems on the stated background:

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0$$

for the perfect branch, and

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\widehat\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau_0\widehat\Pi_t+\widehat\Pi=-\zeta_0c\operatorname{div}w$$

for the bulk-only branch. Derivatives $\nabla$ and $\operatorname{div}$ act on $\mathbf x$; $t$ is physical time and $c$ is the speed parameter in [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. The equations define the effective linear models. No uniform nonlinear error estimate, nonlinear solution lifespan, curved-spacetime evolution result, or existence claim for the nonlinear constitutive equations is postulated. The parameters and systems are adopted model inputs; they are not measurements or claims of universal material behavior.

For later solution claims, $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ is the flat three-torus for $L>0$, and smooth periodic data mean $C^\infty$ maps on that quotient. A multi-index is a triple in $\mathbb N^3$. A Schwartz map $U_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$ means a $C^\infty$ map such that $x^\alpha\partial^\beta U_0(x)$ is bounded for every pair of multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$. The systems have $m=4$ and $m=5$ components, respectively.

items.title: Causal stable perfect-material linear response
items.statement:
Assume the adiabatic perfect-material linear branch of [[post-tgr-linearized-material-model]] on its prescribed Minkowski background, with $c>0$, $h_0>0$, and $0<a_s\le1$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every initial datum $U_0=(r_0,w_0)\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^4)$ or $U_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^4)$ with $L>0$, the Cauchy problem $U(0,\cdot)=U_0$ for the system

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0$$

has a unique global smooth solution on the corresponding space-time domain, contractive in the positive quadratic energy and its weighted Sobolev norms. Its energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm pf}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm pf}+\operatorname{div}(c a_s r w)=0$. For each Sobolev exponent $q\ge0$, its weighted Sobolev norm is nonincreasing for $t\ge0$. The characteristic speeds, meaning eigenvalues of the principal matrix in a unit spatial direction, are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$. Finite propagation means that if initial data vanish on a ball of radius $R$, then at time $t$ they vanish on the concentric ball of radius $R-c\sqrt{a_s}\,t$ whenever $0\le t<R/(c\sqrt{a_s})$; on $\mathbb T_L^3$ use geodesic balls. Thus the exact linear propagation speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}\le c$. Equality is permitted at $a_s=1$. This is a conditional model deduction and makes no claim about nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution, or about nature beyond the adopted model.
items.physical_scope: Adiabatic perfect-material first variations about the specified uniform Minkowski rest state with h0>0 and 0<a_s<=1; linear global evolution only, not nonlinear or curved-spacetime fluid existence or empirical applicability.

items.title: Causal stable bulk-relaxation linear response
items.statement:
Assume the adiabatic bulk-only linear branch of [[post-tgr-linearized-material-model]] on its prescribed Minkowski background, with $h_0,T_0,c,a_s,\zeta_0,\tau_0>0$, the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and

$$a_s+\frac{\zeta_0}{\tau_0h_0}\le1.$$

For every initial datum $U_0=(r_0,w_0,\widehat\Pi_0)\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^5)$ or $U_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^5)$ with $L>0$, the Cauchy problem $U(0,\cdot)=U_0$ for the system

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\widehat\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau_0\widehat\Pi_t+\widehat\Pi=-\zeta_0c\operatorname{div}w$$

has a unique global smooth solution on the corresponding space-time domain and is contractive in its positive quadratic energy and weighted Sobolev norms. Its energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2+\frac{\tau_0}{\zeta_0}\widehat\Pi^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\widehat\Pi)w]=-\widehat\Pi^2/\zeta_0$. For each Sobolev exponent $q\ge0$, its weighted Sobolev norm is nonincreasing for $t\ge0$. The characteristic speeds, meaning eigenvalues of the principal matrix in a unit spatial direction, are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s+\zeta_0/(\tau_0h_0)}$. Finite propagation means that if initial data vanish on a ball of radius $R$, then at time $t$ they vanish on the concentric ball of radius $R-v_{\rm bulk}t$ whenever $0\le t<R/v_{\rm bulk}$, where $v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{a_s+\zeta_0/(\tau_0h_0)}$; on $\mathbb T_L^3$ use geodesic balls. Hence propagation is bounded by $c$ under the stated inequality. Equality at the causal threshold is allowed. Energy contraction does not assert decay of every mode. The result is conditional on the adopted linear model; it is not a nonlinear or curved-spacetime existence claim or an empirical conclusion.

items.title: Perfect sound and neutral perturbation modes
items.statement:
Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, use the perfect linear branch of [[pthm-tgr-perfect-causal-linear-response]] with $h_0>0$, $0<a_s\le1$, and reference speed $c>0$. For any nonzero wave vector $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ and real amplitude $A$ in Pa, define the dimensionless phase $\phi(t,\mathbf x)=\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t$, where $\omega=c\sqrt{a_s}\,|\mathbf k|$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and set

$$r(t,\mathbf x)=A\cos\phi(t,\mathbf x),\qquad w(t,\mathbf x)=\frac{A\omega}{c h_0|\mathbf k|^2}\,\mathbf k\cos\phi(t,\mathbf x).$$

This is an exact sound mode of the adopted linear system. At zero wave vector, the separate constant fields $r=r_0$ and $w=w_0$ are also exact solutions for arbitrary constants $r_0\in\mathbb R$ in Pa and $w_0\in\mathbb R^3$ dimensionless. Every nonzero such choice is a neutral mode, so linear energy contraction does not mean that every perturbation decays. These are calculated model solutions, not observations.
items.physical_scope: Explicit plane-wave and spatially constant solutions of the specified adiabatic perfect-material linear system; no claim that every mode decays, no nonlinear solution, and no empirical data.

row.title: Supported-rest effective Cattaneo thermal model

items.title: Supported-rest effective Cattaneo thermal model
items.statement:
Use the length-coordinate and unit-observer conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Fix Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^4$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x)$, where $t$ is physical time in seconds, $x^i$ are in metres, and $c>0$ is in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The supported rest observer congruence is the smooth future unit vector field $u=\partial_{x^0}$, so $\eta(u,u)=-1$. An external support maintains the modeled material at rest in this congruence; the support is not a dynamical variable, and this subsystem does not claim to include the momentum equations of a full fluid.

Fix constants $T_0>0$ in K, volumetric heat capacity $C>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$, thermal conductivity $\kappa>0$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, and relaxation time $\tau>0$ in seconds. Select an open state neighborhood $D$ of $(0,0)$ in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ contained in $\{(\vartheta,q):T_0+\vartheta>0\}$. The neighborhood is part of the application regime; no universal numerical size is asserted. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval of physical time, and define $\iota_I:I\times\mathbb R^3\to M$ by $\iota_I(t,\mathbf x)=(ct,\mathbf x)$; it identifies these coordinates with an open region of Minkowski spacetime. Choose either $\Sigma=\mathbb R^3$ or, for a fixed $L>0$, $\Sigma=\mathbb T_L^3:=\mathbb R^3/(L\mathbb Z^3)$ with its flat quotient metric; when $\Sigma=\mathbb T_L^3$, let $\pi_L:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T_L^3$ be the quotient map. The spacetime remains $M=\mathbb R^4$: the torus is only an analytic representation of spatially $L$-periodic fields on its Minkowski rest slices, not a quotient of spacetime. Take smooth fields $\vartheta:I\times\Sigma\to\mathbb R$ and $q:I\times\Sigma\to\mathbb R^3$ with $(\vartheta(t,x),q(t,x))\in D$. If $\Sigma=\mathbb T_L^3$, their physical fields on the rest slices are the smooth periodic lifts $\widetilde\vartheta(t,\mathbf x):=\vartheta(t,\pi_L(\mathbf x))$ and $\widetilde q(t,\mathbf x):=q(t,\pi_L(\mathbf x))$ on $I\times\mathbb R^3$; under $\iota_I$, these are coordinate representatives of fields on $\iota_I(I\times\mathbb R^3)\subset M$. If $\Sigma=\mathbb R^3$, the given fields are already coordinate representatives on that region. Here $\vartheta$ is the temperature departure in K, $T=T_0+\vartheta$ is the local temperature, and $q$ is the physical heat-flux vector in the supported rest space, expressed in its fixed Cartesian rest basis and measured in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. Spatial $\nabla$ and $\operatorname{div}$ are Euclidean derivatives in metres on the Minkowski rest space, evaluated by periodic lifts when $\Sigma=\mathbb T_L^3$.

In the source-free effective model, adopt

$$C\,\partial_t\vartheta+\operatorname{div}q=0,\qquad \tau\,\partial_tq+q=-\kappa\nabla\vartheta.$$

The first equation is the subsystem's thermal-energy balance and the second is its Cattaneo constitutive relation. Also adopt the specified effective quadratic entropy density and entropy flux

$$s_{\mathrm{eff}}:=s_0+\frac{C\vartheta}{T_0}-\frac{C\vartheta^2}{2T_0^2}-\frac{\tau|q|^2}{2\kappa T_0^2},\qquad j_s:=\frac{q}{T_0}-\frac{\vartheta q}{T_0^2},$$

where $s_0$ is constant. Both $s_0$ and $s_{\mathrm{eff}}$ have units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, and $j_s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. This quadratic function is an adopted effective state function on $D$, not the exact nonlinear material entropy or a particle Gibbs equation of state. The model assigns no measured values to its coefficients, reports no experiment, and derives no microscopic transport law.

items.title: Separate no-conserved-number radiation fluid branch
items.statement:
Use the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry, metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, and length-coordinate conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. On an open region $O$ of a smooth four-manifold without boundary, take a smooth positive temperature field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ and a smooth future unit observer-congruence field $u$ satisfying $g(u,u)=-1$. Adopt the separate entropy-only state maps of [[def-tgr-entropy-only-radiation-state]] with a fixed parameter $a_R>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-4}}$:

$$\varepsilon=a_RT^4,\qquad p=\frac13a_RT^4,\qquad s=\frac43a_RT^3,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p.$$

The fields $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$ and $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$. Adopt the perfect stress tensor and its source-free balance

$$\mathsf T^{ab}:=h\,u^au^b+p\,g^{ab},\qquad \nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$$

on the specified smooth background. In the proper-time velocity convention $U^a:=c u^a$, this is equivalently $\mathsf T^{ab}=(h/c^2)U^aU^b+p g^{ab}$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. This branch has no conserved particle-number coordinate, particle-number current, or chemical-potential field. It adopts an effective equation of state and perfect-stress balance; it does not determine $a_R$ from quantum statistics, assert that a physical system realizes these maps, report a measurement, or derive an Einstein-field equation.

items.title: Conditional thermal entropy, stability, and finite propagation
items.statement:
For the global-evolution and forward-time clauses below, assume that the postulate's open time interval $I$ contains $0$. The local identities and telegrapher equation hold on any open interval on which a smooth solution is defined.

Let $C,\kappa,\tau,T_0,c,L>0$ and let $\Sigma$ be $\mathbb R^3$ or $\mathbb T_L^3$. If $\Sigma=\mathbb T_L^3$, use the periodic-lift convention of [[post-tgr-cattaneo-thermal-model]]: torus fields represent smooth spatially $L$-periodic fields on the rest slices of $M=\mathbb R^4$. Adopt the supported-rest Cattaneo equations and effective current of [[post-tgr-cattaneo-thermal-model]]. The equations are $C\vartheta_t+\operatorname{div}q=0$ and $\tau q_t+q=-\kappa\nabla\vartheta$, with Euclidean spatial derivatives. For any smooth solution on an open time interval, the exact effective entropy-production and quadratic Lyapunov identities are

$$\partial_t s_{\mathrm{eff}}+\operatorname{div}j_s=\frac{|q|^2}{\kappa T_0^2}\geq0,\qquad \partial_t e_L+\operatorname{div}(\vartheta q)=-\frac{|q|^2}{\kappa},\qquad e_L:=\frac12\left(C\vartheta^2+\frac{\tau}{\kappa}|q|^2\right).$$

The associated telegrapher equation is $\tau\vartheta_{tt}+\vartheta_t-(\kappa/C)\Delta\vartheta=0$, where $\Delta:=\operatorname{div}\nabla=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_{x^i}^2$ on the Euclidean rest space, and its characteristic propagation speed is $v_h:=\sqrt{\kappa/(C\tau)}$. Put $U_0=(\vartheta_0,q_0):=(\vartheta(0,\cdot),q(0,\cdot))$. For Schwartz data on $\mathbb R^3$ or smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$, the unique global smooth evolution, weighted-norm contraction, and finite propagation at $v_h$ follow conditionally from the exact mathematical interface in [F1]. Here Schwartz data mean componentwise $C^\infty$ data for which every $x^\alpha\partial^\beta U_0$ is bounded for multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^3$, as specified in [F2]. Since the spacetime model uses light speed $c$, the heat subsystem is relativistically causal exactly when

$$v_h\leq c\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\kappa\leq C\tau c^2.$$

On $\mathbb T_L^3$, for each integer $r>3/2$, the periodic solution supplied conditionally by [F1] obeys $T_0+\vartheta(t,x)>0$ for all $t\geq0$ whenever $K_{r,L,C}\|U_0\|_{H^r_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}<T_0$, with $K_{r,L,C}$ and $H^r_M$ exactly as defined there. This bound ensures positive temperature but does not by itself ensure that the solution stays in the selected domain $D$ of the postulate. The global linear PDE statement concerns the mathematical extension of the subsystem; its physical interpretation is restricted to times when $(\vartheta,q)\in D$. No empirical coefficient or material-specific validity is asserted.

items.title: Radiation entropy balance and causal linear sound
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. On an open region $O$ of a smooth four-manifold without boundary, let $(g,u,T)$ and the entropy-only equation of state and source-free perfect-stress balance be as in [[post-tgr-radiation-fluid-model]]. For every such smooth solution,

$$\nabla_a(su^a)=0.$$

This is a conditional local model deduction; it assumes no particle-number current. In the additional submodel $M=\mathbb R^4$ with Minkowski coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x)$, constant reference temperature $T_*>0$, and uniform rest observer $u_*=(1,0,0,0)$, the frozen linearized system for $r:=\delta\varepsilon$ and $w^i:=\delta u^i$ has two transverse zero characteristic speeds and longitudinal speeds $\pm c/\sqrt3$. Thus its linear acoustic speed is $c/\sqrt3<c$. This is a conditional prediction of the adopted model, not an observed speed or a claim of global nonlinear evolution. The parameter $a_R$ remains an adopted positive coefficient; no quantum blackbody calibration is supplied.

row.title: Supported-rest effective Cattaneo thermal model — Examples

items.title: Supported thermal finite-speed damped mode
items.statement:
Choose $C,\kappa,\tau,T_0,L>0$, an integer $n\geq1$, and set $k:=2\pi n/L$. Assume $k^2>C/(4\tau\kappa)$ and define

$$\Omega:=\sqrt{\frac{\kappa k^2}{C\tau}-\frac{1}{4\tau^2}}>0,\qquad \phi(t):=A e^{-t/(2\tau)}\cos(\Omega t).$$

On $\mathbb T_L^3$, using the postulate's periodic-lift convention so these fields represent smooth spatially $L$-periodic fields on the Minkowski rest space, let $e_1=(1,0,0)$ and put

$$\vartheta(t,x):=\phi(t)\cos(kx_1),\qquad q(t,x):=-\frac{C}{k}\phi'(t)\sin(kx_1)e_1.$$

For every real amplitude $A$, these fields are smooth on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb T_L^3$ and solve the supported-rest Cattaneo linear subsystem. For a nonzero amplitude chosen sufficiently small, $T_0+\vartheta$ stays positive for all $t\geq0$, and the state $(\vartheta,q)$ stays in the postulate's declared open near-equilibrium neighborhood. The temperature-departure envelope decays as $e^{-t/(2\tau)}$. This is a constructed model solution, not a reported observation; its physical interpretation is restricted to forward times inside that neighborhood.
