row.title: Stationary thermal geometric data

items.title: Stationary thermal geometric data
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and let
$\nabla$ be its unique torsion-free $g$-compatible connection supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix a nonempty
connected open set $O\subseteq M$. A **selected stationary thermal carrier** on
$O$ consists of a smooth future timelike vector field $\xi$ and a smooth
positive scalar field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$, where $T$ is measured in kelvins,
such that $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-killing-field]]. Equivalently, the criterion is
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ by
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. The round brackets mean
symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The choice of $\xi$ specifies the thermal congruence; no
coordinate chart or universal observer field is selected.

Set $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. Then
$g(u,u)=-1$. In the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, $u$ is
dimensionless and $cu$ is the physical four-velocity, with $c>0$ in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the inverse-temperature vector
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the Killing-normalized
temperature field $T_K:=N_\xi T$. Thus $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$; this definition
does not assert that $T_K$ is constant.

For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, put
$\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$, a dimensionless scalar. Define the rest-space metric,
derivative, acceleration, expansion and shear by
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\qquad D:=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_au^a,\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac13\theta h_{ab}.$$
Here $a$, $\theta$ and $\sigma$ have inverse-length units; the physical
proper acceleration is $c^2a$. The smooth tangent-bundle structure used by
the cited GR suppliers assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]; no stronger choice principle is part of this
definition.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§III.3 and VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.2.3 and 4.3.1
José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§III–V

items.title: Canonical future massive mass-shell measure
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $x\in M$, and let
$M_*>0$ be a rest-energy parameter in joules. The **future massive shell at
$x$** is the Borel subset
$$\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}:=\{P\in T_xM:g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}.$$
Use any smooth future orthonormal tetrad near $x$, whose existence is
[[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]]. At $x$ write its basis as
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and, for $q=(q_1,q_2,q_3)\in\mathbb R^3$ with energy
coordinates in joules, put
$$E(q):=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2},\qquad P_e(q):=E(q)e_0+\sum_{i=1}^3q_i e_i.$$
Let $\lambda_3$ be Euclidean Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]],
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]). For every Borel set
$A\subseteq\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, with its subspace Borel sigma-algebra
([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), define
$$\mu_{M_*,x,e}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf1_A(P_e(q))\,\frac{1}{E(q)}\,d\lambda_3(q).$$
In these tetrad coordinates the shell equation is
$-(P^0)^2+|q|^2=-M_*^2$, and the future sheet has $P^0>0$, hence
$P^0=E(q)$. Thus $P_e$ is a bijection onto the shell with continuous inverse
$q_i=g(P,e_i)$, so it is a homeomorphism. Continuous preimages of Borel sets are Borel
([[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]), and
$1/E(q)$ is a positive continuous density. The nonnegative Lebesgue integral
over a measurable set is [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]; the
positive-density measure theorem [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]] makes
$\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ a positive Borel measure. Its coordinate expression is
$d^3q/E(q)$ and its units are $\mathrm{J^2}$.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§II and III.3
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.3.3 and 4.3.1

items.title: Killing temperature normalization and rigidity
items.statement:
Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$
When this holds, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and the Killing congruence has
$$\xi(N_\xi)=0,\qquad a=\nabla\log N_\xi,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0.$$
If $\xi$ is replaced by $b\xi$ with a constant $b>0$, then
$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

references.title: José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§III–V
Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.2.3 and 4.3.1

items.title: Exact thermal Killing kinematic equivalence
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a connected open set in a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold, let $u$ be a smooth future unit timelike vector field on $O$
($g(u,u)=-1$), and let $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth. Define
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, $h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$D:=u^a\nabla_a$, $a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b$,
$\theta:=\nabla_au^a$ and
$\sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\theta h_{ab}/3$ as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then $\beta$ is a Killing field of
$g$ (equivalently $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ by
[[def-gr-killing-field]] and
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]) if and only if
$$DT=0,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0,\qquad h_a{}^b\nabla_b\log T=-a_a.$$
No hypersurface-orthogonality or vanishing-vorticity condition is assumed.

references.title: José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§II–V
Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.2

items.title: Natural tensors under Killing isometries
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], let $O\subseteq M$ be open, and let
$\xi$ be a smooth nowhere-zero vector field on $O$ satisfying
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ for the unique metric-selected connection $\nabla$
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Its local flow
$\Phi_s$ exists on the open flow
domains supplied by [[thm-flow-box-theorem]]. On every common flow domain,
$\Phi_s$ is a local isometry and preserves $\nabla$ and $\xi$. Consequently
it preserves the curvature tensor $R$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], all finite covariant
derivatives of $R$ and $\xi$, and every tensor or scalar obtained from these
fields by finitely many tensor products, contractions, and smooth scalar
operations. The assertion is local; it assumes no complete flow or global
isometry group. It makes no claim about arbitrary quantum observables or their
analytic representation by local curvature data.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.2.3, 2.3.3 and 4.3.1
Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.2

items.title: Mass-shell polynomial rigidity
items.statement:
Let $(V,g,C^+)$ be a four-dimensional time-oriented Lorentz vector space of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with future cone $C^+$ as in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]. Let $M>0$ and let $A$ be a
symmetric bilinear form on $V$ and $b$ a covector. If
$$A(P,P)+b(P)=0\qquad\text{for every }P\in C^+\text{ with }g(P,P)=-M^2,$$
then $A=0$ and $b=0$. If instead this identity holds for every nonzero future
null vector $P\in\overline{C^+}$, then $b=0$ and $A=\lambda g$ for some
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$. The second clause is the exact massless conformal
exception.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§III.3 and VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.1–2.2 and 4.3.1

items.title: Tetrad invariance of the future massive mass-shell measure
items.statement:
Let $x$ be an event of a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$M_*>0$, and let $e$ and $e'$ be any two smooth future orthonormal tetrads
near $x$. The measures $d\mu_{M_*,x,e}$ and $d\mu_{M_*,x,e'}$ defined in
[[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]] agree on every Borel subset of the future
massive shell at $x$. Hence the fiber measure $d\mu_{M_*,x}$ is independent of
the chosen future orthonormal tetrad.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§II and III.3
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.3.3 and 4.3.1

items.title: Jüttner partition, probability, and perfect-fluid moments
items.statement:
Let $x$ be an event in a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$M_*>0$ be an energy in joules, and let $u\in T_xM$ be future unit timelike,
$g(u,u)=-1$. Fix $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $T>0$ in kelvins,
$n>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and a reference
action $h_{\rm ref}>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Put
$$\alpha:=\frac1{k_BT},\qquad \beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},\qquad E_u(P):=-g(P,u).$$
For $j=0,1,2,3$ and $z>0$ define
$$K_j(z):=\int_0^\infty e^{-z\cosh t}\cosh(jt)\,dt.$$
With the future-shell measure of [[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]], define
$$I_{M_*}(\alpha):=\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}e^{g(\beta,P)}\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad Z_{M_*}(\alpha):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\alpha E(q)}\,d^3q,$$
where $E(q)=\sqrt{M_*^2+|q|^2}$ in a future orthonormal tetrad whose time
axis is $u$. Both integrals are finite and positive, and
$$I_{M_*}(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi M_*}{\alpha}K_1(\alpha M_*),\qquad Z_{M_*}(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi M_*^2}{\alpha}K_2(\alpha M_*).$$
The observer-rest momentum law
$$d\nu_u(q):=Z_{M_*}(\alpha)^{-1}e^{-\alpha E(q)}d^3q$$
is a probability measure. Define the dimensionless occupation and its number
current and stress moments by
$$\zeta:=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(\alpha)}\right),\qquad f(P):=e^{\zeta+g(\beta,P)},$$
$$J^a:=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^a f(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad T^{ab}:=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^aP^b f(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P).$$
These integrals converge, and, with
$$\varepsilon:=n\left(M_*\frac{K_1(\alpha M_*)}{K_2(\alpha M_*)}+\frac3\alpha\right),\qquad p:=\frac n\alpha=nk_BT,$$
they satisfy $J^a=nu^a$ and
$T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab}$. The quantities $J$ and $T$ have
units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, respectively. The reference
action $h_{\rm ref}$ is only a declared phase-space unit convention; it is
not Planck's constant or a measured parameter.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §III.3
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.3.1

items.title: Massive Jüttner stationarity and normalization
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $M_*>0$ be a
rest-energy, let $\beta$ be a smooth vector field with units
$\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, let $\zeta:O\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and dimensionless.
For each $x\in O$, let $\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$ be the future fiber shell of
[[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]], and define the total future massive
shell over $O$ by
$$\mathscr H^+_{M_*,O}:=\{(x,P)\in TM:x\in O,\ g_x(P,P)=-M_*^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}=\bigcup_{x\in O}\{x\}\times\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}.$$
Define on this total shell
$$f(x,P):=\exp\bigl(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\bigr),$$
and let $\mathcal L$ be the geodesic Liouville vector field on $TM$; in
induced tangent-bundle coordinates $(x^a,P^a)$ it is
$$\mathcal L:=P^a\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c\frac{\partial}{\partial P^a}.$$
The geodesic Liouville vector field $\mathcal L$ is tangent to
$\mathscr H^+_{M_*,O}$, and
$$\mathcal Lf=0\text{ at every }(x,P)\in\mathscr H^+_{M_*,O} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0\text{ and }d\zeta=0\text{ on }O,$$
where $\nabla_{(a}\beta_{b)}=0$ is the covariant Killing condition
([[def-gr-killing-field]], [[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]).
Since $O$ is connected, $d\zeta=0$ means $\zeta$ is constant on $O$.

For any vector $\beta_x\in T_xM$ with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, define its
shell normalizer by
$$I_{M_*}(\beta_x):=\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}e^{g_x(\beta_x,P)}\,d\mu_{M_*,x}(P).$$
This integral is finite exactly when $\beta_x$ is future timelike. If so, with
$\alpha:=\sqrt{-g_x(\beta_x,\beta_x)}>0$, it equals
$4\pi M_*K_1(\alpha M_*)/\alpha$ as in
[[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]]. In particular, for carrier data
$\beta=u/(k_BT)$, the choice
$$\zeta=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(1/(k_BT))}\right)$$
normalizes the proper number density to $n$ and gives exactly the number
current and stress moments of
[[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]]. This is a mathematical theorem about
the specified exponential ansatz; it does not assert that a material
thermalizes or that a physical equilibrium state exists.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §§III.3 and VI.2
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.3.1
José Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §IV

row.title: Stationary thermal geometric data — Examples

items.title: No massive Killing equilibrium in a spatially flat expanding FLRW metric
items.statement:
Let $L_0>0$ be a length and take
$O=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3$ with coordinates $(s,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, where
$s$ and $x^i$ have length units. Give $O$ the time-oriented Lorentzian metric
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
$$g=-ds^2+a(s)^2\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j,\qquad a(s):=s/L_0,$$
with future direction increasing $s$. This is the spatially flat FLRW
geometry with the scale factor explicitly fixed to $a(s)=s/L_0$.

(a) The scalar curvature, using the convention of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], is $S(s)=6/s^2$. Consequently
no nonempty open subset of $O$ admits a timelike Killing vector field.

(b) By [[thm-tgr-massive-juttner-stationarity]], the specified normalizable
massive exponential ansatz has no stationary state on any nonempty open
subset of $O$.

(c) Define the **future null fiber** and its **total future null shell** over $O$ by
$$\mathcal H^+_{0,x}:=\{P\in T_xO:P\ne0,\ g_x(P,P)=0,\ g_x(P,\partial_s)<0\},\qquad \mathscr H^+_{0,O}:=\{(x,P)\in TO:x\in O,\ P\in\mathcal H^+_{0,x}\}.$$
A smooth vector field $X$ on $O$ is **conformal Killing** when
$\nabla_{(a}X_{b)}=\lambda g_{ab}$ for some smooth scalar
$\lambda:O\to\mathbb R$, with symmetrization factor $1/2$ and
$X_b=g_{bc}X^c$. On the total shell use the restriction of the geodesic
Liouville vector field of [[thm-tgr-massive-juttner-stationarity]], namely
$$\mathcal L=P^a\partial_{x^a}-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c\partial_{P^a}.$$
For a smooth function $f:\mathscr H^+_{0,O}\to(0,\infty)$, the **null-shell
Liouville equation** means $\mathcal Lf=0$ everywhere on this domain.
For smooth $\beta$ and $\zeta$, the exponential transport condition instead
permits conformal Killing inverse-temperature fields. In particular,
$\beta=b(s/L_0)\partial_s$ for a constant $b>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$ is future
timelike and conformal Killing, and for constant $\zeta$ the massless
exponential $f=e^{\zeta+g(\beta,P)}$ satisfies the null-shell Liouville
equation. This is a mathematical null-shell example; it asserts no physical
state or empirical radiation result.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VIII
David Tong, General Relativity, full Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.3.1

row.title: Gauge-compensated charged Killing energy

items.title: Independent finite entropy-exchange equilibrium

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics lecture notes, chapter 1, §§1.2.2 and 1.4
David Schaich, Statistical Physics lecture notes, complete 171-page notes, Unit 6, pp. 80–90

items.statement:
Let $r\ge1$ be finite. For each cell $i=1,\ldots,r$, let $U_i\subseteq\mathbb R^2$
be open and convex, with coordinates $(E_i,n_i)$, and let
$S_i\in C^1(U_i,\mathbb R)$ be concave. The coordinates may be assigned SI
dimensions $[E_i]=\mathrm J$, $[n_i]=1$, and $[S_i]=\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$; the
particle-number coordinate is a continuous thermodynamic variable. Fix
constants $N_i>0$ (dimensionless), $\Phi_i\in\mathbb R$ (volts), and a common
charge $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). Define
$$\mathcal E(x):=\sum_{i=1}^r(N_iE_i+q\Phi_i n_i),\qquad \mathcal N(x):=\sum_{i=1}^r n_i,\qquad S_{\rm tot}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^rS_i(E_i,n_i).$$
For a supplied feasible interior point $x^*\in U:=\prod_iU_i$, let
$A:\mathbb R^{2r}\to\mathbb R^2$ be the linear map whose rows are the
coefficients of $(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)$. Call $x^*$ stationary under
independent exchange variations when
$DS_{\rm tot}(x^*)[h]=0$ for every $h\in\ker A$. Assume
$\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*)>0$ and define
$$\frac1{T_i}:=\partial_{E_i}S_i(x_i^*),\qquad \frac{\mu_i}{T_i}:=-\partial_{n_i}S_i(x_i^*).$$
Then $x^*$ is stationary if and only if there are constants $T_K>0$ and
$\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ such that, for every cell,
$$N_iT_i=T_K,\qquad N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K.$$
If each $S_i$ is concave, every such stationary point is a global maximizer of
$S_{\rm tot}$ on the feasible set in $U$. If each $S_i$ is strictly concave,
that maximizer is unique whenever it exists. No existence or boundary
attainment of a stationary point is asserted. These are finite-dimensional
conditional deductions; the coefficients $N_i,\Phi_i$ are inputs, not
predictions about a physical system.

items.title: Charged particle and Liouville data on a stationary Lorentzian domain

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity lecture notes, §4.3.2, Killing fields and conserved particle quantities
Igor Bogush, Kirill Kobialko and Dmitri Gal’tsov, Constructing massive particles surfaces in static spacetimes, arXiv:2402.03266v1, §II

items.statement:
Use SI dimensions and the signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Take the geometric data of
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]: $O$ is a nonempty connected open domain in a
smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$, $\nabla$ is the
Levi–Civita connection, and $\xi$ is a smooth future-directed timelike Killing
field with dimensionless components in physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$
and $x^i$ measured in metres. Put $N:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and
$u:=\xi/N$, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its smooth
tangent-bundle data carry the supplier's explicit foundational assumption
[[def-countable-choice]] ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$); no stronger choice principle
is added here.

Let $A$ be a smooth real one-form on $O$: for each $x\in O$, $A_x:T_xO\to\mathbb R$
is linear, and in every smooth chart $(x^a)$ its coefficients $A_a$ are smooth
and obey the covector transformation law $A'_i=A_a\,\partial x^a/\partial y^i$
on an overlapping chart $(y^i)$. The coefficients have units tesla metres.
Define $F$ in each chart by
$$F_{ab}:=(dA)_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a.$$
This prescription defines a global smooth antisymmetric covariant two-tensor:
under a change of chart $x=x(y)$ the chain rule gives
$$F'_{ij}=F_{ab}\,\frac{\partial x^a}{\partial y^i}\frac{\partial x^b}{\partial y^j},$$
since the only additional term is
$A_a(\partial_i\partial_jx^a-\partial_j\partial_ix^a)=0$. Thus $F=dA$ is a two-form;
its components have units tesla. A global gauge compensator is a smooth real
function $\Lambda_\xi$ on $O$ satisfying
$$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi,\qquad (\mathcal L_\xi A)_a:=\xi^b\partial_bA_a+A_b\partial_a\xi^b$$
in every smooth chart. This defines the Lie-derivative coefficients globally:
under $x=x(y)$, put $J^a_i:=\partial x^a/\partial y^i$ and
$K^i_a:=\partial y^i/\partial x^a$. Substitution of
$A'_i=A_aJ^a_i$ and $\xi'^i=K^i_a\xi^a$ gives
$$ (\mathcal L_\xi A)'_i=\xi^b(\partial_bA_a)J^a_i+\xi^bA_aK^j_b\partial_jJ^a_i+A_cJ^c_j(\partial_iK^j_b)\xi^b+A_bJ^a_i\partial_a\xi^b. $$
Differentiating $J^c_jK^j_b=\delta^c_b$ and using
$\partial_jJ^a_i=\partial_iJ^a_j$ cancels the two middle terms, leaving
$(\mathcal L_\xi A)'_i=(\mathcal L_\xi A)_aJ^a_i$. The units of
$\Lambda_\xi$ are
tesla metres. Define contraction by
$(\iota_\xi F)_a:=\xi^bF_{ba}$ and set
$$\Psi_\xi:=\xi^aA_a-\Lambda_\xi,\qquad \Phi_\xi:=-c\Psi_\xi.$$
Thus $\Psi_\xi$ has units tesla metres and $\Phi_\xi$ has units volts.

Let $c>0$ be the speed of light, let $m>0$ be a particle rest mass in
kilograms, let $q\in\mathbb R$ be its charge in coulombs, and put
$M:=mc^2>0$ joules. A charged massive Lorentz trajectory is a $C^2$ curve
$x:J\to O$, where $J$ is an open real interval, parametrized by physical
length $s_m=c\tau$ in metres, with future unit tangent
$w:=dx/ds_m$, $g(w,w)=-1$, energy four-vector $P:=Mw$, and equation
$$\nabla_wP^a=cqF^a{}_bw^b,\qquad F^a{}_b:=g^{ac}F_{cb}.$$
In particular $g(P,P)=-M^2$ and $P$ is future directed. This is a conditional
definition of curves satisfying the equation; it makes no existence claim.

The future massive shell for this definition is the subset
$$\mathcal P_M^+(O):=\{(x,P)\in TO:g_x(P,P)=-M^2,\ P\text{ future directed}\}.$$
On the full tangent bundle $TO$, define charged transport as the vector field
whose integral curves, with parameter $\lambda=s_m/M$, satisfy
$$\frac{dx^a}{d\lambda}=P^a,\qquad \nabla_{dx/d\lambda}P^a=cqF^a{}_bP^b.$$
In a smooth chart its expression is
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}:=P^a\partial_{x^a}+\left(-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}P^bP^c+cqF^a{}_bP^b\right)\partial_{P^a}.$$
The restriction of this field to $\mathcal P_M^+(O)$ is justified by
[[lem-tgr-charged-liouville-preserves-mass-shell]]. For any smooth real scalar
$\zeta$ and smooth vector field $\beta$ with components in inverse joules,
define the dimensionless charged exponential ansatz on the shell by
$$f(x,P):=\exp\!\left(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\right),\qquad \beta_b:=g_{bc}\beta^c.$$
The equation $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ means that the derivative of this function
along the restricted charged transport vector field vanishes.

Under a smooth gauge change $A\mapsto A+d\chi$, with $\chi$ in tesla square
metres, the corresponding compensator changes by
$\Lambda_\xi\mapsto\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$. These definitions fix the sign
convention for $F$, the Lorentz force, and the potential terms used on this
page.

items.title: Charged Liouville transport preserves the future massive shell

references.title: Igor Bogush, Kirill Kobialko and Dmitri Gal’tsov, Constructing massive particles surfaces in static spacetimes, arXiv:2402.03266v1, §II

items.statement:
For the smooth Lorentzian data, $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $F=dA$, and charged
transport vector field defined in [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]], the set
$\mathcal P_M^+(O)$ is a smooth hypersurface of $TO$, and $\mathcal L_{F,q}$
is tangent to it. Hence its restriction to the future massive shell is a
well-defined smooth vector field. No mass-shell measure or particle
normalization is asserted.

items.title: Gauge-compensated charged Killing energy

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity lecture notes, §4.3.2, Killing fields and conserved particle quantities
Igor Bogush, Kirill Kobialko and Dmitri Gal’tsov, Constructing massive particles surfaces in static spacetimes, arXiv:2402.03266v1, §II

Kai Shi, Yu Tian, Xiaoning Wu, Hongbao Zhang and Chuanjia Zhu, Thermodynamic equilibrium condition and the first law of thermodynamics for charged perfect fluids in electromagnetic and gravitational fields, §§2–3

items.statement:
Use the Lorentzian geometry, units, charge sign, potential $A$, field $F=dA$,
compensator $\Lambda_\xi$, and $C^2$ charged trajectory $x(s_m)$ of
[[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Assume the global potential symmetry
$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Define
$$H_\xi:=-g(P,\xi)+q\Phi_\xi=-g(P,\xi)-cq\Psi_\xi.$$
Then $\iota_\xi F=-d\Psi_\xi$, and $H_\xi$ is constant along every interval
on which the trajectory obeys the stated Lorentz equation. It is invariant under
$A\mapsto A+d\chi$, $\Lambda_\xi\mapsto\Lambda_\xi+\xi(\chi)$. Replacing the
potential reference by $\Phi_\xi+C_0$ changes $H_\xi$ by $qC_0$.

This is a conditional mathematical statement about curves satisfying the
displayed equation. It asserts neither existence of such curves for arbitrary
initial data nor that the model describes nature.

items.title: Global electrochemical redshift from charged Liouville stationarity

references.title: Jorge A. Rueda, Remo Ruffini and She-Sheng Xue, The Klein first integrals in an equilibrium system with electromagnetic, weak, strong and gravitational interactions, §4

Kai Shi, Yu Tian, Xiaoning Wu, Hongbao Zhang and Chuanjia Zhu, Thermodynamic equilibrium condition and the first law of thermodynamics for charged perfect fluids in electromagnetic and gravitational fields, §§2–3
David Tong, General Relativity lecture notes, §4.3.2
Igor Bogush, Kirill Kobialko and Dmitri Gal’tsov, Constructing massive particles surfaces in static spacetimes, arXiv:2402.03266v1, §II

items.statement:
Let $O$ be a connected domain with the stationary Lorentzian data, potential
$A$, field $F=dA$, Killing field $\xi$, lapse $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, future
unit stationary observer $u=\xi/N$, and charged transport on the future mass
shell from [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Let $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$,
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$ for a smooth proper-temperature scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$,
and $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ for a smooth chemical-potential scalar
$\mu:O\to\mathbb R$. Define $f(x,P)=\exp(\zeta+g(\beta,P))$. Without any global
potential-symmetry assumption,
$$\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \beta\text{ is Killing and }d\zeta=-cq\,\iota_\beta F.$$

If, in addition, a global smooth compensator satisfies
$\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$, define $\Phi_\xi=-c(\iota_\xi A-\Lambda_\xi)$.
Then the stationarity conditions above are equivalent to the existence of
constants $T_K>0$ and $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$NT=T_K,\qquad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K},\qquad N\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K.$$
With $E_{\rm loc}:=-g(P,u)$ and
$H_\xi:=-g(P,\xi)+q\Phi_\xi$, the same exponent then has both forms
$$\zeta+g(\beta,P)=-\frac{E_{\rm loc}-\mu}{k_BT} =-\frac{H_\xi-\mu_K}{k_BT_K}.$$
Here $N$ is dimensionless, $T,T_K$ are kelvins, $\mu,\mu_K,E_{\rm loc},H_\xi$
are joules per particle, $\Phi_\xi$ is volts, $q$ is coulombs, and
$\beta\cdot P$ and $\zeta$ are dimensionless. All claims are mathematical
conditional deductions from the displayed smooth data; no equilibrium state,
particle ensemble, or physical realization is asserted to exist.

row.title: Gauge-compensated charged Killing energy — Examples

items.title: Electric circulation obstructs a global charged equilibrium scalar
items.statement:
Let $L>0$ and let
$O:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times S^1_L\times\mathbb R^2_{x^2,x^3}$, where
$S^1_L:=\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z$. Let $\vartheta$ be the smooth global closed
one-form on $S^1_L$ induced by $d\widetilde\theta$ on its universal cover,
normalized by $\oint_{S^1_L}\vartheta=L$. Give $O$ the flat product metric
$$g=-(dx^0)^2+\vartheta\otimes\vartheta+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2$$
and time orientation $\xi:=\partial_{x^0}$. Then $\xi$ is a future timelike
Killing field with $N=1$. For a nonzero constant $E_0$ in tesla, define the
global potential and field
$$A:=E_0x^0\vartheta,\qquad F:=dA=E_0\,dx^0\wedge\vartheta.$$
For a charged massive species with $qE_0\ne0$, take $T=T_K>0$ constant and
$\beta:=\xi/(k_BT_K)$. Although $F$ is exact and stationary, no smooth
single-valued scalar $\zeta:O\to\mathbb R$ makes
$f(x,P)=\exp(\zeta(x)+g(\beta,P))$ stationary under the charged Liouville
transport of [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]].

row.title: Constructed independent cell Gibbs states

items.title: Constructed independent cell Gibbs states
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Let $r\ge1$ be finite. For each cell $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, let $\mathcal H_i$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d_i\ge1$, let $H_i=H_i^*$ be a Hermitian proper Hamiltonian in joules, and let $Q_i=Q_i^*$ be a dimensionless number observable whose eigenvalues lie in $\mathbb N_0$. Assume $[H_i,Q_i]=0$. Operators $H_i,Q_i$ on the total space $\mathcal H:=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\mathcal H_i$ mean their lifts acting on the $i$th tensor factor and as the identity on the other factors; no intercell interaction is included.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $O\subseteq M$ be a connected open set on which a smooth future-directed timelike Killing field $\xi$ is defined. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and the corresponding dimensionless components of $\xi$. Define its dimensionless lapse $N(x):=\sqrt{-g_x(\xi_x,\xi_x)}>0$. Let $c>0$ be the speed of light in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $k_B>0$ Boltzmann's constant in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and let $A$ be a global smooth real one-form with SI components in tesla-metres, $F:=dA$ with components in teslas, and $\Lambda_\xi:O\to\mathbb R$ a global smooth compensator in tesla-metres with $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Define $\Phi_\xi(x):=-c\bigl((\iota_\xi A)_x-\Lambda_\xi(x)\bigr)$ in volts. Let $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ and $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ be smooth fields in kelvins and joules per particle. Fix a common particle rest mass $m>0$ in kilograms and charge $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs, put $M:=mc^2>0$ in joules, and define $u:=\xi/N$, $\beta:=u/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ dimensionlessly. On the future massive shell $\mathcal P_M^+(O):=\{(x,P)\in TO:g_x(P,P)=-M^2,\ P\text{ future-directed}\}$, where $P$ has energy-vector units and $g_x(P,P)$ has units $\mathrm{J^2}$, let $f(x,P):=\exp\bigl(\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)\bigr)$, as defined for the same charged data in [[thm-tgr-electrochemical-stationarity]], and assume the exact whole-shell stationarity condition $\mathcal L_{F,q}f(x,P)=0$ for every $(x,P)\in\mathcal P_M^+(O)$, where $\mathcal L_{F,q}$ is the charged transport field in that supplier's formulation. This is the stationarity premise of [[thm-tgr-electrochemical-stationarity]]. Choose a cell-location map $\chi:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to O$ and set $x_i:=\chi(i)$. Define the lapse, compensated potential, proper temperature, and chemical potential at cell $i$ by evaluation:
$$N_i:=N(x_i),\qquad \Phi_i:=\Phi_\xi(x_i),\qquad T_i:=T(x_i),\qquad \mu_i:=\mu(x_i).$$
The same theorem supplies constants $T_K>0$ and $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$N_iT_i=T_K,\qquad N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K,$$
where $q$ is the common particle charge in coulombs. This use of the charged smooth-geometry supplier retains its explicit $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption.

Set $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, $\beta_i=N_i\beta_K=(k_BT_i)^{-1}$, $H_K=\sum_{i=1}^r(N_iH_i+q\Phi_iQ_i)$, and $Q=\sum_{i=1}^rQ_i$. Then the grand generator $G_K:=H_K-\mu_KQ$ is Hermitian and
$$G_K=\sum_{i=1}^rN_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i).$$
The finite partition sums
$$Z_i:=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i)},\qquad Z:=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H}e^{-\beta_KG_K}$$
are positive and finite, with $Z=\prod_{i=1}^r Z_i$. The normalized Gibbs density factorizes exactly:
$$\rho:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta_KG_K}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\rho_i,\qquad \rho_i:=Z_i^{-1}e^{-\beta_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i)}.$$
It is a $\beta_K$-KMS state for the grand-generator dynamics on the full finite matrix algebra. On the neutral subalgebra $\mathcal A_0:=\{B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H):[B,Q]=0\}$, grand-generator and physical $H_K$ dynamics coincide, so the restricted state is $\beta_K$-KMS for the physical dynamics there. This constructs only independent finite cells; it does not claim that an interacting system's reduced cell states are Gibbs states.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, Definition 3.4.4 and finite Gibbs/KMS calculation, printed pp. 74, 76–77
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7 and Chapter 2 §6, printed pp. 13–14, 24

items.title: KMS orbit clock rescaling
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra and let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a strongly continuous one-parameter group of $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$. Let $\omega$ be a $\beta_K$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in the physical-time convention of [[def-qsm-kms-state]], where $\beta_K>0$ has units $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $\hbar>0$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. For a constant dimensionless $\lambda>0$, define
$$\alpha^\lambda_\tau:=\alpha_{\tau/\lambda},$$
where $t$ and $\tau$ are real time parameters in seconds. Then $\omega$ is a $\lambda\beta_K$-KMS state for $\alpha^\lambda$, with strip width $\lambda\beta_K\hbar$ seconds. Conversely, if $\omega$ is a $\widehat\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha^\lambda$, then it is a $(\widehat\beta/\lambda)$-KMS state for $\alpha$.

For the geometric interpretation, let $O$ be a connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $\xi$ be a smooth future-directed timelike Killing field on $O$ with dimensionless components in length coordinates $x^0=ct$, where $c>0$ is the speed of light in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Define $N_\xi(x):=\sqrt{-g_x(\xi_x,\xi_x)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a selected point $x_0\in O$, let $I_K\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval in seconds containing $0$, and let $\gamma_{x_0}:I_K\to O$ be the $C^1$ integral curve of $c\xi$ with $\gamma_{x_0}(0)=x_0$, so $\gamma_{x_0}'(t_K)=c\,\xi_{\gamma_{x_0}(t_K)}$; this is the Killing orbit through $x_0$ with Killing-time parameter $t_K$. For a cell assigned to $x_i$, take $x_0=x_i$ and denote this curve by $\gamma_i$. Define its proper-time parameter from the metric by
$$\tau(t_K):=\frac1c\int_0^{t_K}\sqrt{-g_{\gamma_{x_0}(s)}\bigl(\gamma_{x_0}'(s),\gamma_{x_0}'(s)\bigr)}\,ds,\qquad \tau(0)=0.$$
By [[lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization]], $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, so $N:=N_\xi(x_0)>0$ is constant along this orbit. The metric definition then gives $d\tau=N\,dt_K$ and, with the chosen origins, $\tau=Nt_K$; equivalently $d\gamma_{x_0}/d\tau=cu$ for $u=\xi/N_\xi$. For $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and reference temperature $T_K>0$ in kelvins, the inverse temperature $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$ rescales orbitwise to $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}:=N\beta_K$; defining $T_{\mathrm{loc}}:=(k_B\beta_{\mathrm{loc}})^{-1}$ gives $T_{\mathrm{loc}}=T_K/N$. No spatially varying lapse is treated as one global time-rescaled automorphism group.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, §3.4, Definition 3.4.4, printed p. 74
David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, Chapter 1 §7, printed pp. 13–14

items.title: Finite response and spectral clock redshift
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Fix a cell label $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$ in [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]], let $x_i=\chi(i)$ be its assigned point, and write $N:=N_i=N(x_i)>0$, $H_{\mathrm{loc}}:=H_i$, $Q:=Q_i$, and $\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\mu_i$. Let $\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and $\mu_K$ in joules be the global parameters supplied there. Put $G_{\mathrm{loc}}:=H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}Q$ and $G_K:=NG_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Set $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}:=N\beta_K$ and define the cell normalizer $Z_{\mathrm{loc}}:=Z_i=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}G_{\mathrm{loc}}}=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_KG_K}>0$. Let $\sigma$ be the cell Gibbs density supplied by that theorem, so $\sigma=Z_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}G_{\mathrm{loc}}}=Z_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1}e^{-\beta_KG_K}$. For neutral Hermitian matrices, define
$$\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(C):=e^{iG_{\mathrm{loc}}\tau/\hbar}Ce^{-iG_{\mathrm{loc}}\tau/\hbar},\qquad \alpha^K_t(C):=e^{iG_Kt/\hbar}Ce^{-iG_Kt/\hbar}.$$
For this selected cell, let $q$ be the common charge in coulombs and $\Phi_i:=\Phi_\xi(x_i)$ its compensated potential in volts from the supplier. Define $H_{K,i}:=NH_{\mathrm{loc}}+q\Phi_iQ$ in joules, and write $H_K:=H_{K,i}$ in the physical control below. The supplier normalization gives $N\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}+q\Phi_i=\mu_K$, hence $H_K=G_K+\mu_KQ$.

Let $A=A^*$ and $B=B^*$ satisfy $[A,Q]=[B,Q]=0$. Then their local proper-time and Killing-time dynamics agree after $\tau=Nt$.

Let $h:[0,S]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $S>0$ seconds, and let $h(\tau)B$ have units joules. For dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, the proper-time grand-generator control $G_{\mathrm{loc}}-\epsilon h(\tau)B$ corresponds in Killing time to $G_K-\epsilon N h(Nt)B$. Define $E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)$ and $E_K(t)$ as the finite-time expectations of $A$ from the same initial density $\sigma$ under these controls. Because $A$ and $B$ commute with $Q$, replacing each grand generator by its physical Hamiltonian changes the propagator only by a unitary generated by a constant multiple of $Q$ and leaves the expectation of $A$ unchanged. Thus these expectations also equal those obtained from the respective physical controls $H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\epsilon h(\tau)B$ and $H_K-\epsilon Nh(Nt)B$. In particular,
$$E_K(t)=E_{\mathrm{loc}}(Nt)\qquad(0\le t\le S/N).$$
The finite-time Kubo expansions have identical first-order terms under this rescaling and the same quadratic remainder bound. With
$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(u):=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_S:=\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_0^S|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds,$$
the local expansion is
$$E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(A))+\epsilon\int_0^\tau h(s)R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau-s)\,ds+r_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau),\qquad |r_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_S)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_S}}2.$$
Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, so $C_S$ is dimensionless and $R_{\mathrm{loc}}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm{J\,s})$. The Killing-time response kernel is $R_K(t)=R_{\mathrm{loc}}(Nt)$ and its control amplitude is $Nh(Nt)$.

For the equilibrium correlation spectral measures, use the Fourier convention of [[thm-qsm-dt-spectral-fdt]]. If $D_N(\omega):=N\omega$, then
$$S_K=(D_N)_*S_{\mathrm{loc}},\qquad S_K(\omega)=N^{-1}S_{\mathrm{loc}}(\omega/N)$$
in distribution notation; the measure form preserves the weights of delta-function spectral lines. Since $\beta_K\hbar(N\omega)=\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\hbar\omega$, detailed balance is unchanged. Any zero-frequency atom remains an atom at zero and is not assigned a value by the coth formula, which remains restricted to nonzero frequencies.

For a static local perturbation $G_{\mathrm{loc}}-\lambda B$, where $\lambda B$ has units joules, the re-prepared Gibbs family satisfies
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\lambda}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\lambda B)\right|_{\lambda=0}=\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)=N\beta_K\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)\ge0.$$
Here $\delta B:=B-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma B)I$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B):=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma^{1-u}\delta B\,\sigma^u\delta B\right)\,du.$$
It reduces to the ordinary variance when $B$ commutes with $G_{\mathrm{loc}}$; no such reduction is asserted otherwise. These are exact finite-dimensional deductions for the constructed neutral cell. They imply no infinite-time relaxation, dc transport coefficient, or response law for arbitrary interacting reduced states.

items.title: Completeness of countable square-summable sequences
items.design_state: Local mathematical supplier added under the Step 1 prerequisite rule; complete coordinate-limit proof is on the A page.
items.statement:
With the inner product and norm of [[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]], the complex sequence space
$$\ell^2(\mathbb N_0,\mathbb C):=\left\{x=(x_n)_{n\ge0}:\sum_{n\ge0}|x_n|^2<\infty\right\}$$
is complete. Hence it is a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]].

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, Chapter 2 §2.1, Definition 2.1.1 and Exercise 2.1.2, printed pp. 13–14 (PDF pp. 12–13)

items.title: Rotating mode Gibbs obstruction
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved A-page claim; hypotheses, caveats, and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-64 notes.
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and let $\mathcal H:=\ell^2(\mathbb N_0,\mathbb C)$ be the complex square-summable sequences with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{n\ge0}x_n\overline{y_n}$, linear in its first argument. Let $e_n$ be the sequence with value $1$ at $n$ and $0$ elsewhere. Write $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ for the bounded complex-linear operators on $\mathcal H$, with operator norm $\|B\|:=\sup_{\|x\|_2\le1}\|Bx\|_2$; for $C\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$, $C^*$ is its bounded Hilbert-space adjoint, characterized by $\langle Cx,y\rangle=\langle x,C^*y\rangle$. A state on this operator algebra means a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(C^*C)\ge0$ for every $C\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Define the occupation-number operator
$$D(\mathcal N):=\left\{x\in\mathcal H:\sum_{n\ge0}n^2|x_n|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad (\mathcal Nx)_n:=nx_n.$$
For a densely defined operator $T$ on this space, use the adjoint relation
$$D(T^\dagger):=\left\{y\in\mathcal H:\exists z\in\mathcal H\ \forall x\in D(T),\ \langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,z\rangle\right\},\qquad T^\dagger y:=z.$$
The representing $z$ is unique when $D(T)$ is dense; here “self-adjoint” means $D(T^\dagger)=D(T)$ and $T^\dagger x=Tx$ on that domain.

Let $\epsilon>0$ be in joules, $m\in\mathbb Z$ a dimensionless azimuthal mode number, $\Omega\in\mathbb R$ an angular velocity in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, and $\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$. Set
$$H:=\epsilon\mathcal N,\qquad J:=\hbar m\mathcal N,\qquad a:=\epsilon-\hbar m\Omega.$$ 
For $m\ne0$, $J$ has domain $D(\mathcal N)$; for $m=0$, $J$ is the zero operator on all of $\mathcal H$. The operator $H$ has energy units J, $J$ has angular-momentum units J s, and $a$ has energy units J, so $\Omega J$ also has units J. Define $K_0:=H-\Omega J$ on the common domain $D(\mathcal N)$ and let $K:=\overline{K_0}$ be its operator closure. For $a\ne0$, $K=a\mathcal N$ has domain $D(\mathcal N)$; for $a=0$, $K$ is the zero operator on all of $\mathcal H$. Thus $K$ is the self-adjoint closure of the rotating generator $H-\Omega J$, including at the zero threshold. Then $\mathcal N$, $H$, $J$ and $K$ are self-adjoint on the stated domains.

Define the one-mode occupation partition sum by
$$Z_{\beta_K}(a):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty e^{-\beta_Kan}\in[0,+\infty].$$
It is the diagonal trace of the positive Gibbs weights in the occupation basis whenever the sum is finite. This sum is finite exactly when $a=\epsilon-\hbar m\Omega>0$, in which case
$$Z_{\beta_K}(a)=\frac{1}{1-e^{-\beta_Ka}}.$$
For $a>0$, the weights $p_n=Z_{\beta_K}(a)^{-1}e^{-\beta_Kan}$ sum to one and define the diagonal Gibbs functional
$$\omega_a(B):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_n\langle Be_n,e_n\rangle,\qquad B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H).$$
The proof shows that this is a state in the stated sense. For $a\le0$, the occupation partition sum diverges, so no normalized Gibbs state of this trace form exists. This is a single bosonic mode calculation; it constructs no continuum field state or rotating-spacetime equilibrium.

items.title: Proper clock two-level response
items.design_state: Authored exact finite-dimensional worked example under the reserved B-page scope; no apparatus or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Take a cell label $i$ from [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]], with assigned location $x_i=\chi(i)$ and lapse $N:=N_i=N(x_i)>0$. For this neutral two-level example, take Hilbert space $\mathbb C^2$, number operator $Q=0$, and proper Hamiltonian
$$H_{\mathrm{loc}}=\frac{\Delta}{2}Z,\qquad \Delta>0\ \mathrm J.$$
Here
$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
are dimensionless Hermitian Pauli matrices. Let $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}=N\beta_K>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and prepare
$$\sigma=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}H_{\mathrm{loc}}}}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}H_{\mathrm{loc}}})}.$$
For the dimensionless observable and control $A=B=X$, the proper-time Kubo kernel, its Killing-time version, and the spectral measure are
$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=\frac{2}{\hbar}\tanh\!\left(\frac{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta}{2}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{\Delta\tau}{\hbar}\right),\qquad R_K(t)=\frac{2}{\hbar}\tanh\!\left(\frac{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta}{2}\right)\sin\!\left(\frac{N\Delta t}{\hbar}\right),$$
$$S_{\mathrm{loc}}=2\pi\left(p_+\delta_{-\Delta/\hbar}+p_-\delta_{\Delta/\hbar}\right),\qquad p_+=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2}}{2\cosh(\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2)},\quad p_-=\frac{e^{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2}}{2\cosh(\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta/2)}.$$
The Killing-time spectral measure is the pushforward of $S_{\mathrm{loc}}$ under $\omega\mapsto N\omega$, so its two lines are at $\pm N\Delta/\hbar$ with the same respective weights. The oscillation period is $2\pi\hbar/\Delta$ in proper time and $2\pi\hbar/(N\Delta)$ in Killing time.

For the separately re-prepared static family
$$\sigma_\lambda:=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}(H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\lambda X)}}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}(H_{\mathrm{loc}}-\lambda X)})},\qquad \lambda\ \mathrm J,$$
the static Gibbs susceptibility is
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\lambda}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\lambda X)\right|_{\lambda=0}=\frac{2}{\Delta}\tanh\!\left(\frac{\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}\Delta}{2}\right).$$
This finite model has persistent spectral lines and an oscillatory response. Its static Gibbs derivative is not a dc transport coefficient, and no infinite-time decay is asserted.

row.title: Heat and viscous entropy specialization

items.title: Spatial shear properties and nonnegative norm
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, let $O\subseteq M$ be open, and let $u$ be a smooth vector field on $O$ satisfying $g(u,u)=-1$ and $g(u,N)<0$ pointwise. Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of $g$. Define
$$
h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_a u_b,\qquad h_a{}^c:=\delta_a{}^c+u_a u^c,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_a u^a,
$$
and the shear
$$
\sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^c h_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac{\theta}{3}h_{ab},
$$
where parentheses denote symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The field $u$ is a future unit timelike observer field in the convention of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Then $\sigma_{ab}$ is symmetric, spatial in both indices ($u^a\sigma_{ab}=u^b\sigma_{ab}=0$), and trace-free ($g^{ab}\sigma_{ab}=0$). The metric restricted to $u^\perp$ is positive definite, so
$$
\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}\ge 0,
$$
with equality exactly when $\sigma_{ab}=0$. More generally, every spatial vector $Y$ satisfies $g_{ab}Y^aY^b\ge0$, with equality exactly when $Y=0$. These are pointwise geometric statements and assume no field equation.

items.title: Heat and viscous entropy specialization
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, let $O\subseteq M$ be nonempty and open, and let $u$ be a smooth future unit timelike vector field on $O$. Use the metric-compatible torsion-free connection $\nabla$ and a smooth local state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$ with $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ open and $e\in C^\infty(X)$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Thus $n=v^{-1}>0$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\epsilon=ne$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, and $\mu=e+pv-T\sigma_p$; assume $T>0$ on $O$ and the Gibbs and Euler identities of [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. Use the convention $x^0=ct$ with $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Define $\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b$, $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c$, $\Delta_{ab}=g_{ab}+u_a u_b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, and $a^b=D u^b$. Let $\sigma_{ab}$ be the shear defined in [[lem-tgr-spatial-shear-properties]]: the spatially projected symmetrized derivative of $u$, minus $\theta\Delta_{ab}/3$, with averaged symmetrization. That lemma proves $\sigma$ symmetric, spatial, trace-free, and of nonnegative squared norm. Let $\kappa,\eta,\zeta_{\rm b}\in C^\infty(O)$ be pointwise nonnegative, with SI units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$ and $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, respectively. Put
$$
X^a=\Delta^{ab}(\nabla_bT+Ta_b),\qquad q^a=-\kappa X^a,\qquad Q^a=q^a/c,
$$
so $q$ is the physical heat flux and $Q$ is its geometric stress component. Set the particle-diffusion current $V^a=0$, the bulk correction $\Pi=-\zeta_{\rm b}c\theta$, and the symmetric spatial trace-free stress $\pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab}$. Suppose $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ for $J^a=nu^a$, and suppose the symmetric stress
$$
\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab}+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab}
$$
satisfies $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=f^b$ with zero local power $u_bf^b=0$. Then for $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ the exact entropy-production identity is
$$
\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\kappa}{cT^2}X^aX_a+\frac{2\eta c}{T}\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}+\frac{\zeta_{\rm b}c}{T}\theta^2\ge0.
$$
The conclusion is a conditional identity for the stated smooth fields and closure; it asserts neither existence nor causality, stability, or empirical applicability of an evolution.

items.title: Constructed supported static heat evolution
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ with $L_i>0$, and let $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$. Let $N\in C^\infty(U,(0,\infty))$ satisfy $0<N_{\min}\le N(x)\le N_{\max}<\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$. On $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times U$, use $x^0=ct_K$ with $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, give $M$ the time orientation $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$, and use the metric
$$
g=-N(x)^2(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,
$$
where $x^i$ are measured in metres, $t_K$ in seconds, and $N$ is dimensionless. By [[def-gr-killing-field]], a Killing field is one satisfying $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, where $\mathcal L_\xi g=\frac d{dt}|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g$ for the local flow $\Phi_t$ of $\xi$. Thus $\xi$ is a future timelike Killing field, $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, and $u=N^{-1}\xi$ is the smooth future unit timelike observer congruence of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]; here this congruence means the unit timelike vector field, not a coordinate chart. Write $\nabla_x$, $\operatorname{div}_x$, $\nu$, and $dx$ for the Euclidean spatial gradient, divergence, outward unit normal, and three-dimensional Lebesgue volume on the box, and set $|\Omega|:=\int_\Omega1\,dx=L_1L_2L_3$. For scalar fields on $\Omega$, $L^2(\Omega)$ and its norm use this measure.

For $t_K>0$ use the open domain $O=(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Spatial vectors such as $q$ are extended to spacetime with zero $x^0$ component.

Fix constants $C_V,n_0,A_0,T_{\rm ref}>0$, a reference entropy $\sigma_{\rm ref}\in\mathbb R$, and a reference energy $e_0\in\mathbb R$. Their units are $C_V$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}K^{-1}}$, $n_0$ in $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $A_0$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $T_{\rm ref}$ in kelvins, $\sigma_{\rm ref}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and $e_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. Define the derived per-marker heat capacity $c_v=C_V/n_0$, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and the local mathematical material state function on $X=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ by
$$
e(v,\sigma_p)=c_vT_{\rm ref}\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma_p-\sigma_{\rm ref}}{c_v}\right)+e_0,
$$
independent of $v$. For a positive proper temperature $T$, set $\sigma_p=\sigma_{\rm ref}+c_v\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$ and $v=1/n_0$. The state definitions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] give $n=n_0$, $p=0$, $\epsilon=C_VT+n_0e_0$, and $s=n_0\sigma_{\rm ref}+C_V\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$.

Let $\vartheta_0\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ satisfy $0<m_0\le\vartheta_0\le M_0$ and admit a $C^2$ extension $\widetilde\vartheta_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ with the same bounds, period $2L_i$ in coordinate $x^i$, and evenness under $x^i\mapsto-x^i$ for each $i$. These conditions make the extension even about every face $x^i=0,L_i$. Set $T_0=\vartheta_0/N$. Define the physical heat flux, conductivity, static heat balance, and insulated-face condition by
$$
q=-\kappa_{\rm th}(\nabla_xT+T\nabla_x\log N),\qquad \kappa_{\rm th}=A_0/N,\qquad NC_V\partial_{t_K}T+\operatorname{div}_x(N^2q)=0,\qquad N^2q\cdot\nu=0\ \text{on each face},
$$
where $q$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, $\kappa_{\rm th}$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal to a face. In the entropy identity use zero particle diffusion and zero shear and bulk viscosity, $V=0$ and $\eta=\zeta_{\rm b}=0$, so $\Pi=0$ and $\pi^{ab}=0$. The thermal diffusivity $A_0/C_V$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. There is a unique solution $T\in C([0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)\cap C^{2,1}((0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)$, where $C^{2,1}$ means two continuous spatial derivatives and one continuous time derivative up to the box faces, satisfying the heat balance, the face condition, and the initial condition $T(0,x)=T_0(x)=\vartheta_0(x)/N(x)$. It is given by
$$\vartheta(t_K,x):=N(x)T(t_K,x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma\!\left(x-y,\frac{A_0}{C_V}t_K\right)\widetilde\vartheta_0(y)\,dy\quad(t_K>0),\qquad \vartheta(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x),\qquad \Gamma(z,t)=(4\pi t)^{-3/2}e^{-|z|^2/(4t)},\quad z\in\mathbb R^3,\ t>0.$$
Thus $T=\vartheta/N$. It satisfies $C_V\partial_{t_K}\vartheta=A_0\Delta_x\vartheta$, $\partial_\nu\vartheta=0$ on each face, and $m_0\le\vartheta\le M_0$.

For this solution set $Q^0=0$, $Q^i=q^i/c$, $J=n_0u$, and
$$
\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b,\qquad f^b:=\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}.
$$
Here $Q=q/c$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, $\mathsf T$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, and $f$ has units $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. Then $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $u_bf^b=0$: $f$ is an explicitly defined external support that supplies no local power. The entropy current $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}m^{-3}}$ and total entropy $\mathcal S(t_K)=\int_\Omega s(t_K,x)\,dx$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, with
$$
\frac{d\mathcal S}{dt_K}=A_0\int_\Omega\frac{|\nabla_x\vartheta|^2}{\vartheta^2}\,dx\ge0.
$$
The lapse-weighted energy $\mathcal E_K(t_K)=\int_\Omega N\epsilon\,dx$ is constant in $\mathrm{J}$. If $\overline\vartheta=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega\vartheta_0\,dx$ and $C_\Omega=\frac32(\max_iL_i)^2$, then
$$
\left\|\vartheta(t_K,\cdot)-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0t_K}{C_VC_\Omega}\right)\left\|\vartheta_0-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.
$$
Thus $T$ converges in $L^2(\Omega)$ to $T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta/N$. Since $N T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta>0$, the inverse-temperature vector $\beta=u/(k_BT_{\rm eq})$, for $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, is Killing by [[lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization]]. This is a mathematical solution of the specified fixed-background, supported first-order heat model; it asserts no Einstein equation, general dissipative-fluid initial-value theorem, or finite propagation speed.

items.title: Static cosine relaxation
items.statement:
Use the fixed-background box, lapse $N$, constants and material model of [[thm-tgr-supported-static-heat-evolution]]. Let $\overline\vartheta>0$ and $\delta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|\delta|<\overline\vartheta$, and take the initial redshifted temperature
$$
\vartheta_0(x)=\overline\vartheta+\delta\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi x^1}{L_1}\right),\qquad x\in\overline\Omega.
$$
It has a positive even-reflected periodic extension, and the corresponding exact solution and proper-temperature field are
$$
\vartheta(t_K,x)=\overline\vartheta+\delta\exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0\pi^2t_K}{C_VL_1^2}\right)\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi x^1}{L_1}\right),\qquad T(t_K,x)=\frac{\vartheta(t_K,x)}{N(x)}.
$$
The proper temperature tends to $\overline\vartheta/N(x)$, which varies spatially when the lapse is nonconstant, while the redshifted temperature $NT$ tends to the constant $\overline\vartheta$.

items.title: Selected stationary thermal equilibrium
items.physical_scope: One selected comoving bath on a connected smooth Lorentzian domain with a future timelike Killing field and a Killing inverse-temperature vector; no universal equilibrium existence, KMS state, or empirical thermometer law.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
On a nonempty connected open set $O$ in the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], select one smooth future timelike Killing field $\xi$ and one smooth scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ in kelvins. Its dimensionless lapse and selected observer congruence are

$$N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0,\qquad u:=\xi/N_\xi.$$

Thus $g(u,u)=-1$ and the physical four-velocity is $cu$ in the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$. A reference normalization of $\xi$ is part of the selected model. The local temperature $T$ is assigned to this comoving observer congruence; it is not a coordinate temperature or a value assigned to every observer.

Adopt the inverse-temperature vector

$$\beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},$$

where $k_B>0$ is Boltzmann's constant in joules per kelvin, and assume that this field is Killing on $O$. In this item, a selected stationary thermal equilibrium means precisely this adopted bath, observer congruence, positive proper-temperature field, and Killing condition on $\beta$. The field $N_\xi T$ is not assumed constant here; its constancy is the conclusion of [[pthm-tgr-tolman-ehrenfest]].

This is a model assumption, not a statement that every stationary geometry admits a thermal state or that every material realizes this bath. It asserts no complete Killing flow, KMS state, trace-class stress exponential, collision or thermalization law, Hawking or Unruh temperature, or empirical thermometer reading.

items.physical_scope: Conditional redshift law for the local proper temperature of one selected connected stationary bath; no claim that arbitrary stationary flows or geometries are in equilibrium.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Use the connected stationary thermal carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on $O$. Let $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$, $u=\xi/N_\xi$, and $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ as there, and assume the postulated Killing condition on $\beta$. Then a positive constant $T_K$ exists such that

$N_\xi(x)T(x)=T_K\quad\text{and}\quad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K}\qquad(x\in O).$

In the same convention, $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, the observer acceleration satisfies $a=\nabla\log N_\xi$, the expansion and shear vanish, and

$\nabla\log T=-a.$

For any chosen reference event $x_{\rm ref}\in O$, $T_K=N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})T(x_{\rm ref})$. If the reference normalization has $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, then $T_K$ is the local temperature at that event. Rescaling $\xi$ by a constant $b>0$ rescales $N_\xi$ and $T_K$ by $b$ while leaving the local scalar $T$ unchanged. The result is a conditional deduction from the selected physical postulate and the stated mathematical supplier; it is not a thermometer law for arbitrary observers or a KMS-existence theorem.

items.title: Specified equilibrium particle exchange
items.physical_scope: A selected fixed-composition local material branch with either a finite independent-cell exchange model or a massive classical charged Liouville ansatz; charged conclusions require the stated global potential symmetry and reference.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
For a selected fixed-composition material branch, adopt the local state function and energy convention of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] and [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. In that state map, $T>0$ is the derivative of the supplied energy per marker with respect to entropy per marker, and the chemical potential is $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$ in joules per marker. Rest energy stays in the energy convention used for $\mu$ and for any particle generator; a rest-energy subtraction made in a different convention must be tracked explicitly.

For particle exchange, select and declare one of these physical model protocols:

- **Finite-cell exchange.** Supply $r\ge1$ finitely many independent cells with differentiable concave entropy functions $S_i(E_i,n_i)$, positive lapse values $N_i$, a fixed common charge $q$, and potential values $\Phi_i$ in a stated common reference. The adopted exchange conserves $\sum_i(N_iE_i+q\Phi_i n_i)$ and $\sum_i n_i$. The local $T_i$ and $\mu_i$ for this protocol are those defined by the entropy derivatives in [[thm-tgr-finite-entropy-exchange-equilibrium]]. Their identification with another material state map is an additional model identification, not inferred here.

- **Charged kinetic exchange.** On the selected stationary domain, supply a species of rest mass $m>0$, charge $q$, smooth local fields $T>0$ and $\mu$, a global smooth real potential $A$ with $F=dA$, and a smooth compensator $\Lambda_\xi$ satisfying $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Use the future massive shell, charged transport, and dimensionless exponential ansatz exactly as defined in [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]]. Adopt whole-shell stationarity $\mathcal L_{F,q}f=0$ as the exchange criterion. This is a model assumption on every future mass-shell momentum, not an assertion that collisions drive a gas to this ansatz.

The two protocols are separate model choices. This postulate does not derive either protocol from gravity, assert a global electrostatic potential when no single-valued symmetry compensator exists, establish a Gibbs state or material realization, or identify finite entropy variables with kinetic fields without an explicit model assumption.

items.title: Conditional Tolman–Klein relation
items.physical_scope: Conditional redshift relation in either the stated connected charged kinetic model or a finite independent-cell entropy-exchange model; no universal chemical law, chemical reaction, hydrostatic equation of state, or non-exact global potential.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Use the selected stationary carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] and the declared exchange protocol of [[post-tgr-equilibrium-particle-exchange]]. The following two conclusions are conditional on their respective model inputs.

**Charged kinetic protocol.** Let $O$ be connected, let $\xi$ be the selected future timelike Killing field, and set $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$. For a species with $m>0$ and charge $q$, assume a global smooth potential symmetry $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$ and define $\Phi_\xi=-c(\iota_\xi A-\Lambda_\xi)$ in volts. Suppose the smooth fields $T>0$ and $\mu$ define $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ and $\zeta=\mu/(k_BT)$, and the ansatz $f=\exp(\zeta+g(\beta,P))$ is stationary under the charged transport of [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]] at every future massive-shell momentum. Then there are constants $T_K>0$ and $\mu_K$ such that

$N_\xi T=T_K,\qquad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K},\qquad N_\xi\mu+q\Phi_\xi=\mu_K.$

Here $\mu$ and $\mu_K$ use the same full-energy convention as the conserved generator, including rest energy when that generator includes it. The gauge-compensated potential reference may be shifted by $\Phi_\xi\mapsto\Phi_\xi+C$ only with $\mu_K\mapsto\mu_K+qC$.

**Finite-cell exchange protocol.** For $r\ge1$ finitely many independent cells with $C^1$ concave entropies $S_i(E_i,n_i)$, positive lapse values $N_i$, common charge $q$, and the supplied potential values $\Phi_i$, define $1/T_i=\partial_{E_i}S_i>0$ and $\mu_i/T_i=-\partial_{n_i}S_i$ at a supplied feasible interior point. If independent variations preserving $\sum_i(N_iE_i+q\Phi_i n_i)$ and $\sum_i n_i$ leave the total entropy stationary, then constants $T_K>0,\mu_K$ exist with

$N_iT_i=T_K,\qquad N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K\quad(1\le i\le r).$

That stationary point is a global entropy maximum on the feasible set when the cell entropies are concave, and it is unique if they are strictly concave. No existence or boundary attainment is asserted. In either branch, $q=0$ gives the neutral relation $N\mu=\mu_K$ (or $N_i\mu_i=\mu_K$). The finite-cell symbols are not identified with the kinetic fields unless the model explicitly supplies that identification.

items.title: Defined classical Jüttner kinetic preparation
items.physical_scope: One massive classical species with prescribed positive density and temperature and a chosen observer congruence; an exactly normalized model preparation, not an assertion of collisional equilibration, material validity, or quantum statistics.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$. On an open region $O\subseteq M$, take a smooth observer congruence $u$ whose value at each event is a future unit timelike observer in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]] and [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. The congruence is a field of observer directions, not an adapted coordinate chart or a tetrad. Let $n:O\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth proper number density in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ a smooth proper-temperature scalar in kelvins. These fields are prescribed model data.

Choose one species with rest mass $m>0$ in kilograms, put $M_*:=mc^2>0$ in joules, choose $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and choose a reference action $h_{\rm ref}>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. At an event $x\in O$, the future massive shell $\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$ and its tetrad-independent measure $d\mu_{M_*}$ are those of [[def-tgr-future-mass-shell-measure]]. For each $P\in\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}$, define the positive observer-measured energy

$$E_u(P):=-g_x(P,u_x)>0,\qquad \alpha(x):=\frac{1}{k_BT(x)}.$$

In any future orthonormal tetrad whose time axis is $u_x$, write the spatial energy-momentum coordinates as $\mathbf p\in\mathbb R^3$, so $E_u(P)=\sqrt{M_*^2+|\mathbf p|^2}$ and $d^3\mathbf p=E_u(P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P)$. The spatial mechanical momentum is $\mathbf p/c$; $\mathbf p$ itself is the spatial part of the energy four-vector $P$.

Define

$$Z_{M_*}(\alpha):=\frac{4\pi M_*^2}{\alpha}K_2(\alpha M_*),\qquad K_j(z):=\int_0^\infty e^{-z\cosh t}\cosh(jt)\,dt\quad(j=1,2).$$

and the observer-rest momentum probability law

$$d\nu_{u,x}(\mathbf p):=Z_{M_*}(\alpha(x))^{-1}e^{-\alpha(x)E_u(P)}\,d^3\mathbf p.$$

Set

$$\beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},\qquad \zeta:=\log\!\left(\frac{n h_{\rm ref}^3c^3}{Z_{M_*}(\alpha)}\right),\qquad f(x,P):=e^{\zeta(x)+g_x(\beta(x),P)}.$$

Finally define the model number current and stress-energy tensor by the convergent shell moments

$$J^a(x):=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^a f(x,P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P),\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}(x):=(h_{\rm ref}^3c^3)^{-1}\int_{\mathcal H^+_{M_*,x}}P^aP^b f(x,P)\,d\mu_{M_*}(P).$$

The mathematical suppliers [[thm-tgr-juttner-partition-and-moments]] and [[def-probability-measure]] give $0<Z_{M_*}<\infty$, show that $\nu_{u,x}$ has total mass one, and evaluate the current and stress moments:

$$J^a=nu^a,\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)u^au^b+pg^{ab},\qquad \varepsilon=n\left(M_*\frac{K_1(\alpha M_*)}{K_2(\alpha M_*)}+\frac3\alpha\right),\quad p=\frac n\alpha=nk_BT.$$

Here $\varepsilon$ and $p$ are the exact moments of this one-species kinetic model. They are not automatically identified with an independently adopted material state function or stress tensor. The suppliers use the stated countable-choice strength $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ only; this definition adds no arbitrary-index choice principle. The scale $h_{\rm ref}$ is a declared phase-space unit convention, not Planck's constant or a measured parameter.

This is an exact classical model definition. It does not claim that an actual material realizes this distribution, that collisions drive it to equilibrium, that the full field $f$ solves a transport equation, or that any quantum-statistical or empirical law follows.

items.title: Schwarzschild supported thermal bath
items.physical_scope: Static test bath on the Schwarzschild exterior r>r_s, with asymptotic Killing-time normalization, exact lapse and acceleration, and a bounded weak-field expansion; no horizon or quantum-temperature claim.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
Let $m_s>0$ be a source mass in kilograms, distinct from any kinetic particle mass, let $G_N>0$ be Newton's constant in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and let $c>0$ be the speed of light in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Set

$r_s:=\frac{2G_Nm_s}{c^2},\qquad f(r):=1-\frac{r_s}{r},\qquad r>r_s.$

In physical length coordinates $x^0=ct$, use the Schwarzschild exterior metric

$ds^2=-f(r)(dx^0)^2+f(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2(d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2),$

and select $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$ with the asymptotic normalization $N_\xi\to1$ as $r\to\infty$. The time orientation is chosen so $\xi$ is future-directed. Under the selected stationary-bath assumption, the local proper temperature satisfies

$T(r)=\frac{T_\infty}{\sqrt{1-r_s/r}},\qquad T_\infty:=T_K>0.$

The static observer congruence has outward covariant acceleration component $a_r=r_s/(2r^2f)$, contravariant component $a^r=r_s/(2r^2)$, and physical proper-acceleration magnitude

$c^2\sqrt{g_{ab}a^aa^b}=\frac{G_Nm_s}{r^2\sqrt{f(r)}}.$

For a fixed $z_0\in(0,1)$ and $0<r_s/r\le z_0$, the weak-field expansion has the explicit bound

$\left|\frac{T(r)}{T_\infty}-1-\frac{G_Nm_s}{c^2r}\right|\le\frac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}\left(\frac{r_s}{r}\right)^2.$

This is a conditional calculation in the specified exterior model. At $r=r_s$, the chosen Killing field is null and the normalized stationary observers do not exist. The limiting divergence as $r\downarrow r_s$ is not a constructed horizon state, a Hawking temperature, or a claim that every observer measures an infinite temperature.

items.title: Rindler and rigid rotating bath domains
items.physical_scope: Rindler right wedge and rigidly rotating Minkowski domain inside its light cylinder; arbitrary positive classical reference temperature; differential rotation and one-mode trace restrictions kept distinct.
items.design_state: Authored draft for the reserved selected stationary thermal-equilibrium claim; exact hypotheses and source dispositions are recorded in batch-66 notes.
items.statement:
**Rindler right wedge.** Let $a_0>0$ be an acceleration in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, use coordinates $(x^0,x,y,z)$ with $x^0=ct$, and take the open domain $x>0$ with metric

$ds^2=-\left(\frac{a_0x}{c^2}\right)^2(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2.$

The selected Killing field $\xi_R=\partial_{x^0}$ has lapse $N_R=a_0x/c^2$ and observer acceleration $a_x=1/x$, so the physical proper-acceleration magnitude is $c^2/x$. The selected stationary-bath model gives

$T_R(x)=\frac{T_Kc^2}{a_0x}.$

At the reference point $x_{\rm ref}=c^2/a_0$, $N_R=1$ and $T_R=T_K$. Any $T_K>0$ is allowed by this classical geometric model; the metric and temperature relation do not select the Unruh value.

**Rigid rotation in Minkowski spacetime.** In cylindrical coordinates let

$ds^2=-(dx^0)^2+dr^2+r^2d\phi^2+dz^2,\qquad \xi_\Omega=\partial_{x^0}+\frac{\Omega}{c}\partial_\phi,$

where $\Omega$ is a constant angular velocity in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For $\Omega\ne0$, use the annular domain $0<r<c/|\Omega|$; for $\Omega=0$, $\xi_\Omega=\partial_{x^0}$ is timelike throughout Minkowski space. On the rotating domain,

$N_\Omega=\sqrt{1-\frac{\Omega^2r^2}{c^2}},\qquad T_\Omega(r)=\frac{T_K}{N_\Omega}.$

The radial acceleration component is $a_r=-\Omega^2r/[c^2(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)]$, directed inward, with physical magnitude $\gamma^2\Omega^2r$, where $\gamma=(1-\Omega^2r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. At the light cylinder $r=c/|\Omega|$, $\xi_\Omega$ becomes null and the normalized stationary observer does not exist. A differential-rotation field $\partial_{x^0}+[\Omega(r)/c]\partial_\phi$ is not Killing when $\Omega'(r)\ne0$: its metric Lie derivative has $(\mathcal L_\xi g)_{r\phi}=r^2\Omega'(r)/c$.

**One-mode trace check.** If an additional model specifies a single bosonic mode with lab Hamiltonian $H=\epsilon\mathcal N$ and angular momentum $J=\hbar j\mathcal N$, then its rotating generator is $H-\Omega J$. Its Gibbs trace is finite exactly when $\epsilon-\hbar j\Omega>0$. This is the separate one-mode spectral condition of [[prop-tgr-rotating-mode-gibbs-obstruction]]; it does not prove a continuum-field trace obstruction or describe every rotating equilibrium state.

items.title: Actually constructed Gibbs/KMS preparation
items.physical_scope: An adopted canonical state assignment for finitely many independent finite-dimensional cells in one selected stationary bath, conditional on the exact global stationarity and potential hypotheses of the finite-cell theorem; no generic curved-spacetime or infinite-volume KMS state, thermalization dynamics, or empirical realization.
items.design_state: Authored draft following the reserved TGR-PET02 claim; exact supplier interfaces, assumptions, and source dispositions are recorded in batch-67 notes.
items.statement:
Adopt the selected stationary bath of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on its connected smooth Lorentzian domain. A finite-cell preparation in this item means exactly the setup of [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]]: finitely many $r\ge1$ noninteracting cells with finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_i$, Hermitian proper Hamiltonians $H_i$ in joules, and dimensionless Hermitian number matrices $Q_i$ with nonnegative integer eigenvalues and $[H_i,Q_i]=0$. Their tensor product is $\mathcal H=\bigotimes_{i=1}^r\mathcal H_i$; each cell operator acts as the identity on the other factors.

Choose a placement map $p:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to O$ assigning each cell to a spacetime event, and write $p_i:=p(i)$. Let $N_\xi(x):=\sqrt{-g_x(\xi_x,\xi_x)}$ be the dimensionless lapse field, and let $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ and $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ be the smooth proper-temperature and chemical-potential fields in the stationarity hypotheses. Evaluate them at the assigned event:
$$N_i:=N_\xi(p_i),\qquad T_i:=T(p_i),\qquad \mu_i:=\mu(p_i).$$
Assume the same connected stationary geometry, selected future timelike Killing field $\xi$, common charge $q$ in coulombs, global smooth potential $A$, global compensator $\Lambda_\xi$ satisfying $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$, and charged whole-future-mass-shell stationarity hypotheses as in that theorem; no patchwise potential is substituted. Using the length-coordinate convention and $c>0$ in metres per second from [[def-tgr-framework-units]], define the global gauge-compensated potential scalar $\Phi_\xi:O\to\mathbb R$ by $\Phi_\xi(x):=-c(\iota_\xi A-\Lambda_\xi)(x)$ in volts, and set $\Phi_i:=\Phi_\xi(p_i)$. The common parameters satisfy $N_iT_i=T_K>0$ and $N_i\mu_i+q\Phi_i=\mu_K$. The theorem's geometric stationarity argument is conditional on the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); no stronger choice axiom is used here.

Put $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$ in joules$^{-1}$, $\beta_i=N_i\beta_K=(k_BT_i)^{-1}$, $H_K=\sum_i(N_iH_i+q\Phi_iQ_i)$, $Q=\sum_iQ_i$, and $G_K=H_K-\mu_KQ=\sum_iN_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i)$. The finite-cell theorem constructs

$$Z_i=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H_i}e^{-\beta_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i)},\qquad Z=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H}e^{-\beta_KG_K}=\prod_i Z_i,$$

$$\rho_i=Z_i^{-1}e^{-\beta_i(H_i-\mu_iQ_i)},\qquad \rho=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta_KG_K}=\bigotimes_i\rho_i.$$

For $X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$, write $\omega_\rho(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X)$ and define the Killing-time grand-generator dynamics, with $t_K$ in seconds, by

$$\alpha^G_{t_K}(X)=e^{it_KG_K/\hbar}Xe^{-it_KG_K/\hbar},\qquad \hbar>0\text{ in joule-seconds}.$$

The referenced finite-dimensional theorem proves that $\rho$ is a normalized positive state and is $\beta_K$-KMS for $\alpha^G$; the physical-time strip has width $\hbar\beta_K$ seconds under [[def-qsm-kms-state]]. Its restriction to observables commuting with $Q$ is also KMS for the physical $H_K$ dynamics. This postulate adopts that actually constructed finite state as the state assignment for this specified model. It asserts no state on an infinite-volume algebra, no trace-class stress exponential in generic curved quantum field theory, no approach to equilibrium, and no observed preparation or material realization.
