items.title: Conditional local KMS clock temperature
items.physical_scope: Orbitwise KMS-time rescaling for each actually constructed finite cell in the selected stationary model; no spatially varying global time rescaling, generic curved-spacetime KMS existence, equilibration law, or empirical temperature measurement.
items.design_state: Authored draft following the reserved TGR-PET02 claim; exact supplier interfaces, assumptions, and source dispositions are recorded in batch-67 notes.
items.statement:
Fix one cell $i$ of the finite preparation in [[post-tgr-selected-gibbs-kms-preparation]], at its assigned event $p_i\in O$, with $N_i=N_\xi(p_i)$, $T_i=T(p_i)$, and $\mu_i=\mu(p_i)$. Set $\beta_K:=(k_BT_K)^{-1}>0$ in joules$^{-1}$. Let $\mathcal A_i=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_i)$, let $G_i:=H_i-\mu_iQ_i$ be its proper grand generator in joules, let $G_{K,i}:=N_iG_i$ be its Killing-time grand generator, and let $\omega_i(X):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_iX)$. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$, with $c>0$ the speed of light in metres per second and the reference-normalized $\xi$ dimensionless in these coordinates. Choose an open interval $I_{K,i}\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$ on which the integral curve through $p_i$ remains in $O$. Define the unique smooth curve $\gamma_i:I_{K,i}\to O$ by
$$\gamma_i(0)=p_i,\qquad \frac{d\gamma_i}{dt_K}(t_K)=c\,\xi_{\gamma_i(t_K)},$$
where $t_K$ is physical Killing time in seconds; the equation states its parameterization by the reference-normalized Killing field. This curve is future-directed timelike. The stationary normalization used in [[thm-tgr-kms-orbit-time-rescaling]] gives $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, so $N_\xi(\gamma_i(t_K))=N_i$ throughout this interval. Its proper-time parametrization is
$$\Gamma_i:N_iI_{K,i}\to O,\qquad \Gamma_i(\tau):=\gamma_i(\tau/N_i),$$
which satisfies $g(d\Gamma_i/d\tau,d\Gamma_i/d\tau)=-c^2$. Thus $\tau$ is proper time in seconds and $\tau=N_it_K$ on the geometric orbit. No completeness of $\xi$ is assumed: the geometric curve is defined on its flow interval, while the finite-matrix dynamics below are defined for all real parameters by their generators and use the same constant rescaling.

Define

$$\alpha^{K,i}_{t_K}(X):=e^{it_KG_{K,i}/\hbar}Xe^{-it_KG_{K,i}/\hbar},\qquad \alpha^{\mathrm{loc},i}_{\tau}(X):=e^{i\tau G_i/\hbar}Xe^{-i\tau G_i/\hbar},$$

where both $t_K$ and $\tau$ are measured in seconds, and $N_i>0$ is dimensionless. Write $\mathcal A_i^0:=\{X\in\mathcal A_i:[X,Q_i]=0\}$ for the neutral observable algebra. Then $\omega_i$ is $\beta_K$-KMS for $\alpha^{K,i}$ and is $\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}$-KMS for $\alpha^{\mathrm{loc},i}$, where

$$\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}=N_i\beta_K=\frac{1}{k_BT_i},\qquad \hbar\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}\text{ is the strip width in seconds}.$$

On $\mathcal A_i^0$, the same proper-time automorphism is generated by the physical Hamiltonian $H_i$, because its chemical-potential term commutes with every observable in that subalgebra. Thus the local temperature is $T_i=T_K/N_i$ for this constructed state and selected orbit. The conclusion is only orbitwise; it does not make a position-dependent lapse into one global time-rescaled dynamics.

items.title: Conditional finite stationary response
items.physical_scope: Exact finite-time and spectral predictions for neutral bounded observables and controls in one actually constructed independent finite cell; no observation, infinite-time relaxation, dc transport coefficient, or response law for arbitrary interacting reduced states.
items.design_state: Authored draft following the reserved TGR-PET02 claim; exact supplier interfaces, assumptions, and source dispositions are recorded in batch-67 notes.
items.statement:
Fix one cell $i$ of the preparation in [[post-tgr-selected-gibbs-kms-preparation]] at its assigned event $p_i\in O$, with $N_i=N_\xi(p_i)$, $T_i=T(p_i)$, and $\mu_i=\mu(p_i)$. Let $H_i=H_i^*$ be its proper Hamiltonian in joules, $Q_i$ its dimensionless number matrix, $G_i:=H_i-\mu_iQ_i$, and $\sigma:=\rho_i$ its constructed density. Put $\beta_K:=(k_BT_K)^{-1}>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}:=N_i\beta_K=(k_BT_i)^{-1}$. Take Hermitian matrices $A,B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H_i)$ with $[A,Q_i]=[B,Q_i]=0$. Let $h:[0,S]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous for $S>0$ seconds, let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless, and require $h(\tau)B$ to have units of joules. Define the local and Killing-time dynamics by

$$\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(C)=e^{iG_i\tau/\hbar}Ce^{-iG_i\tau/\hbar},\qquad \alpha^K_t(C)=e^{iN_iG_it/\hbar}Ce^{-iN_iG_it/\hbar}.$$

Let $H_{K,i}:=N_iH_i+q\Phi_iQ_i$ be the cell's physical Killing-energy operator, where $q$ is the common charge in coulombs and $\Phi_i=\Phi_\xi(p_i)$ is in volts as in the preparation. Let $U_{\mathrm{loc}}:[0,S]\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_i)$ and $U_K:[0,S/N_i]\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_i)$ be the unique solutions of
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{d\tau}U_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=\bigl(H_i-\epsilon h(\tau)B\bigr)U_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau),\qquad U_{\mathrm{loc}}(0)=I_{\mathcal H_i},$$
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}U_K(t)=\bigl(H_{K,i}-\epsilon N_i h(N_it)B\bigr)U_K(t),\qquad U_K(0)=I_{\mathcal H_i}.$$
They are unitary propagators. Define the model expectations by
$$E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau):=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma U_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)^*A U_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)\right),\qquad E_K(t):=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma U_K(t)^*A U_K(t)\right).$$
Because $A$ and $B$ commute with $Q_i$, the second expectation is unchanged if $H_{K,i}$ is replaced by $N_iH_i$; that is the neutral-sector version of the Killing control. The exact finite-cell predictions are

$$E_K(t)=E_{\mathrm{loc}}(N_it)\qquad(0\le t\le S/N_i),$$

and

$$E_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_\tau(A))+\epsilon\int_0^\tau h(s)R_{\mathrm{loc}}(\tau-s)\,ds+r(\tau),$$

where

$$R_{\mathrm{loc}}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_S=\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_0^S|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds,\qquad |r(\tau)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_S)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_S}}2.$$

Here $C_S$ is dimensionless and $R_{\mathrm{loc}}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm{J\,s})$. For the equilibrium correlations $C_{\mathrm{loc}}(u)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha^{\mathrm{loc}}_u(A)A)$ and $C_K(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha^K_t(A)A)$, let $S_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and $S_K$ be their Fourier measures in the distributional convention $S(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{i\omega t}C(t)\,dt$, where $\omega$ is in seconds$^{-1}$. Set $D_{N_i}(\omega)=N_i\omega$. Then

$$S_K=(D_{N_i})_*S_{\mathrm{loc}},\qquad S_K(\omega)=N_i^{-1}S_{\mathrm{loc}}(\omega/N_i),$$

the detailed-balance factor is unchanged because $\beta_K\hbar(N_i\omega)=\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}\hbar\omega$, and any zero-frequency atom remains at zero and is kept separate from the $\coth$ formula. Finally, for the separately re-prepared finite Gibbs family $\sigma_\lambda\propto e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}(G_i-\lambda B)}$, where $\lambda B$ has units of joules,

$$\left.\frac{d}{d\lambda}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\lambda B)\right|_{\lambda=0}=\beta_{\mathrm{loc},i}\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)\ge0,$$

with $\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathrm{KM},\sigma}(B,B)=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma^{1-u}\delta B\,\sigma^u\delta B)\,du$ and $\delta B=B-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma B)I$. It equals the ordinary variance when $[B,G_i]=0$; otherwise no such reduction is asserted. These are conditional model predictions, not reported observations or a theorem of relaxation.

items.title: Independent redshifted finite cells
items.physical_scope: An exact two-cell finite-dimensional Gibbs/KMS construction at two points of a Rindler stationary domain, conditional on the adopted bath and the specified neutral whole-shell stationarity input; no measured realization or interacting/infinite-volume state.
items.design_state: Authored draft following the reserved TGR-PET02 claim; exact supplier interfaces, assumptions, and source dispositions are recorded in batch-67 notes.
items.statement:
Let $L>0$ be a length in metres and $T_K>0$ a reference temperature in kelvins. On the connected open Rindler domain $O=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(0,\infty)_x\times\mathbb R_y\times\mathbb R_z$, use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and the metric

$$ds^2=-\left(\frac{x}{L}\right)^2(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2.$$

Choose the future direction of increasing $x^0$ and the Killing field $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$. The selected lapse is $N(x)=x/L$. Define $\beta_K:=(k_BT_K)^{-1}>0$ in joules$^{-1}$ and adopt the stationary-bath temperature field $T(x)=T_KL/x$, so the inverse-temperature vector is $\beta=\beta_K\xi=\xi/(k_BT_K)$. For the global-stationarity input of [[thm-tgr-finite-cell-gibbs-factorization]], use an auxiliary neutral species with rest mass $m>0$, charge $q=0$, chemical potential $\mu=0$, global potential $A=0$, and compensator $\Lambda_\xi=0$. This auxiliary kinetic sector is a supplier hypothesis for the finite-cell construction; it is not identified with the two quantum cells.

Set $x_1:=L$, $x_2:=2L$ and place the cells at $p_i:=(x^0=0,x=x_i,y=0,z=0)\in O$, as in the placement map of [[post-tgr-selected-gibbs-kms-preparation]]. For $t_K,\tau\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\gamma_i(t_K):=(ct_K,x_i,0,0),\qquad \Gamma_i(\tau):=(c\tau/N_i,x_i,0,0).$$
Here $t_K$ is the Killing-flow parameter in seconds and $\tau$ is proper time in seconds. Each $\gamma_i$ is a smooth future-directed timelike integral curve of $c\xi$ through $p_i$; since $N_i=x_i/L$ is constant on it, $\Gamma_i(\tau)=\gamma_i(\tau/N_i)$ and $g(d\Gamma_i/d\tau,d\Gamma_i/d\tau)=-c^2$. Thus $\tau=N_it_K$ is the proper-time relation on the two worldlines. For each $i\in\{1,2\}$ take $\mathcal H_i=\mathbb C^2$ with an orthonormal basis $\{|0_i\rangle,|1_i\rangle\}$, let $Q_i=0$, and set

$$H_i=\Delta_i|1_i\rangle\langle1_i|,\qquad \Delta_i>0\text{ joules}.$$

Set $q=0$ for the cells and use $\mu_i=0$. Then $N_1=1$, $N_2=2$, $T_1=T_K$, and $T_2=T_K/2$. With $\beta_i=N_i\beta_K=(k_BT_i)^{-1}$, the exact local partition functions and states are

$$Z_i=1+e^{-\beta_i\Delta_i},\qquad \rho_i=\frac{|0_i\rangle\langle0_i|+e^{-\beta_i\Delta_i}|1_i\rangle\langle1_i|}{Z_i}.$$

The total state and Killing-time generator are

$$\rho=\rho_1\otimes\rho_2=\frac{e^{-\beta_K(H_1+2H_2)}}{Z_1Z_2},\qquad G_K=H_1+2H_2.$$

This is a positive normalized finite-dimensional state. It is $\beta_K$-KMS for the Killing-time dynamics and its $i$th cell state is $\beta_i$-KMS for the local proper-time dynamics of [[pthm-tgr-local-kms-clock-temperature]]. The equality $N_iT_i=T_K$ is exact within this constructed model; no observation, material-realization claim, infinite-volume limit, or interaction between cells is asserted.

row.title: Supported static heat model

items.title: Supported static heat model
items.statement:
Choose positive lengths $L_1,L_2,L_3$, the rectangular box $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$, and an open neighborhood $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ of $\overline\Omega$. Let $N\in C^\infty(U,(0,\infty))$ satisfy $0<N_{\min}\leq N(x)\leq N_{\max}<\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$. On $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times U$, use $x^0=ct_K$, where $c>0$ is in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and the fixed metric

$$g=-N(x)^2(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2.$$

The coordinates $x^i$ and lengths $L_i$ are measured in metres, $t_K$ in seconds, and the lapse $N$ is dimensionless. The metric is independent of $x^0$ and has no time-space cross terms; this is the static background in this model. Give $M$ time orientation $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$. Then $\xi$ is a future timelike Killing field, $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, and $u=N^{-1}\xi$ is the smooth future unit timelike observer congruence in the conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Here a frame means this vector field and its pointwise rest spaces, not a coordinate chart or tetrad. The material is held at rest in this congruence; no flow evolution is included. The scalar $T>0$ is proper temperature in kelvins, and $\vartheta:=NT$ is the Killing-normalized (redshifted) temperature of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]; this definition alone does not assert that $\vartheta$ is constant.

Adopt the fixed-composition material branch of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] with constants $C_V,n_0,T_{\rm ref}>0$, $\sigma_{\rm ref}\in\mathbb R$, and $e_0\in\mathbb R$. The units are $C_V$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}K^{-1}}$, $n_0$ in $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $T_{\rm ref}$ in kelvins, $\sigma_{\rm ref}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and $e_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. Put $c_v=C_V/n_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$ and choose the state function on $X=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ to be

$$e(v,\sigma_p)=c_vT_{\rm ref}\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma_p-\sigma_{\rm ref}}{c_v}\right)+e_0,$$

independent of the rest volume per marker $v$. For a given positive $T$, set $v=1/n_0$ and $\sigma_p=\sigma_{\rm ref}+c_v\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$. For this branch define $n=v^{-1}$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\epsilon=ne$, $T=\partial_{\sigma_p}e$, and $p=-\partial_ve$, using the units of [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and the adopted material convention of [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]]. These maps give $n=n_0$, $p=0$, $\epsilon=C_VT+n_0e_0$, and $s=n_0\sigma_{\rm ref}+C_V\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$. These assignments describe the selected model only; they do not assert a measured equation of state.

Take an admissible initial redshifted-temperature profile $\vartheta_0\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ with constants $0<m_0\leq M_0<\infty$ such that $m_0\leq\vartheta_0\leq M_0$, and require a $C^2$ extension $\widetilde\vartheta_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ with the same bounds, period $2L_i$ in each coordinate $x^i$, and evenness under each reflection $x^i\mapsto-x^i$. Its even periodic extension makes the normal derivative vanish at both faces in each coordinate once evolved smoothly. The initial proper temperature is $T(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x)/N(x)$.

On $O=(0,\infty)\times\Omega$, identified with the subset of $M$ by $x^0=ct_K$, the admissible temperature field is a positive map $T:[0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega\to(0,\infty)$ continuous with initial trace $T(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x)/N(x)$ and $C^\infty$ on $O$. For every $0<a<b<\infty$, it extends smoothly in all space-time variables to a neighborhood of $[a,b]\times\overline\Omega$; no smoothness across $t_K=0$ is required. The state map on $O$ is

$$v=1/n_0,\qquad \sigma_p=\sigma_{\rm ref}+c_v\log(T/T_{\rm ref}).$$

With the definition $\mu=e+pv-T\sigma_p$ in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]], this branch has $\mu/T=c_v+e_0/T-\sigma_p$ and $\nabla_a(\mu/T)=-(e_0/T^2+c_v/T)\nabla_aT$. The state map and these derived fields are smooth on $O$.

For [[post-tgr-first-order-dissipation]], declare the regime $\mathcal R$ as follows. Its tuples record $(v,\sigma_p,u,T,\mu/T)$ and the first covariant derivatives $\nabla u$, $\nabla T$, and $\nabla(\mu/T)$ generated by first derivatives of the displayed state maps and of a future unit timelike field $u$; thus $u_b\nabla_a u^b=0$. Require $1/(2n_0)<v<3/(2n_0)$, with arbitrary $\sigma_p\in\mathbb R$ and no bounds on the derivatives. This is a nonempty open regime in the relative topology of the state/first-jet space after the normalization and state-map constraints are imposed. It contains the fixed-density heat branch pointwise because $v=1/n_0$, $T>0$, and $u=N^{-1}\xi$ is future unit timelike. In this application set the diffusion coefficient $L=0$, so $V=0$ and the supplier's number current is $J=nu$; it is future timelike throughout $\mathcal R$ since $n=1/v>0$, and on the fixed-density branch $J=n_0u$.

Adopt from [[post-tgr-first-order-dissipation]] the first-order heat closure and current/stress/entropy conventions on this regime. The physical heat-flux field $q$ is spatial, has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, and has constitutive coefficient $\kappa_{\rm th}=A_0/N$ for a constant $A_0>0$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$. With $\nabla_x$ the Euclidean spatial gradient, its specified static heat law, local energy balance, and insulated-face condition are

$$q=-\kappa_{\rm th}(\nabla_xT+T\nabla_x\log N),\qquad \kappa_{\rm th}=\frac{A_0}{N},\qquad NC_V\partial_{t_K}T+\operatorname{div}_x(N^2q)=0,\qquad N^2q\cdot\nu=0\ \text{on each face},$$

where $\operatorname{div}_x$ is Euclidean divergence and $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal to a box face. The adopted first-order closure specializes to this lapse-gradient form in the selected static frame; it is not inferred from an experiment. Since $N$ is time independent, $\nabla_xT+T\nabla_x\log N=N^{-1}\nabla_x\vartheta$, so this coefficient choice gives $N^2q=-A_0\nabla_x\vartheta$ and diffusivity $A_0/C_V$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$.

For the material stress/current in this selected branch put $Q^0=0$, $Q^i=q^i/c$, $J^a=n_0u^a$, and

$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b.$$

Here $Q=q/c$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in $\mathrm{Pa}$. In the first-order notation set the bulk, shear, and diffusion coefficients to zero, so $\Pi=0$, $\pi^{ab}=0$, and $V^a=0$; the thermal coefficient is $\kappa=\kappa_{\rm th}$. These are nonnegative $C^1(O)$ coefficient fields. The source-free number balance $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ remains part of this branch. The external support is the force-density field $f^b:=\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$, in $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, required to hold the medium on the fixed background. This model adopts the first-order heat closure but replaces that supplier's source-free stress balance by this supported balance. Require $u_bf^b=0$: the support may supply spatial force but no local power. Thus the state maps, constitutive fields, currents, and stress are smooth on $O$, and $f^b$ is a classical covariant divergence; this is a supported material model, not source-free full matter dynamics. Its entropy current is $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}m^{-3}}$; this postulate alone does not assert an entropy inequality.

This is an adopted effective parabolic model. It asserts no Einstein equation, no general relativistic-fluid initial-value theorem, no finite propagation speed, and no universal material law. It supplies no experiment, measurement, empirical premise, or evidence that a physical medium realizes the model.

items.title: Conditional redshift heat relaxation
items.statement:
Use the fixed static box, positive bounded lapse $N$, constants, material state function, observer field, heat flux, support, initial-data class, and SI conventions of [[post-tgr-supported-static-heat-model]]. Let $\widetilde\vartheta_0$ be its positive $C^2$ even periodic extension, and define $|\Omega|=L_1L_2L_3$, $\overline\vartheta=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega\vartheta_0\,dx$, and $C_\Omega=\frac32(\max_iL_i)^2$. Use Euclidean Lebesgue volume $dx$ and the associated $L^2(\Omega)$ norm. Then the model has a unique solution

$$T\in C([0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)\cap C^{2,1}((0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega),$$

where $C^{2,1}$ means two continuous spatial derivatives and one continuous time derivative up to the box faces at positive times. With $\vartheta=NT$ and $\Gamma(z,\tau)=(4\pi\tau)^{-3/2}\exp(-|z|^2/(4\tau))$ for $z\in\mathbb R^3$ and $\tau>0$, the solution is

$$\vartheta(t_K,x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma\!\left(x-y,\frac{A_0}{C_V}t_K\right)\widetilde\vartheta_0(y)\,dy\quad(t_K>0),\qquad \vartheta(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x),\qquad T=\frac{\vartheta}{N}.$$

It satisfies $C_V\partial_{t_K}\vartheta=A_0\Delta_x\vartheta$, the six insulated-face conditions $\partial_\nu\vartheta=0$, and $m_0\leq\vartheta\leq M_0$. The lapse-weighted material energy

$$\mathcal E_K(t_K)=\int_\Omega N(x)\epsilon(t_K,x)\,dx$$

is constant. For the entropy current $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ and total entropy $\mathcal S(t_K)=\int_\Omega s(t_K,x)\,dx$, the exact model rate is

$$\frac{d\mathcal S}{dt_K}=A_0\int_\Omega\frac{|\nabla_x\vartheta|^2}{\vartheta^2}\,dx\geq0.$$

Moreover,

$$\left\|\vartheta(t_K,\cdot)-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\leq\exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0t_K}{C_VC_\Omega}\right)\left\|\vartheta_0-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

Thus $T$ converges in $L^2(\Omega)$ to the positive proper-temperature profile $T_{\rm eq}(x)=\overline\vartheta/N(x)$, while the redshifted temperature $NT$ converges to the constant $\overline\vartheta$. These are conditional predictions of the adopted model. They do not establish that a real material obeys the postulates, and they do not assert a full Einstein-fluid solution, causal or stable relativistic-fluid evolution, or finite propagation speed. No empirical data are used.

items.title: Redshifted cosine medium
items.statement:
Use the box, positive lapse $N$, constants, material and support of [[pthm-tgr-supported-redshift-heat-relaxation]]. Assume $N$ is nonconstant on $\Omega$. Choose $\overline\vartheta>0$ and $\delta\in\mathbb R$ with $|\delta|<\overline\vartheta$. Set

$$\vartheta_0(x)=\overline\vartheta+\delta\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi x^1}{L_1}\right),\qquad x\in\overline\Omega.$$

The unique redshifted-temperature solution and proper-temperature field are

$$\vartheta(t_K,x)=\overline\vartheta+\delta\exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0\pi^2t_K}{C_VL_1^2}\right)\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi x^1}{L_1}\right),\qquad T(t_K,x)=\frac{\vartheta(t_K,x)}{N(x)}.$$

The redshifted temperature converges to $\overline\vartheta$, while the proper temperature converges to the nonconstant profile $\overline\vartheta/N(x)$. This is a calculated solution of the postulated model, not an observation about an actual material.

items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, $m>0$, and $0<\beta_0\le\beta_1<\infty$. For every $\beta\in[\beta_0,\beta_1]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-\beta|p|^2/(2m)}\,dp=\left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{d/2}.$$
For every integer $s\ge0$, the polynomially weighted Gaussian has a uniform finite bound
$$\sup_{\beta\in[\beta_0,\beta_1]}\int_{\mathbb R^d}(1+|p|^{2s})e^{-\beta|p|^2/(2m)}\,dp<\infty.$$

items.statement:
Let $0\le a<b<\infty$ and let $F:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. The closed radial shell $A_{a,b}=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:a\le|x|\le b\}$ is Jordan measurable, and
$$\int_{A_{a,b}}F(|x|)\,dx=4\pi\int_a^b F(r)r^2\,dr.$$
The angular area measure used below is the pushforward of $\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$ under $(\theta,\phi)\mapsto(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$; its total mass is $4\pi$.

items.statement:
Use the phase space and dimensionless reference measure of [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]]. Fix an integer $N\ge1$, a bounded Lebesgue measurable $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ with positive finite volume, a common mass $m>0$, a gravitational coupling $G>0$, and a softening length $a>0$. On $\Gamma_N=B^N\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ define
$$H_{N,a}(q,p)=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{|p_i|^2}{2m}+U_a(q),\qquad U_a(q)=-\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac{Gm^2}{\sqrt{|q_i-q_j|^2+a^2}}.$$
The positions and momenta are mathematical phase variables; the softening is a fixed regulator parameter. The Hamiltonian is measurable and its potential is bounded because each pair denominator is at least $a$. A point-particle model is a different Hamiltonian and is not included at $a=0$.

items.statement:
Use SI units, positive masses $m_1,m_2$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, gravitational parameter $A=Gm_1m_2$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$, relative position $q\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm m$, relative momentum $p\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and a fixed action reference $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume $r_0>0$ and $R>16r_0$. The relative phase domain is
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{rel}}=\{(q,p):r_0\le |q|\le R,\ p\in\mathbb R^3\},\qquad d\nu_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{d^3q\,d^3p}{h_*^3},$$
with no center-of-mass variables or factor $1/2!$. The relative Hamiltonian is
$$h(q,p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2\mu}-\frac{A}{|q|}.$$

For $E=-e<0$ with $A/R<e\le A/(16r_0)$, put $\delta=e r_0/A\in(0,1/16]$ and
$$J(\delta)=\int_\delta^1s^{1/2}(1-s)^{3/2}\,ds,\qquad \Omega(E)=\nu_{\mathrm{rel}}\{(q,p)\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{rel}}:h(q,p)\le E\}.$$
The radial integration formula of [[lem-tgr-annular-radial-integration]] gives the explicit phase volume
$$\Omega(-e)=\frac{(4\pi)(4\pi/3)(2\mu)^{3/2}A^3}{h_*^3}\,e^{-3/2}J(\delta).$$
This is finite and positive on the stated branch.

Define $S^2=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:|u|=1\}$ and $p_*(r,E)=\sqrt{2\mu(E+A/r)}$ for $r_0\le r\le A/e$. Let $d\sigma$ be the angular area measure of total mass $4\pi$ from [[lem-tgr-annular-radial-integration]]. Push the finite measure $(\mu p_*/h_*^3)d^3q\,d\sigma(u)$ on $\{r_0\le|q|\le A/e\}\times S^2$ forward by $(q,u)\mapsto(q,p_*(|q|,E)u)$; call the resulting measure $\Sigma_E$. Its candidate normalized shell law is $P_E=\Sigma_E/\Omega'(E)$. The separate result [[lem-tgr-regulated-kepler-shell-law-normalization]] proves $\Omega'(E)>0$, finite total mass, and $P_E(\{h=E\})=1$. Thus the energy-shell preparation is explicitly defined; it is not inferred from phase-volume counting alone.

The entropy convention attached to this model is Gibbs volume, $S_G(E)=k_B\log\Omega(E)$, with $1/T_G=dS_G/dE$ and $C_G=dE/dT_G$ where defined. Other finite-system entropy conventions are distinct.

items.title: Static relativistic finite gas normalization and hydrostatics
items.design_state: Batch 69 authoring draft; exact claim, scoped hypotheses, current supplier interfaces, and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Let $I_{x^0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ an open bounded coordinate box with compact closure and positive volume. On a neighborhood of $I_{x^0}\times\overline B$, with $x^0=ct$ assigned metres and $t$ in seconds, prescribe the smooth static metric
$$g=-\mathcal N(x)^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(x)dx^i dx^j,$$
where $h_{ij}$ is positive definite with eigenvalues bounded above and away from zero, and the lapse satisfies $0<\mathcal N_0\le\mathcal N(x)\le\mathcal N_1<\infty$. The static unit observer is $u=\mathcal N^{-1}\partial_{x^0}$, so $g(u,u)=-1$; this is a prescribed background, not a solution sourced by the gas.

Use SI units: particle mass $m>0$ is in $\mathrm{kg}$, $c>0$ is in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, orthonormal momentum $\hat p$ is in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and local energy $E$ is in $\mathrm J$. In any local orthonormal coframe, $p_i=e_i{}^a\hat p_a$ and $h_{ij}=\sum_a e_i{}^ae_j{}^a$, so $dV_h\,d^3\hat p=d^3x\,d^3p_i$; orthonormal-frame changes are rotations and preserve $d^3\hat p$. This defines a fibre measure without assuming a global frame. Use the fixed action reference $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $\beta_K>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$:
$$E(\hat p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p|^2},\qquad H_K(x,\hat p)=\mathcal N(x)E(\hat p),\qquad Z_1(\beta_K)=\int_B\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\beta_KH_K}\frac{dV_h\,d^3\hat p}{h_*^3}.$$
Then $0<Z_1<\infty$, with all polynomial momentum moments and compact-positive-$\beta_K$ derivatives finite. For each fixed particle count $M\ge1$, the classical ideal-gas preparation with Gibbs factor $1/M!$ has $Z_M=Z_1^M/M!$; a grand fugacity preparation with dimensionless $z>0$ has $\Xi=\exp(zZ_1)$.

Define $f(x,\hat p)=z h_*^{-3}e^{-\beta_KH_K}$ and the proper local densities
$$n(x)=\int f\,d^3\hat p,\quad \varepsilon(x)=\int E f\,d^3\hat p,\quad P(x)=\frac13\int \hat p\cdot\nabla_{\hat p}E\,f\,d^3\hat p.$$
Their units are $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, respectively. With $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}=\beta_K\mathcal N(x)$ and $T_K=(k_B\beta_K)^{-1}$, the exact model identities are
$$T_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)=\frac1{k_B\beta_{\mathrm{loc}}}=\frac{T_K}{\mathcal N(x)},\quad P=nk_BT_{\mathrm{loc}},\quad \partial_iP=-(\varepsilon+P)\partial_i\log\mathcal N.$$
If $z=e^{\beta_K\mu_K}$ with $\mu_K$ in joules, the local chemical parameter is $\mu_{\mathrm{loc}}=\mu_K/\mathcal N$. No Einstein equation, self-consistent gas backreaction, interacting quantum trace, or arbitrary curved-space mode spectrum is asserted.

items.statement:
Use the box, mass $m$, integer $N\ge1$, regulator $a>0$, and Hamiltonian $H_{N,a}=K_N+U_a$ of [[def-tgr-softened-gravity-finite-phase]], with $K_N=\sum_i|p_i|^2/(2m)$. Put $C_N=Gm^2N(N-1)/(2a)$ and use the reference measure of [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]]. For every $\beta>0$,
$$0<\frac{|B|^N}{N!h_*^{3N}}\left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{3N/2} \le Z_N(\beta) \le e^{\beta C_N}\frac{|B|^N}{N!h_*^{3N}}\left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{3N/2}<\infty.$$
The density $p_\beta=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}$ is a positive probability density. For each integer $j\ge0$, $\int_{\Gamma_N}|H_{N,a}|^j e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}d\nu_N$ is finite, and $Z_N$ is $C^\infty$ on $(0,\infty)$ with
$$Z_N^{(j)}(\beta)=\int_{\Gamma_N}(-H_{N,a})^j e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}\,d\nu_N.$$
On every compact positive $\beta$ interval, one integrable majorant works for each fixed derivative order.

items.title: Point collapse and unscaled gravity nonextensivity
items.design_state: Batch 69 authoring draft; exact claim, scoped hypotheses, current supplier interfaces, and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Use the dimensionless phase reference of [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]] and the softened Hamiltonian of [[def-tgr-softened-gravity-finite-phase]].

1. For two equal positive masses in a bounded three-dimensional box with nonempty interior, the distinct point Hamiltonian
$$H_2^{\mathrm{pt}}(q,p)=\frac{|p_1|^2+|p_2|^2}{2m}-\frac{Gm^2}{|q_1-q_2|}$$
makes the canonical partition integral infinite for every $\beta>0$.

2. For fixed $a>0$, let $B_N$ be a sequence of bounded boxes containing one fixed cube $C$ of volume $v>0$ and diameter $D<\infty$, with constants $b_1,b_2>0$ such that $b_1N\le |B_N|\le b_2N$. The softened canonical partition functions satisfy
$$\frac{\log Z_N(\beta)}{N}\ge \beta c(N-1)-\log N+K_\beta, \qquad c=\frac{Gm^2}{2\sqrt{D^2+a^2}}>0,$$
where $K_\beta$ is independent of $N$. Hence $\log Z_N/N\to+\infty$ and the free energy per particle $-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N/N$ tends to $-\infty$.

3. For the unscaled point attraction $-Gm^2/r$ restricted to the hard-core position domain $D_N=\{q\in B_n^N:|q_i-q_j|>a\text{ for }i\ne j\}$ with fixed $a>0$, there is a fixed-density sequence of integers $n\ge2$, $N=n^3$, boxes $B_n=(0,nd)^3$ of side $O(n)$ for fixed $d>a$, and positive-volume admissible position sets on which the interaction energy is at most $-c_0N^{5/3}$ for some $c_0>0$. Its canonical partition functions therefore also satisfy $\log Z_N/N\to+\infty$.

For the sequences in clauses 2 and 3, write $F_N(\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N(\beta)$. In clause 2, the free energy per particle $F_N/N$ tends to $-\infty$. Since $b_1\le |B_N|/N\le b_2$, the free energy per volume $F_N/|B_N|$ also tends to $-\infty$. Clause 3 gives the same per-particle limit along its fixed-density sequence, and there $|B_n|/N=d^3$, so the per-volume free energy also tends to $-\infty$. Thus finite boxes at each particle count, fixed softening in clause 2, and hard-core exclusion with unscaled attraction in clause 3 do not ensure a finite real thermodynamic-limit value for either normalized free energy in these sequences. These results do not address differently scaled interactions or every possible gravitational thermodynamic limit.

items.title: Exact relative-shell canonical normalization and response
items.design_state: Batch 69 authoring draft; exact claim, scoped hypotheses, current supplier interfaces, and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Use the relative Kepler Hamiltonian and shell $Q=\{q\in\mathbb R^3:r_0\le|q|\le R\}$ from [[def-tgr-regulated-kepler-shell-law]], with $\mu,A,r_0>0$ and $R>16r_0$. For every $\beta>0$, define
$$Z_{\mathrm{rel}}(\beta)=\frac1{h_*^3}\int_Q\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\beta h(q,p)}\,d^3p\,d^3q.$$
Then
$$0<\frac{|Q|e^{\beta A/R}}{h_*^3}\left(\frac{2\pi\mu}{\beta}\right)^{3/2} \le Z_{\mathrm{rel}}(\beta) \le \frac{|Q|e^{\beta A/r_0}}{h_*^3}\left(\frac{2\pi\mu}{\beta}\right)^{3/2}<\infty.$$
All energy moments are finite, and on every compact positive $\beta$ interval one integrable majorant justifies all derivatives of $Z_{\mathrm{rel}}$. Put $d\nu_{\mathrm{rel}}=h_*^{-3}d^3q\,d^3p$ on $Q\times\mathbb R^3$ and $p_\beta=Z_{\mathrm{rel}}(\beta)^{-1}e^{-\beta h}$. For a measurable observable $A:Q\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ with finite second moment, define $\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int A p_\beta\,d\nu_{\mathrm{rel}}$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(A):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\nu_{\mathrm{rel}}$. The normalized canonical density has
$$\langle h\rangle_\beta=-\partial_\beta\log Z_{\mathrm{rel}},\qquad \frac{d\langle h\rangle_\beta}{d\beta}=-\operatorname{Var}_\beta(h),\qquad C_K:=\frac{d\langle h\rangle_\beta}{dT_K}=k_B\beta^2\operatorname{Var}_\beta(h)\ge0, \quad T_K=(k_B\beta)^{-1}.$$
This is the exact six-dimensional relative canonical preparation; center-of-mass degrees are absent.

items.title: Negative Gibbs-volume capacity in a finite regulated shell
items.design_state: Batch 69 authoring draft; exact claim, scoped hypotheses, current supplier interfaces, and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Under [[def-tgr-regulated-kepler-shell-law]], let $E=-e$, $\delta=er_0/A\in(0,1/16]$, and
$$z(\delta)=\frac{\delta^{3/2}(1-\delta)^{3/2}}{J(\delta)},\qquad \mathcal B(\delta)=\frac32+z(\delta).$$
For the Gibbs-volume entropy $S_G(E)=k_B\log\Omega(E)$ and temperature convention $1/T_G=dS_G/dE$,
$$T_G(E)=\frac{e}{k_B\mathcal B(\delta)},\qquad C_G(E):=\frac{dE}{dT_G} =-\frac{k_B\mathcal B(\delta)^2}{\mathcal B(\delta)-\delta\mathcal B'(\delta)}<0.$$
The denominator is at least $1$. Derivatives are ordinary for $0<\delta<1/16$; at $\delta=1/16$, compute $dS_G/dE$ and $dT_G/dE$ as right derivatives from within the branch and define $C_G=1/(dT_G/dE)$. This is a finite regulated mathematical branch with the stated entropy convention; it does not identify a universal operational temperature or dynamical stability.

items.design_state: Batch 69 authoring draft; exact claim, scoped hypotheses, current supplier interfaces, and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:

For a measurable observable $A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ with finite second moment, define $\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\Gamma_N}A p_\beta\,d\nu_N$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(A):=\int_{\Gamma_N}(A-\langle A\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\nu_N$. Define $T_K=(k_B\beta)^{-1}$ and $C_K=d\langle H_{N,a}\rangle_\beta/dT_K$. Then
$$\langle H_{N,a}\rangle_\beta=-\partial_\beta\log Z_N,\qquad \partial_\beta\langle H_{N,a}\rangle_\beta=-\operatorname{Var}_\beta(H_{N,a}),\qquad C_K=k_B\beta^2\operatorname{Var}_\beta(H_{N,a})\ge0.$$
This is a response identity for a fixed Hamiltonian and fixed regulator; it does not assert stability when the Hamiltonian or background varies with temperature.

items.design_state: Batch 69 authoring draft; exact claim, scoped hypotheses, current supplier interfaces, and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
This is a finite-mode conditional construction. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the exact current interface for the batch-45 draft [[lem-qsm-models-diagonal-occupation-trace]], whose Statement matches its planned manifest entry on [[qsm-bose-fermi-gases]]. Its current carrier has a complete authored proof and precheck, plus a Step-1 ready authoring record; those records do not assert independent review approval. Let $J=\{1,\ldots,M\}$ be a nonempty finite set of supplied modes, let $m,c>0$, let $\mathcal N_j>0$ be supplied dimensionless lapse values, and let $\hat p_j\in\mathbb R^3$ be supplied mode momenta. Put
$$\epsilon_j=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p_j|^2},\qquad E_j=\mathcal N_j\epsilon_j,\qquad \mathcal H_F=\mathbb C^{2^M},$$
with occupation basis $|n_1,\ldots,n_M\rangle$, $n_j\in\{0,1\}$, and diagonal operators $H|n\rangle=(\sum_jE_jn_j)|n\rangle$, $N|n\rangle=(\sum_jn_j)|n\rangle$. For $\beta_K>0$ and finite $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$, conditional on that exact supplier result,
$$\Xi_F=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta_K(H-\mu_KN)} =\prod_{j=1}^M\left(1+e^{-\beta_K(E_j-\mu_K)}\right)<\infty,$$
and the normalized diagonal state has occupation mean
$$\mathbb E[n_j]=\frac1{e^{\beta_K(E_j-\mu_K)}+1}.$$
With $\beta_j=\beta_K\mathcal N_j$ and $\mu_j=\mu_K/\mathcal N_j$, this is exactly
$$\mathbb E[n_j]=\frac1{e^{\beta_j(\epsilon_j-\mu_j)}+1}.$$
No arbitrary curved-space Dirac spectrum or self-consistent quantum-gravity state is asserted.

items.title: Finite-bath entropy curvature and specified exchange stability
items.design_state: Batch 69 authoring draft; exact claim, scoped hypotheses, current supplier interfaces, and Step 1 disposition are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Let $I_1,I_2\subseteq\mathbb R$ be open energy intervals (energies in joules), and let $S_i:I_i\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ entropies measured in joules per kelvin. Fix a total energy $E_{\mathrm{tot}}$ in joules and define the open exchange domain $I:=\{x\in I_1:E_{\mathrm{tot}}-x\in I_2\}$. For $x\in I$, set $E_1=x$, $E_2=E_{\mathrm{tot}}-x$, and $T_i(E_i):=1/S_i'(E_i)$ wherever $S_i'(E_i)>0$. At a point $x\in I$ with $T_1(E_1)=T_2(E_2)=T>0$ and $T_i'(E_i)\ne0$, define the finite nonzero heat capacities $C_i(E_i):=1/T_i'(E_i)=dE_i/dT_i$. For
$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x)=S_1(x)+S_2(E_{\mathrm{tot}}-x),$$
one has
$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}''(x)=-\frac1{T^2}\left(\frac1{C_1}+\frac1{C_2}\right).$$
In particular, if $C_1<0<C_2$, the critical point is a strict local entropy maximum in this energy-exchange direction whenever $0<C_2<|C_1|$.

This condition is realized by taking $S_1=S_G$ from [[thm-tgr-regulated-kepler-negative-capacity]] at an interior branch energy $E_*$ (for example, $r_0/R<\delta<1/16$), where $T_*=T_G(E_*)>0$ and $C_1=C_G(E_*)<0$. The explicit phase-volume formula makes $S_1$ $C^2$ on an open energy interval around $E_*$. Choose a finite bath entropy
$$S_b(E_b)=C_b\log\left(\frac{E_b-E_0}{C_bT_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right)+S_0,\qquad E_b>E_0,$$
with $C_b>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $E_0$ in $\mathrm J$, $T_{\mathrm{ref}}>0$ in $\mathrm K$, and $S_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. It has $T_b=(E_b-E_0)/C_b$ and heat capacity $C_b$; choose $E_b=E_0+C_bT_*$ to match the subsystem temperature $T_*$ and choose $C_b<|C_1|$.

Separately adopt, on the open domain $I$ and with time $t$ in seconds, the effective scalar exchange equation
$$\dot x=L S_{\mathrm{tot}}'(x),\qquad L>0\ \mathrm{J\,K\,s^{-1}}.$$
For each strict local maximum $x_*\in I$ with $S_{\mathrm{tot}}''(x_*)<0$, there are $a,r>0$ such that $I_0=[x_*-r,x_*+r]\subset I$, $S_{\mathrm{tot}}''\le-a$ on $I_0$, and every solution with $x(0)\in I_0$ exists for all $t\ge0$, remains in $I_0$, and satisfies $|x(t)-x_*|\le e^{-La t}|x(0)-x_*|$. Thus the equilibrium solution $x(t)\equiv x_*$ attracts those initial states exponentially. Along every solution, $dS_{\mathrm{tot}}/dt=L(S_{\mathrm{tot}}')^2\ge0$. This is stability of the specified one-dimensional exchange law, not of a general relativistic star or a causal transport equation.

The per-particle free-energy density is $f_N=F_N/N$ (in joules), and the per-volume free-energy density is $g_N=F_N/V_N$ (in joules per cubic metre). Here a “finite extensive free-energy density” means that the chosen normalized sequence has a finite real thermodynamic-limit value. The claim refuted is that a fixed positive softening length guarantees such a finite limit for every sequence of unscaled self-gravitating boxes whose volumes are bounded above and below by positive multiples of $N$. The counterexample below has both $f_N\to-\infty$ and $g_N\to-\infty$.

items.title: Smooth static spherical geometry and state domain
items.design_state: Planned static spherical metric, areal radius, time orientation, source tensor, mass function and SI conventions.
items.statement:
Assume the countable-choice convention of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical smooth tangent- and tensor-bundle structures in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Fix positive formal parameters $c>0$ and $G>0$ with SI dimensions $[c]=\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and $[G]=\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$. In this mathematical definition they are fixed parameters, not derived quantities, and no numerical or empirical value is asserted. Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval for a length coordinate $x^0$, and define the corresponding time coordinate $t:=x^0/c\in I_0/c$, measured in seconds. Let $r$ be the coordinate on $(0,\infty)$, and let $(S^2,\gamma)$ be the unit round sphere with the induced smooth round metric of [[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]. On the product smooth four-manifold $M=I_0\times(0,\infty)\times S^2$, using the canonical product smooth structure of [[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]], define, for $\phi,b\in C^\infty((0,\infty),\mathbb R)$ with $b(r)>0$,
$$g=-e^{2\phi(r)}(dx^0)^2+b(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma.$$
Set $N=\partial_{x^0}$ as time orientation. The signature convention is $(-,+,+,+)$, $x^0$ and $r$ are measured in metres, the line element has units $\mathrm m^2$, and $\phi$ and $b$ are dimensionless. The sphere at fixed $(x^0,r)$ has induced metric $r^2\gamma$. In spherical coordinates its area element is $r^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$ by [[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]], so $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi r^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi=4\pi r^2$; hence $r$ is the areal radius. The flow of $N$ is translation in $x^0$ and preserves $g$ because its coefficients are independent of $x^0$; here a Killing field means a vector field whose local flow preserves the metric. Moreover, $g(N,\cdot)=-e^{2\phi}dx^0$, so $N$ is normal to the hypersurfaces $x^0=\mathrm{constant}$. In this definition, the metric is static in the precise sense that it has a timelike Killing field normal to such hypersurfaces; $N$ is timelike because $g(N,N)=-e^{2\phi}<0$.

A **static isotropic diagonal source field** is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,1)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]], defined globally using the product splitting $TM\cong TI_0\oplus T(0,\infty)\oplus TS^2$ by
$$T(v_0,v_r,v_S)=(-\epsilon(r)v_0,p(r)v_r,p(r)v_S).$$
In every standard spherical chart its mixed components are
$$T^a{}_b=\operatorname{diag}(-\epsilon(r),p(r),p(r),p(r)),$$
where $\epsilon,p\in C^\infty((0,\infty),\mathbb R)$ represent energy density and isotropic pressure, respectively, under the formal physical reading, with $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The associated covariant tensor has components $T_{ab}:=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$; it is smooth and symmetric because both component matrices are diagonal, as defined for covariant $2$-tensor fields in [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Define the mass function $M:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ by
$$M(r):=\frac{c^2r}{2G}\bigl(1-b(r)\bigr),$$
which has units $\mathrm{kg}$. No Einstein equation, equation of state, central regularity, physical applicability, or empirical claim is part of this definition. The Einstein tensor and component conventions used later are those of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] and [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]].

items.title: Even radial coefficients give a C² Cartesian center
items.design_state: Additional A-page supplier required by the regular-center geometry: prove even radial C2 data give a Cartesian C2 center before the local TOV and entropy consumers use it.
items.statement:
Let $\delta>0$, let $f,h\in C^2((-\delta,\delta),\mathbb R)$ be even, and let $B_\delta(0)\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ carry its standard Euclidean coordinates $x=(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ and radius $r=|x|$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Then $F(x)=f(|x|)$ is $C^2$ on $B_\delta(0)$, and each component $H_{ij}(x)=\delta_{ij}+x_ix_jh(|x|)$ is $C^2$ there. In particular, if an areal spherical spatial metric has $b(r)=1-r^2q(r)$ with even $q\in C^2((-\delta,\delta))$ and $b>0$, then its Cartesian coefficients
$$g_{ij}(x)=\delta_{ij}+x_ix_j\frac{q(|x|)}{b(|x|)}$$
extend $C^2$ across the center. This result is a coordinate regularity statement; it asserts no field equation or physical claim.

items.title: Complete spherical Einstein and conservation reduction
items.design_state: Planned complete signed component calculation and both directions between Einstein/conservation equations and the mass, lapse and pressure system.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ exactly as in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $J\subseteq(0,\infty)$ be an open interval; let the state domain, metric, mixed source tensor, mass function, units, and signature be those of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Write $\kappa=8\pi G/c^4$, and let $G^a{}_b$ be the mixed Einstein tensor defined from the signed curvature convention in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Suppose $\phi,b,\epsilon,p$ are smooth on $J$ and $b>0$. As a conditional mathematical system, assume the component equations
$$G^a{}_b=\kappa T^a{}_b.$$
Then on $J$,
$$M'=\frac{4\pi r^2\epsilon}{c^2},\qquad \phi'=\frac{GM/c^2+4\pi G r^3p/c^4}{r^2b},\qquad p'=-\frac{G(\epsilon+p)(M+4\pi r^3p/c^2)}{c^2r^2b}.$$
Conversely, if these three ordinary differential equations hold with $M=c^2r(1-b)/(2G)$, then every mixed Einstein component satisfies $G^a{}_b=\kappa T^a{}_b$. The identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ used for this converse is the geometric theorem of [[thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-free-einstein]], not a field equation or empirical premise. This lemma is a pure conditional calculation and makes no claim that the model describes nature.

items.title: Proper spherical entropy and particle constrained functionals
items.design_state: Planned fixed-radius proper entropy, particle-number and mass-energy functionals on a regular positive-b state chart.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in [[def-countable-choice]]. Fix $R>0$, an open state chart $\mathcal U\subset(0,\infty)^2$, and a function $s\in C^2(\mathcal U,\mathbb R)$ with $s_\epsilon>0$. The coordinates on $\mathcal U$ are energy density $\epsilon$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and particle number density $n$ in $\mathrm m^{-3}$; the entropy density has units $[s]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. Define the local temperature, chemical potential, and pressure functions by
$$\Theta(\epsilon,n):=\frac1{s_\epsilon(\epsilon,n)},\qquad \mu(\epsilon,n):=-\Theta(\epsilon,n)s_n(\epsilon,n),\qquad p(\epsilon,n):=\Theta s+\mu n-\epsilon.$$
These are $C^1$ functions on $\mathcal U$; their formal SI dimensions are $\mathrm K$, $\mathrm J$, and $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, respectively. By definition $\epsilon+p=\Theta s+\mu n$, and differentiation gives $d\epsilon=\Theta\,ds+\mu\,dn$ and $dp=s\,d\Theta+n\,d\mu$ on the chart.

Let $\epsilon,n$ be restrictions to $[0,R]$ of even $C^2$ functions on an open interval containing $[-R,R]$, positive on $[0,R]$, with image in a compact subset of $\mathcal U$. This evenness is the center regularity convention. With $K:=4\pi G/c^4$, define
$$M(r):=\frac{4\pi}{c^2}\int_0^r \epsilon(t)t^2\,dt,\qquad b(r):=1-\frac{2GM(r)}{c^2r}\quad(r>0),\qquad b(0):=1.$$
Equivalently, $b(r)=1-r^2q(r)$ on $[-R,R]$, where
$$q(r):=2K\int_0^1s^2\epsilon(rs)\,ds.$$
The compact-parameter differentiation theorem [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]] makes $q$ even $C^2$. Therefore [[lem-tgr-even-radial-center-regularity]] gives the corresponding $C^2$ Cartesian spatial metric coefficients.
Assume $b(r)\ge b_*>0$ on $[0,R]$. The displayed integrals are Riemann integrals in the Darboux convention of [[def-darboux-integral]]; their continuous integrands are integrable by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], and $b^{-1/2}$ is continuous on this positive range by [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]. Use the spatial metric $h=b(r)^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma$ on $(0,R)\times S^2$, where $\gamma$ is the unit round sphere metric used in [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Here $h$ has $C^2$ coefficients and the Cartesian center extension just established; no globally smooth static state is required. Define its volume density in a spherical coordinate chart by $\sqrt{\det(h_{ij})}\,dr\,d\theta\,d\varphi$. Since $\det(h_{ij})=b^{-1}r^4\sin^2\theta$, integration over the unit sphere gives the radial density $4\pi r^2b(r)^{-1/2}dr$. This uses the same spatial metric formula as the smooth static domain, at the present $C^2$ regularity. Define the proper entropy, proper particle number, and spherical mass-energy functionals
$$S[\epsilon,n]:=4\pi\int_0^R s(\epsilon(r),n(r))\,r^2b(r)^{-1/2}\,dr,\quad N_b[\epsilon,n]:=4\pi\int_0^R n(r)\,r^2b(r)^{-1/2}\,dr,\quad E[\epsilon,n]:=c^2M(R)=4\pi\int_0^R\epsilon(r)r^2\,dr.$$
Their formal dimensions are $[S]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, $[N_b]=1$, and $[E]=\mathrm J$. These are mathematical functionals on the supplied state chart and positive-$b$ profile domain; they assert no entropy law, equilibrium, maximum, dynamics, or empirical fact.

items.title: Regular-center TOV local existence and dependence
items.design_state: Planned uniform local regular-center existence and parameter dependence; prove the singular center by Volterra contraction and use ordinary continuation only for r>0.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, where $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly [[def-countable-choice]] and is inherited from the smooth Lorentzian/tensor suppliers. Let $\epsilon:I_p\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^\infty$ on an open interval $I_p\subseteq(0,\infty)$, let $P_c\subset I_p$ be a nonempty compact interval, and choose $\delta>0$ such that the closed $\delta$-neighbourhood of $P_c$ lies in $I_p$. Fix $\phi_c\in\mathbb R$ and use the units and signature of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Put $K=4\pi G/c^4$, with formal units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm J^{-1}$; $v$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. There is $R_0>0$, common to all $p_c\in P_c$, such that for each $p_c$ there is a unique pair of even continuous functions $p,v$ on $[-R_0,R_0]$ with $|p(r)-p_c|\le\delta$ and satisfying
$$v(r)=K\int_0^1 s^2\epsilon(p(rs))\,ds,\qquad p(r)=p_c-\int_0^r t\frac{(\epsilon(p(t))+p(t))(v(t)+Kp(t))}{1-2t^2v(t)}\,dt.$$
They are $C^\infty$, $p(0)=p_c$, $v(0)=K\epsilon(p_c)/3$, $p'(0)=v'(0)=0$, and $b(r):=1-2r^2v(r)\ge1/2$ on $[0,R_0]$. Define
$$M(r)=\frac{c^2}{G}r^3v(r),\qquad \phi(r)=\phi_c+\int_0^r t\frac{v(t)+Kp(t)}{1-2t^2v(t)}\,dt\quad(|r|\le R_0).$$
Then $(M,p,\phi)$ satisfies the mass, pressure, and lapse equations of [[lem-tgr-spherical-einstein-tov-reduction]] for $0<r\le R_0$. The metric extends across $r=0$ as a $C^2$ Lorentzian metric in Cartesian spatial coordinates, with $b(0)=1$ and lapse $e^{\phi_c}>0$; this is the regular-center conclusion in this item. On the common interval, $p,v,\phi$ depend continuously in the uniform norm on $p_c\in P_c$. For $r>0$, the solution continues past any finite endpoint at which its graph remains in a compact subset of
$$\{(r,p,v):r>0,\ p\in I_p,\ 1-2r^2v>0\}.$$
No assertion is made that every equation of state reaches a zero-pressure surface, avoids a horizon globally, or gives a dynamically stable solution.

items.title: Exact regular constant-density solution with verified matching
items.design_state: Planned exact uniform-density interior with regular center, explicit pressure/lapse, vacuum exterior and no-layer matching; no general Buchdahl claim.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ exactly as in [[def-countable-choice]] and use the geometry and units of [[def-tgr-spherical-static-state-domain]]. Let $\rho_0>0$ be a constant mass density in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, $R>0$ in metres, $\epsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, $M_R=4\pi\rho_0R^3/3$ in kilograms, and
$$u=\frac{2GM_R}{c^2R}\in(0,8/9),\qquad a=\sqrt{1-u},\qquad B(r)=\sqrt{1-u r^2/R^2}.$$
For $0\le r\le R$, define
$$M(r)=M_R(r/R)^3,\quad b(r)=B(r)^2,\quad p(r)=\epsilon_0\frac{B(r)-a}{3a-B(r)},\quad e^{\phi(r)}=\frac{3a-B(r)}2.$$
Set $\epsilon(r)=\epsilon_0$ for $0\le r<R$ and $\epsilon(r)=0$ for $r\ge R$. For $r\ge R$, also set $M(r)=M_R$, $b(r)=1-2GM_R/(c^2r)$, $p(r)=0$, and $e^{\phi(r)}=\sqrt{b(r)}$. Then $p(R)=0$, $b>0$, the interior lapse is positive, and the central pressure is finite and equals $\epsilon_0(1-a)/(3a-1)$. The interior and exterior fields solve the spherical Einstein and conservation system of [[lem-tgr-spherical-einstein-tov-reduction]] on their open pieces; the interior equations extend to the center by continuity. The interior metric has a $C^2$ Cartesian center; the interior and exterior join at $r=R$ as a $C^1$ metric that is piecewise $C^2$, with matching first derivatives at the interface. For this interface assertion, a radial distribution on an open radial-coordinate interval $U$ is a linear functional $T$ on $C_c^\infty(U)$, the space of smooth real functions with compact support in $U$, such that for every compact $K\subset U$ there exist $C_K\ge0$ and an integer $N_K\ge0$ satisfying $|T[\psi]|\le C_K\max_{0\le j\le N_K}\sup_K|\psi^{(j)}|$ whenever $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq K$, the Dirac distribution is $\delta_R[\psi]=\psi(R)$, and a delta-supported surface stress means a source term $S^a{}_b\delta_R$. The prescribed piecewise source has no such term. The proof also shows that $0<u<8/9$ is necessary and sufficient for these algebraic formulas to give real interior data with $b>0$, finite nonnegative pressure, and positive lapse throughout $[0,R]$. This range is specific to the constant-density family and is not a general Buchdahl theorem.

items.title: Constrained entropy criticality, Tolman–Klein equivalence and TOV consequence
items.design_state: Planned first-variation equivalence for fixed-radius constrained entropy; prove criticality only and do not claim a maximum or stability.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in [[def-countable-choice]]. Fix $R>0$, a state chart and positive even $C^2$ profiles $(\epsilon,n)$ with compact range and $b\ge b_*>0$ as in [[def-tgr-spherical-entropy-constraint-functional]]. Let $\Theta,\mu,p,S,N_b,E$ be the functions and functionals defined there. Define the lapse by
$$\phi(r)=\frac12\log b(R)-\int_r^R\frac{GM(t)/c^2+4\pi Gt^3p(t)/c^4}{t^2b(t)}\,dt,$$
whose integrand extends continuously to $0$ because $M(t)=O(t^3)$, so it solves the lapse equation of [[lem-tgr-spherical-einstein-tov-reduction]] with boundary normalization
$$\phi(R)=\frac12\log b(R).$$
An admissible profile curve is a map $\lambda\mapsto(\epsilon_\lambda,n_\lambda)$ on an open interval about $0$, $C^1$ in the sup-norm space $C^0([0,R])^2$, whose values are even $C^2$ profiles in the stated compactly-contained state chart and positive-$b$ domain, and whose derivative at $0$ is a smooth pair compactly supported in $(0,R)$ (extended evenly at the center). Define constrained stationarity to mean that $S$ has zero derivative at the base profile along every such curve on which both $E$ and $N_b$ are constant. Then constrained stationarity is equivalent to the existence of constants $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and $\beta\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$\frac{\mu(r)}{\Theta(r)}=\alpha,\qquad \Theta(r)e^{\phi(r)}=\Theta_K,\qquad \mu(r)e^{\phi(r)}=\mu_K$$
are constant on $(0,R)$. In that case the profile satisfies
$$p'(r)=-(\epsilon(r)+p(r))\phi'(r) =-\frac{G(\epsilon(r)+p(r))(M(r)+4\pi r^3p(r)/c^2)}{c^2r^2b(r)},$$
the Tolman and Klein products are $\Theta_K=\Theta(R)\sqrt{b(R)}$ and $\mu_K=\mu(R)\sqrt{b(R)}$, and the two multipliers are $\alpha=\mu/\Theta$ and $\beta=1/\Theta_K$. The conclusion is a first-variation criticality statement only; it proves neither a local or global entropy maximum nor existence or dynamical stability of a physical fluid.

items.title: Constant-density profile has unequal pressures at equal energy density
items.design_state: Planned counterexample distinguishing a static constant-density profile from an invertible causal barotropic transport law.
items.statement:
For this item, a differentiable barotropic pressure law is a $C^1$ map $P:J_\epsilon\to\mathbb R$, where $J_\epsilon\subset(0,\infty)$ is an open interval of energy-density values containing $\epsilon_0$, both input energy density and output pressure have units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and $p(r)=P(\epsilon(r))$ for each interior radius $0\le r<R$. The finite causal-slope criterion under consideration is $0\le P'(x)\le1$ for $x\in J_\epsilon$, so $P'$ is dimensionless. For units only, set the formal parameter $c_s^2:=c^2P'(x)$, with units $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$; this item assigns no fluid-dynamical meaning to it and makes no claim about an observed signal speed.

The claim refuted is that every regular static constant-density solution supplies such a map $P$ satisfying this slope criterion.

items.title: Finite regulated Newtonian gravitational canonical preparation
items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Work in SI units. Adopt positive Newton constant $G$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, common particle mass $m$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, positions $q_i$ in $\mathrm m$, momenta $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy $H$ in joules, Boltzmann constant $k_B$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. Fix an action reference $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$; it is a phase-counting convention, not an assertion that $h_*$ equals Planck's constant. These conventions follow [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]].

For an integer $N\ge2$, take a bounded measurable confining region $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $0<|B|<\infty$ and adopt the ordered phase space $\Gamma_N=B^N\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and identical-particle reference measure $d\nu_N=d^{3N}q\,d^{3N}p/(N!h_*^{3N})$ of [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]]. Fix a softening length $a>0$ in metres and adopt the Hamiltonian
$$H_{N,a}(q,p)=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{|p_i|^2}{2m}-\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac{Gm^2}{\sqrt{|q_i-q_j|^2+a^2}},$$
which is the model defined in [[def-tgr-softened-gravity-finite-phase]]. The preparation assigns canonical weight $e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}$ relative to $\nu_N$. Its normalizer is $Z_B(\beta):=\int_{B^N\times\mathbb R^{3N}}e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}d\nu_N$. To check finiteness for this general region, enclose $B$ in a bounded cube $Q$ and apply [[lem-tgr-finite-gravitational-gibbs]] on $Q$ with the same parameters and Hamiltonian formula. Restriction of its nonnegative integral gives $Z_B\le Z_Q<\infty$. Moreover, the integrand is strictly positive everywhere, and $B^N$ times any positive-volume bounded momentum cube has positive measure, so $Z_B>0$. Thus the density $p_\beta=Z_B^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,a}}$ is normalized. These are mathematical consequences of the specified weight, not proofs of the physical preparation. For box instances, the further variational and response conclusions are stated in [[pthm-tgr-regulated-gravity-canonical-equilibrium]]. Confinement specifies the finite position region; no wall regularity or wall dynamics is used in this calculation.

Within this formulation, $N,m,G,a,B,h_*$ and $\beta$ are fixed model/preparation inputs. The displayed $H_{N,a}$ is the defined effective Hamiltonian; $Z_N$, the normalized density, mean energy, entropy and response are derived mathematical quantities. Their definition does not make them universal properties of gravitating matter.

This is an adopted effective Newtonian statistical model in a stated weak-field, slow-motion regime. The unbounded momentum domain is part of the canonical mathematical preparation and does not give a uniform speed bound on every point in its support. The postulate asserts neither dynamical equilibration, an observed gravitating gas, nor stability of a self-consistently gravitating relativistic solution.

items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
In SI units, take two labelled masses $m_1,m_2>0$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, positions $q_1,q_2$ in a bounded box $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ with nonempty interior, momenta $p_1,p_2$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $G>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. Fix $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$ as the phase-action reference and $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, with the unit conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]] and [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]]. The labelled-pair phase space is $\Gamma_{12}=B^2\times\mathbb R^6$ with reference measure
$$d\nu_{12}=h_*^{-6}\,d^3q_1\,d^3q_2\,d^3p_1\,d^3p_2.$$
On the off-diagonal domain $q_1\ne q_2$, adopt the unregulated point Hamiltonian
$$H^{\rm pt}_{12}(q,p)=\frac{|p_1|^2}{2m_1}+\frac{|p_2|^2}{2m_2}-\frac{Gm_1m_2}{|q_1-q_2|}.$$
Attempt canonical sampling with weight $e^{-\beta H^{\rm pt}_{12}}$, but do not assume its integral is finite or that the normalized probability law exists. If $m_1=m_2$, the identical-particle reference measure of [[def-tgr-gravitating-phase-reference]] is $d\nu_{12}/2$; this constant convention does not alter whether the integral converges.

The masses, $G$, box, action reference and $\beta$ are fixed inputs of this attempted model; $H^{\rm pt}_{12}$ is defined by the formula. A finite partition function or probability law is not a primitive input and is not postulated.

This is a distinct unregulated model, not the softened preparation with $a$ set to zero after normalization. Arbitrarily small separations are not asserted to remain in a controlled Newtonian weak-field regime. The attempted weight is a model specification, not a reported physical preparation or an assertion of successful thermalization.

items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Use positive masses $m_1,m_2$ in $\mathrm{kg}$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, $A=Gm_1m_2>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$, relative position $q\in\mathbb R^3$ in metres, relative momentum $p\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and action reference $h_*>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Fix $r_0>0$ and $R>16r_0$. Adopt the relative phase region and Hamiltonian of [[def-tgr-regulated-kepler-shell-law]]:
$$\Gamma_{\rm rel}=\{(q,p):r_0\le|q|\le R,\ p\in\mathbb R^3\},\qquad d\nu_{\rm rel}=h_*^{-3}d^3q\,d^3p,\qquad h(q,p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2\mu}-\frac A{|q|}.$$
There are no center-of-mass variables and no identical-particle factor in this relative phase convention. Adopt a canonical preparation at inverse energy $\beta>0$ with $T_K=(k_B\beta)^{-1}$ and density $p_\beta(q,p)=Z_{\rm rel}(\beta)^{-1}e^{-\beta h(q,p)}$ relative to $d\nu_{\rm rel}$ on all of $\Gamma_{\rm rel}$. Its finite positive normalizer and normalized density follow from [[lem-tgr-relative-shell-canonical-response]]. Since $h$ is finite throughout this domain, the density is positive for arbitrarily large momentum magnitudes. This is a fixed relative-shell effective Newtonian model, distinct from the microcanonical preparation and Gibbs-volume entropy convention in [[post-tgr-kepler-microcanonical-volume-preparation]].

Here $m_1,m_2,G,r_0,R,h_*$ and $\beta$ are fixed inputs; the reduced mass $\mu$, coupling product $A$, and Hamiltonian $h$ are the specified derived constructions. The partition function, density, temperature parameter and response are derived within this selected preparation.

Because canonical momenta are unbounded, this preparation does not have the whole-ensemble slow-motion bound imposed on the separate bounded-energy microcanonical branch. The postulate makes no claim that either distribution is dynamically reached or empirically observed.

items.title: Finite static fermion-mode trace and occupation identity
items.design_state: Batch-local finite-mode prerequisite; full choice-free proof and actual interface recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Let $M\ge0$ be an integer, let $E_1,\ldots,E_M\in\mathbb R$, $\beta>0$, and $\mu\in\mathbb R$. Define the finite index set $\mathcal N_M=\{0,1\}^M$ and the finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H_M=\mathbb C^{\mathcal N_M}$ with orthonormal basis $|n_1,\ldots,n_M\rangle$. Define diagonal operators $H$ and $N$ on this basis by
$$H|\mathbf n\rangle=\left(\sum_{j=1}^M E_jn_j\right)|\mathbf n\rangle,\qquad N|\mathbf n\rangle=\left(\sum_{j=1}^M n_j\right)|\mathbf n\rangle.$$
For a matrix on $\mathcal H_M$, trace means the finite sum of its diagonal entries in this basis. Then
$$\Xi=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta(H-\mu N)}=\prod_{j=1}^M\left(1+e^{-\beta(E_j-\mu)}\right)\in(0,\infty).$$
The normalized diagonal state with weights $\Xi^{-1}e^{-\beta(\sum_j E_jn_j-\mu\sum_jn_j)}$ has, for each $1\le j\le M$, occupation mean
$$\langle n_j\rangle=\frac{1}{e^{\beta(E_j-\mu)}+1}.$$
For $M=0$, the empty product and trace are $1$, and there are no occupation marginals. This is a finite-dimensional algebraic identity and uses no choice principle, curved-space spectrum, or gravitational field equation.

items.title: Fixed static ideal gas or finite fermion regulator preparation
items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
For the classical branch, prescribe a smooth static metric on a neighborhood of $I_{x^0}\times\overline B$, where $I_{x^0}\subset\mathbb R$ is an open interval and $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ is an open bounded coordinate box with compact closure and positive volume:
$$g=-\mathcal N(x)^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(x)dx^i dx^j,\qquad x^0=ct.$$
Here $h_{ij}$ is a smooth positive-definite spatial metric whose eigenvalues are bounded above and away from zero, and the dimensionless lapse satisfies $0<\mathcal N_0\le\mathcal N(x)\le\mathcal N_1<\infty$. The static chart and observer congruence are distinct objects: with $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$, the static unit observer is $u=\mathcal N^{-1}\xi$, satisfying $g(u,u)=-1$, under the conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. This geometry is prescribed and is not assumed to solve an Einstein equation with gas stress as source.

Take particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, $c>0$ in metres per second, orthonormal momentum $\hat p\in\mathbb R^3$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and adopt the massive-particle dispersion function $E(\hat p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p|^2}$ in joules as a model input. The Killing energy is the derived function $H_K(x,\hat p)=\mathcal N(x)E(\hat p)$, and the action reference $h_*>0$ is in joule-seconds. For a classical ideal gas with no interparticle potential and inverse Killing-energy parameter $\beta_K>0$ in inverse joules, choose exactly one of these alternatives: (i) a fixed-particle canonical branch with an integer $M\ge1$ and the $1/M!$ phase-counting convention; or (ii) a grand-canonical branch with dimensionless fugacity $z>0$, in which particle number is summed using the same $1/M!$ convention. The finite proper-phase one-particle integral and the corresponding fixed-particle and grand-canonical normalizers are supplied by [[lem-tgr-static-gas-finite-normalization]]. If a Killing-normalized chemical parameter $\mu_K$ in joules is used for the classical gas, it belongs to the grand-canonical branch and is related by $z=e^{\beta_K\mu_K}$; the fixed-particle branch has no fugacity parameter. There is no interaction term or gas-induced change of the metric in either branch.

As a distinct finite quantum regulator, one may instead specify a finite mode set $J=\{1,\ldots,M\}$, $M\ge0$, positive dimensionless lapse values $\mathcal N_j$, and momenta $\hat p_j\in\mathbb R^3$. Adopt mode energies $E_j=\mathcal N_j\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p_j|^2}$, canonical parameter $\beta_K>0$ in inverse joules, and chemical-potential parameter $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ in joules, together with the finite occupation basis $n_j\in\{0,1\}$. The associated finite trace and occupation identity are given by [[lem-tgr-finite-static-mode-occupation-trace]]. This is an explicitly supplied spectral cutoff, not a claim that arbitrary curved spacetime has these modes. Neither branch reports an observation or asserts actual thermalization.

The metric $h_{ij}$, lapse $\mathcal N$, region, $m,c,h_*$, canonical parameters and (in the finite-mode branch) the mode list are supplied inputs. The local energy, Killing-energy weight, partition functions, normalized state, local densities and response identities are derived constructions under the stated mathematical results; no universal equation of state or metric backreaction is assumed.

items.title: Constructed static gas redshift and hydrostatics
items.design_state: Batch 71 authoring draft; exact claim, dependencies, scope and conditional proof are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the prescribed static background in [[post-tgr-fixed-static-gas-preparation]] and consider its two alternative classical branches. Let
$$Z_1(\beta_K)=\int_B\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-\beta_K\mathcal N(x)E(\hat p)}\frac{dV_h(x)\,d^3\hat p}{h_*^3},\qquad dV_h=\sqrt{\det(h_{ij}(x))}\,d^3x.$$
Then $0<Z_1<\infty$. In the fixed-particle canonical branch, for the selected integer $M\ge1$, the normalizer is $Z_M=Z_1^M/M!$. In the grand-canonical branch, for dimensionless fugacity $z>0$, the normalizer is $\Xi=e^{zZ_1}$.

For either classical branch, define its coefficient $\alpha$ by $\alpha=M/Z_1$ in the fixed-particle branch and $\alpha=z$ in the grand-canonical branch. Its proper local expected particle phase-space density is
$$f_\alpha(x,\hat p)=\alpha h_*^{-3}e^{-\beta_K\mathcal N(x)E(\hat p)}.$$
Define proper local number density $n=\int f_\alpha\,d^3\hat p$, energy density $\varepsilon=\int E f_\alpha\,d^3\hat p$, and isotropic pressure $P=\frac13\int\hat p\cdot\nabla_{\hat p}E\,f_\alpha\,d^3\hat p$. With $T_K=(k_B\beta_K)^{-1}$, both branches satisfy
$$T_{\rm loc}(x)=\frac{T_K}{\mathcal N(x)},\qquad P=nk_BT_{\rm loc},\qquad \partial_iP=-(\varepsilon+P)\partial_i\log\mathcal N.$$
Only in the grand-canonical branch, if $z=e^{\beta_K\mu_K}$ for a Killing-normalized chemical parameter $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$ measured in joules, rewriting the local weight as $e^{-\beta_K\mathcal N(E-\mu_{\rm loc})}$ gives $\mu_{\rm loc}=\mu_K/\mathcal N$.

In the finite fermion-mode branch, let $E_j=\mathcal N_j\epsilon_j$ with $\epsilon_j=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\hat p_j|^2}$, $\mathcal N_j>0$, $\beta_K>0$, and $\mu_K\in\mathbb R$. The normalized diagonal state has
$$\langle n_j\rangle=\frac{1}{e^{\beta_K(E_j-\mu_K)}+1}=\frac{1}{e^{\beta_j(\epsilon_j-\mu_j)}+1},\qquad \beta_j=\beta_K\mathcal N_j,\quad \mu_j=\frac{\mu_K}{\mathcal N_j}.$$
Both conclusions are conditional model deductions on the fixed background or finite supplied mode set. They assert no Einstein equation, gas backreaction, arbitrary curved-space spectrum, or observed equilibrium.

items.title: Half-capacity bath attracts the selected exchange state
items.design_state: Batch 72 authoring draft; exact claim, current suppliers and complete argument are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
At a selected subsystem state with $T_*>0$ and $C_G<0$, choose the finite bath capacity $C_b=|C_G|/2$ and bath energy $E_b=E_0+C_bT_*$. In the adopted scalar exchange model, the common-temperature state is a strict local entropy maximum and is locally exponentially attracting; its entropy curvature is
$$S_{\rm tot}''(x_*)=-\frac1{T_*^2|C_G|}<0.$$
items.physical_scope: A single common-temperature point of the adopted finite-bath scalar exchange model with C_b=|C_G|/2; no causal transport or generic star-stability claim.

items.title: Smooth null screen and subextremal Kerr–Newman parameter family
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the metric-selected connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth future timelike vector field defining the time orientation; it is not a coordinate frame or a tetrad.

A **smooth null hypersurface** is a smooth embedded three-dimensional submanifold $H\subset\mathcal M$ such that, at every $p\in H$, the restriction of $g_p$ to $T_pH$ has a one-dimensional radical
$$L_p:=\{v\in T_pH:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for every }w\in T_pH\}.$$
Write $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathcal M$ for the inclusion, and let $\pi:T\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ be the tangent-bundle projection. A smooth vector field $V$ along $H$ means a smooth map $V:H\to T\mathcal M$ with $\pi\circ V=i$, equivalently a smooth section of
$$i^*T\mathcal M=\{(p,v):p\in H,\ v\in T_p\mathcal M\}.$$
For a smooth tangent field $X$ on $H$, the notation $\nabla_XV$ means $(i^*\nabla)_XV$, using the pullback connection of [[def-pullback-connection]] for the ambient metric-selected connection $\nabla$; its prescription in a pulled-back frame and frame-independent well-definedness are given by [[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. It agrees with restricting $\nabla_{\widetilde X}\widetilde V$ for any local smooth ambient extensions when $V$ and $X$ are restricted to $H$. Such extensions exist in the slice coordinates of [[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]] by extending coordinate coefficients smoothly off the slice. For tangent $X,Y$, extending their tangential coordinate coefficients independently of the transverse coordinate and setting their transverse components to zero makes the ambient bracket restrict to the intrinsic bracket on $H$. Restricting the ambient metric-compatibility and torsion-free identities therefore gives, for tangent $X,Y$ on $H$ and fields $V,W$ along $H$,
$$Xg(V,W)=g(\nabla_XV,W)+g(V,\nabla_XW),\qquad \nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y].$$
Pullback functoriality along any integral curve $\gamma$ in $H$ identifies the curve derivative with the pullback of $i^*\nabla$; accordingly $\nabla_k k=0$ means the tangent field is parallel along its generator with this affine parameter.

A **smooth affine null generator field** on $H$ is a smooth vector field $k$ along $H$ such that $k_p$ is a nonzero future-directed section of $L_p$ and $\nabla_k k=0$ along $H$. Thus $k$ is both tangent and normal to $H$, and its integral-curve parameter is affine.

For each $p\in H$, the **screen space** is the quotient vector space
$$\mathcal S_p:=k_p^\perp/\mathbb R k_p,\qquad k_p^\perp:=\{v\in T_p\mathcal M:g_p(v,k_p)=0\}.$$
Its candidate **screen metric** is $\bar g_p([X],[Y]):=g_p(X,Y)$. The result [[lem-tgr-null-screen-quotient-positive]] establishes that these spaces form a smooth rank-two vector bundle over $H$ and that $\bar g$ is a well-defined positive-definite metric on it.

For smooth local screen sections represented by smooth fields $X,Y$ tangent to $H$, define the **screen deformation form**
$$B([X],[Y]):=g(\nabla_X k,Y).$$
The same lemma establishes that this form is well defined on the quotient. Its **expansion** is $\theta:=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar g}B$ and its **shear** is $\sigma:=B-\frac12\theta\bar g$. In the area theorem below, $B$ is proved symmetric, so $\sigma$ is a symmetric trace-free form on each screen space.

Independently, let
$$\mathcal P:=\{(m,a,q)\in\mathbb R^3:m>0,\ m^2>a^2+q^2\}.$$
These are real mathematical parameters with no physical units assigned here. On this open parameter domain set
$$s:=\sqrt{m^2-a^2-q^2},\quad r_+:=m+s,\quad D:=r_+^2+a^2,$$
$$A:=4\pi D,\quad j:=ma,\quad \kappa_{\rm KN}:=\frac{r_+-m}{D},\quad \Omega_{\rm KN}:=\frac{a}{D},\quad \Phi_{\rm KN}:=\frac{qr_+}{D}.$$
Because the radicand and $D$ are strictly positive on $\mathcal P$, these are smooth real-valued functions there: the repeated derivative formula for $x^{1/2}$ on $(0,\infty)$ and the chain rule are given in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], Facts [F2]. This definition assigns no geometric or thermodynamic interpretation to these functions and asserts no event-horizon existence, formation, uniqueness or thermodynamic-identification theorem.

items.title: The null screen quotient is a smooth positive two-plane
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $H\subset\mathcal M$ be a smooth null hypersurface, and let $k$ be a smooth affine null generator field on $H$, as defined in [[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]]. Then the screen spaces
$$\mathcal S_p=k_p^\perp/\mathbb R k_p,\qquad p\in H,$$
form a smooth rank-two real vector bundle. The formula
$$\bar g_p([X],[Y]):=g_p(X,Y)$$
is independent of the representatives $X,Y\in k_p^\perp$ and defines a positive-definite inner product on each fiber. The screen deformation form $B([X],[Y])=g(\nabla_Xk,Y)$ is also independent of the representatives and is a smooth bilinear form on the screen bundle.

items.title: Exact Schwarzschild horizon data at the zero-rotation KN point
items.statement:
In the selected smooth ingoing KN model of [[thm-emg-xs-kn-extension]], set $a=q=0$ and let $m=M>0$. The metric, time orientation field and potential reduce to
$$g=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma,\qquad N=\partial_v-\frac{1+f(r)^2}{2}\partial_r,\qquad \mathcal A_{\rm in}=0,\qquad f(r)=1-\frac{2m}{r}.$$
The hypersurface $H=\{r=2m\}$ is a null Killing horizon for $\chi=\partial_v$ in the exact vocabulary of [[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. Its generator is future-directed, its signed surface gravity is $\kappa_H=1/(4m)$, and its round sections have area $16\pi m^2$. The angular-velocity, potential and angular-momentum parameter functions of [[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]] are respectively $\Omega_{\rm KN}=0$, $\Phi_{\rm KN}=0$, and $j=0$ at this parameter point.

This is an exact geometric special case of the selected metric, not a uniqueness or formation theorem.

items.title: Null focusing and a restricted smooth future area theorem
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal M,g,N)$, a smooth null hypersurface $H\subset\mathcal M$, its smooth affine future null generator field $k$, screen metric $\bar g$, screen deformation form $B$, expansion $\theta$, and shear $\sigma$ be as in [[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the smooth manifold structures, partition of unity and intrinsic density integrals used below. Let $S_0\subset H$ be a compact smooth embedded two-dimensional submanifold such that $g_x|_{T_xS_0}$ is positive definite for every $x\in S_0$ (the meaning of “spacelike” here) and
$$T_xH=T_xS_0\oplus\mathbb Rk_x\qquad(x\in S_0),$$
which defines transversality to $k$. Let $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$. Suppose there is a smooth map
$$\Phi:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times S_0\to H$$
such that $\Phi(\lambda_0,x)=x$, $\partial_\lambda\Phi(\lambda,x)=k_{\Phi(\lambda,x)}$, and, for each $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, $\Phi_\lambda:=\Phi(\lambda,\cdot)$ is an embedding with compact image $S_\lambda$ whose induced metric is positive definite, meaning $g_y(v,v)>0$ for every $y\in S_\lambda$ and every nonzero $v\in T_yS_\lambda$. Thus each $S_\lambda$ is spacelike, the same affine parameter runs along each generator for all future values, and the smooth embedded cross-sections persist for the entire half-line. Assume also
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{\Phi(\lambda,x)}(k,k)\ge0\qquad(\lambda\ge\lambda_0,\ x\in S_0).$$
Then $\theta\ge0$ everywhere on every $S_\lambda$. Let $q_\lambda:=\Phi_\lambda^*g$ be the induced Riemannian metric on $S_0$, let $\mu_{q_\lambda}$ be its Riemannian volume density, and define
$$A(\lambda):=\int_{S_0}\mu_{q_\lambda}=\int_{S_\lambda}\mu_{g|_{S_\lambda}},$$
where the second equality is the density change-of-variables formula for the embedding $\Phi_\lambda$. Then for every $\lambda>\lambda_0$,
$$A'(\lambda)=\int_{S_0}\theta(\Phi(\lambda,x))\,\mu_{q_\lambda}(x)=\int_{S_\lambda}\theta\,dA\ge0,$$
and $A(\lambda_2)\ge A(\lambda_1)$ whenever $\lambda_2\ge\lambda_1\ge\lambda_0$.

This is a conditional theorem about a complete smooth affine null congruence with persistent embedded cuts. It does not assert area monotonicity for an arbitrary null surface or an event-horizon theorem.
