items.title: Verified Kerr-Newman family first law and Smarr identity
items.statement:
On the strictly subextremal open parameter family $\mathcal P$ of [[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]], use the outer-horizon functions $(r_+,D,A,j,\kappa_{\rm KN},\Omega_{\rm KN},\Phi_{\rm KN})$ defined there. These functions give the exact selected-model outer-horizon data throughout $\mathcal P$: [[prop-emg-xs-kn-horizon-data]] verifies every point with $a^2+q^2>0$, and [[lem-tgr-schwarzschild-horizon-data]] verifies the Schwarzschild slice $m>0$, $a=q=0$. On $\mathcal P$ the following identities of one-forms and functions hold:
$$dm=\frac{\kappa_{\rm KN}}{8\pi}\,dA+\Omega_{\rm KN}\,dj+\Phi_{\rm KN}\,dq,$$
$$m=\frac{\kappa_{\rm KN}A}{4\pi}+2\Omega_{\rm KN}j+\Phi_{\rm KN}q.$$
For each fixed pair $(a_0,q_0)$, on the connected subfamily $I_{a_0,q_0}:=\{m>\sqrt{a_0^2+q_0^2}\}$ with $a=a_0$ and $q=q_0$, the correct pullback retains the angular-momentum work term $dj=a_0\,dm$:
$$\frac{\kappa_{\rm KN}}{8\pi}\,dA=\frac{r_+^2}{D}\,dm.$$
For every $b>0$ and $s_*\in\mathbb R$, define on $\mathcal P$
$$T_b:=b\kappa_{\rm KN},\qquad S_{b,s_*}:=\frac{A}{8\pi b}+s_*.$$
Their product on this fixed-$(a,q)$ subfamily is therefore $T_b\,dS_{b,s_*}=(r_+^2/D)\,dm$.

There is also a work-free subfamily for each fixed pair of angular-momentum and charge values $(j_0,q_0)\in\mathbb R^2$. Put
$$m_0:=\sqrt{\frac{q_0^2+\sqrt{q_0^4+4j_0^2}}2},\qquad J_{j_0,q_0}:=(m_0,\infty),\qquad \iota_{j_0,q_0}(m):=(m,j_0/m,q_0).$$
This is a smooth parametrization into $\mathcal P$ of the connected subfamily with $j=j_0$ and $q=q_0$. On this subfamily $dj=dq=0$, $\kappa_{\rm KN}>0$, and
$$dm=\frac{\kappa_{\rm KN}}{8\pi}\,dA=T_b\,dS_{b,s_*}.$$
All functions in these subfamily identities mean their pullbacks by the indicated parametrizations. On each of the two types of subfamily, distinct positive $b$ and distinct offsets give distinct real-valued functions, so the geometric first-law product alone fixes neither this temperature scale nor the absolute entropy offset. These are mathematical functions; no operational temperature, physical entropy, quantum calibration, or process statement is asserted.

items.title: Schwarzschild and charged endpoint algebra
items.statement:
Take the nonrotating slice $a=0$ of the parameter family in [[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]].

- If $q=0$ and $m>0$, then $r_+=2m$, $D=4m^2$, $A=16\pi m^2$, $\kappa_{\rm KN}=1/(4m)$, and $j=\Omega_{\rm KN}=\Phi_{\rm KN}=0$. The local horizon data are exactly those proved in [[lem-tgr-schwarzschild-horizon-data]]. The first-law identity becomes $dm=\kappa_{\rm KN}\,dA/(8\pi)$, and the Smarr identity becomes $m=\kappa_{\rm KN}A/(4\pi)$.
- If $q^2<m^2$, put $s=\sqrt{m^2-q^2}$ and $r_+=m+s$. Then $D=r_+^2$, $A=4\pi r_+^2$, $\kappa_{\rm KN}=s/r_+^2$, $\Phi_{\rm KN}=q/r_+$, and $j=\Omega_{\rm KN}=0$. The family identities reduce to $dm=\kappa_{\rm KN}\,dA/(8\pi)+\Phi_{\rm KN}\,dq$ and $m=\kappa_{\rm KN}A/(4\pi)+\Phi_{\rm KN}q$.
- At the boundary $q^2=m^2$ with $m>0$, the exact double-root supplier gives $r_+=m$, $D=m^2$, $A=4\pi m^2$, $\kappa_{\rm KN}=0$, and $\Phi_{\rm KN}=q/m$. This is a boundary value, not an assertion about attaining the extremal parameter in a physical process.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use Euclidean Lebesgue measure. Let $m\ge0$. For $m=0$ take $\mathbb R^0$ to be a singleton with measure $1$. For each sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$ let $d_\epsilon:\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth and real-valued. Assume that for every compact $V\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ and every $R>0$ there are constants $c,C,M,\epsilon_0>0$ such that, on $V\times[-R,R]$ and for $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$,
$$c\le d_\epsilon(v,s)\le C,\qquad |\partial_s d_\epsilon(v,s)|+|\partial_s^2d_\epsilon(v,s)|\le M.$$
For $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ set $\widehat\varphi(k)=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(s)e^{-iks}\,ds$ and define $B$ by
$$\langle B,\varphi\rangle:=\int_0^\infty k\widehat\varphi(k)\,dk.$$
For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ write $\widehat\psi(v,k)=\int_{\mathbb R}\psi(v,s)e^{-iks}\,ds$ and define $K$ by
$$\langle K,\psi\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^m}\int_0^\infty k\widehat\psi(v,k)\,dk\,dv.$$
Then $B$ and $K$ are distributions, $B$ is the lower boundary denoted $-(s-i0)^{-2}$, and $K=1\otimes B$ in the explicitly defined pairing above. The smooth kernels
$$K_\epsilon(v,s):=-\bigl(s-i\epsilon d_\epsilon(v,s)\bigr)^{-2}$$
converge to $K$ in the distributional sense: $\int K_\epsilon(v,s)\psi(v,s)\,dv\,ds\to\langle K,\psi\rangle$ for every such $\psi$. When $s$ and $\epsilon$ carry units of length, $d_\epsilon$ is dimensionless.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2((0,\infty),dk;\mathbb C),\qquad \langle h,q\rangle_2=\int_0^\infty\overline{h(k)}q(k)\,dk,$$
using the second-variable-linear convention. For
$f\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ define
$$h_f(k)=\sqrt{\frac{k}{4\pi}}\int_{\mathbb R}f(U)e^{ikU}\,dU\quad(k>0).$$
Then $h_f,h_{\bar f}\in\mathcal H$, and $f\mapsto h_f$ is continuous on each fixed-compact-support test space. With the bosonic Fock conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], define on its finite-particle domain
$$J(f)=a(h_{\bar f})+a^\dagger(h_f).$$
This is a complex-linear operator-valued distribution on that invariant domain. For real $f$, its closure is $\overline{J(f)}=\sqrt2\,\Phi(h_f)$, where $\Phi(h_f)$ is the closed Segal field of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]; the corresponding Weyl one-parameter group has generator $i\Phi(h_f)$. The vacuum two-point form is positive type and has boundary kernel
$$C(s)=-\frac{1}{4\pi(s-i0)^2},$$
where $s-i0$ means the distributional limit from $s-i\epsilon$, $\epsilon\downarrow0$.

For $\kappa>0$ with units of inverse length, let $u,U$ have units of length and set
$$U_\kappa(u)=-\kappa^{-1}e^{-\kappa u},\qquad u_\kappa(U)=-\kappa^{-1}\log(-\kappa U)\quad(U<0).$$
For $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ put $f_g(U)=g(u_\kappa(U))$ for $U<0$ and $f_g(U)=0$ for $U\ge0$, and define $j_\kappa(g)=J(f_g)$. The zero extension is smooth and compactly supported. Its vacuum covariance is the positive-type distribution
$$C_\kappa(s)=-\frac{\kappa^2}{16\pi}\,\operatorname{csch}^2\!\left(\frac{\kappa}{2}(s-i0)\right).$$
Here the notation is fixed as follows: for $b=\kappa/2$, set $Y_b(s)=\sinh(bs)/b$. Since $Y_b'(s)=\cosh(bs)>0$ and $Y_b(s)\to\pm\infty$ as $s\to\pm\infty$, it is a smooth increasing diffeomorphism. Define $\operatorname{csch}^2(b(s-i0)):=b^{-2}Y_b^*((y-i0)^{-2})$, where
$$\langle Y_b^*T,\varphi\rangle:=\left\langle T,\varphi(Y_b^{-1}(y))(Y_b^{-1})'(y)\right\rangle.$$
This is a one-dimensional chiral test-coordinate model. It asserts no restriction of a four-dimensional field to a null curve.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A,b>0$, put $\beta=\pi/b$ and $L=A/b^2$, and define the analytic kernel
$$C(z)=-A\operatorname{csch}^2(bz),\qquad \operatorname{csch}w=1/\sinh w.$$
Use the angular-frequency convention
$$\widehat\varphi(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(s)e^{-i\omega s}\,ds,\qquad \varphi(s)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat\varphi(\omega)e^{i\omega s}\,d\omega$$
for Schwartz functions $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$, where Schwartz space has seminorms $\sup_s|s^m\varphi^{(n)}(s)|$ and a tempered distribution is a continuous complex-linear functional on that space. Define its Fourier transform by the bilinear pairing $\langle\widehat T,\varphi\rangle=\langle T,\widehat\varphi\rangle$; test functions are not conjugated.

For $0<\epsilon<\beta$, $C_\epsilon(s)=C(s-i\epsilon)$ is a smooth $L^1$ function. These regularizations have a limit $C_{A,b}\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, denoted $-A\operatorname{csch}^2(b(s-i0))$. The kernel is holomorphic on $-\beta<\operatorname{Im}z<0$, has period $i\beta$, and its tested boundary values obey
$$C(s-i\beta+i0)=C(-s-i0).$$
The Fourier transform of $C_{A,b}$ is the continuous nonnegative function
$$S_{A,b}(\omega)=\frac{2\pi(A/b^2)\omega}{e^{\pi\omega/b}-1},\qquad S_{A,b}(0)=\frac{2\pi L}{\beta}=\frac{2A}{b}.$$
In particular $S_{A,b}(-\omega)=e^{\beta\omega}S_{A,b}(\omega)$ for $\omega>0$. The zero-frequency value is the removable limit, and the boundary and Fourier assertions are distributional, not pointwise integrals at a double pole.

If the coordinate has a specified unit, $s,z,\beta,\epsilon$ have that unit and $b,\omega$ its reciprocal. If $A$ has covariance units, $L$ has those units times the square of the coordinate unit and $S_{A,b}$ has those units times the coordinate unit.

In particular, for $\kappa>0$ in inverse length, take $A=\kappa^2/(16\pi)$ and $b=\kappa/2$. Then $L=1/(4\pi)$, $\beta=2\pi/\kappa$, and $C_{A,b}$ is precisely the tested chiral covariance $C_\kappa$ of [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Its spectrum and detailed balance are
$$S_\kappa(\omega)=\frac{\omega}{2(e^{2\pi\omega/\kappa}-1)},\qquad S_\kappa(0)=\frac{\kappa}{4\pi},\qquad S_\kappa(-\omega)=e^{2\pi\omega/\kappa}S_\kappa(\omega)\quad(\omega>0).$$
Here $C_\kappa$ has units of inverse length squared and $S_\kappa$ inverse length. This is a two-point strip and detailed-balance statement, including the specified chiral current as a specialization. It does not assert a norm-continuous $C^*$-algebra KMS dynamics or an exact detector transition probability.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $u$ be a length coordinate measured in metres, let $\kappa>0$ have units of inverse metres, and let $b>0$ be dimensionless; set $u'=u/b$ and $\kappa'=b\kappa$. Write $\beta=2\pi/\kappa$ and $\beta'=2\pi/\kappa'$ for the corresponding strip widths, measured in metres. Here “generator frequency” means only the angular Fourier-dual parameter: for the convention $\widehat g(\omega)=\int g(u)e^{-i\omega u}\,du$, $\omega$ has units of inverse metres and is not the eigenvalue of a separately asserted operator generator. To express it using an energy parameter, take $E>0$ in joules and a fixed formal $\sigma>0$ in joule-metres, and define $\omega=E/\sigma$; no physical energy or clock identification is assumed. For a primed parameter $E'>0$ in joules define $\omega'=E'/\sigma$. Matching the phase means $\omega'u'=\omega u$ for every $u\in\mathbb R$, and holds exactly when $E'=bE$, equivalently $\omega'=b\omega$. For $g'\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ define the transformed current by $j'(g')=j_\kappa(g'(\cdot/b))$. If $j_\kappa$ is represented by a regular density, changing variables $u=bu'$ in this test pairing gives $j'(u')=b j_\kappa(bu')$; the same formula defines the density transformation distributionally. For $\varphi'\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$, the corresponding two-point test pairing transforms as $\langle C',\varphi'\rangle=\langle C_\kappa,b\varphi'(\cdot/b)\rangle$, equivalently $C'=b^2C_\kappa(b\,\cdot)$ as a distribution. Thus the covariance retains its chiral form, the spectrum acquires the factor $b$, and $\beta'\omega'=\beta\omega$, so the detailed-balance exponent is unchanged. This is a coordinate and parameter identity within the mathematical model; no physical clock normalization or temperature assignment is included.

items.title: Constructed timelike smear and massless accelerated spectrum
items.design_state: Local shell restriction, field domain, regulated covariance, and inertial spectrum are proved; the accelerated spectrum is conditional on the actual batch-74 draft contour interface, rescaled with alpha=a/c^2 and u=cs. Both MHS02 items remain draft; their Step-1 records report ready, which records authoring readiness rather than proof acceptance.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the affine Minkowski
space, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, shell pairing
$p\circ x=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x$, and massless one-particle space
of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. Thus $x^0,\mathbf x$ have length units,
$\mathbf k$ has inverse-length units, the omitted shell apex $\mathbf k=0$
has measure zero, and
$$d\nu_0(\mathbf k)=\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf k|},\qquad \mathcal H_0=L^2(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\},d\nu_0;\mathbb C).$$
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open proper-time interval, with $\tau$ in
seconds, and let $\gamma=(\gamma^0,\boldsymbol\gamma)\in
C^\infty(I,\mathbb R^4)$ satisfy
$$\eta(\dot\gamma(\tau),\dot\gamma(\tau))=-c^2,\qquad \dot\gamma^0(\tau)>|\dot{\boldsymbol\gamma}(\tau)|$$
for all $\tau\in I$, where $c>0$ is in metres per second. This defines a
future-directed timelike curve parametrized by proper seconds. For
$f\in C_c^\infty(I;\mathbb C)$ define its curve-smearing amplitude by
$$K_\gamma f(\mathbf k)=\int_I f(\tau) e^{i(|\mathbf k|\gamma^0(\tau)-\mathbf k\cdot\boldsymbol\gamma(\tau))}\,d\tau.$$
Then $K_\gamma f\in\mathcal H_0$, and on every fixed compact support set the
map $f\mapsto K_\gamma f$ is continuous in the test-function topology. If
$f$ has units metres per second, then $K_\gamma f$ has units metres and its
$\mathcal H_0$ norm is dimensionless. For real $f$, define the actual
finite-particle-domain field
$$\Phi_\gamma(f)=a(K_\gamma f)+a^\dagger(K_\gamma f)$$
using the bosonic Fock space and creation/annihilation conventions of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. It is symmetric on the finite-particle
domain and has the self-adjoint Segal closure supplied by
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. Its vacuum covariance on real compact tests is
the well-defined pairing $\langle K_\gamma f,K_\gamma g\rangle_2$. This
construction is an additional temporal smearing of the massless shell; it
does not define a point field or an interaction.

For $a>0$ in metres per second squared, put $\ell=c^2/a$ and define the
uniformly accelerated curve on $I=\mathbb R$ by
$$\gamma_a(\tau)=\bigl(\ell\sinh(a\tau/c),\ell\cosh(a\tau/c),0,0\bigr).$$
It has proper acceleration magnitude $a$. The restriction of the massless
Minkowski-vacuum covariance constructed above is stationary and, in the
distributional boundary-value sense on the real line, is
$$C_a(s)=-\frac{a^2}{16\pi^2c^4}\,\operatorname{csch}^2\!\left(\frac{a(s-i0)}{2c}\right).$$
Here $\operatorname{csch}z=1/\sinh z$, and the displayed expression means
the limit of the smooth damped shell pairings against compact smooth tests;
no product or pullback of point-field distributions is assumed. With the
angular-frequency convention
$$S_a(\nu)=\mathcal F_{-}C_a(\nu),\qquad \mathcal F_{-}C(\nu)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-i\nu s}C(s)\,ds$$
interpreted distributionally, the local conclusion about the spectrum is conditional on the current
batch-74 draft suppliers [[lem-tgr-thermal-contour-spectrum]] and its
prerequisite [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Their carriers exist in the
batch-74 manifest, and both items have status `draft`. The current run's
Step-1 records report `ready` for both items; this is authoring-readiness
evidence, not proof acceptance. The contour item's actual statement uses a length
coordinate and an inverse-length parameter (renamed from its $\kappa$ to
$\alpha$ here); the proof below uses
$\alpha=a/c^2$ and $u=cs$, for which the covariance obeys
$C_a(s)=\pi^{-1}C_\alpha(cs)$. Under the contour item's exact conditional
Fourier formula and this rescaling,
$$S_a(\nu)=\frac{\nu}{2\pi c^2\bigl(e^{2\pi c\nu/a}-1\bigr)},\qquad S_a(0)=\frac{a}{4\pi^2c^3},\qquad S_a(-\nu)=e^{2\pi c\nu/a}S_a(\nu)\quad(\nu>0).$$
The continuous value at zero is the removable limit. $\nu$ has units
seconds$^{-1}$ and $S_a$ has units seconds per square metre; the spectral
claim remains conditional until both draft suppliers are accepted.

For comparison, on the inertial curve $\gamma_0(\tau)=(c\tau,0,0,0)$ the
same construction gives
$$C_0(s)=-\frac{1}{4\pi^2c^2(s-i0)^2},\qquad S_0(\nu)=\frac{\max(-\nu,0)}{2\pi c^2}.$$
These are mathematical covariance and Fourier-transform statements in the
specified representation. They do not assert a measured spectrum or a
detector transition probability.

items.design_state: Finite-switch coefficient bound and defined two-state Markov solution are proved; accelerated uses remain conditional on the actual batch-74 draft contour item and its draft prerequisite, whose Step-1 records report ready without proof acceptance.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the massless accelerated
covariance $C_a$ and its conditional spectrum $S_a$ from
[[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]], with $a>0$ in metres per second
squared, $c>0$ in metres per second, and angular frequency in seconds$^{-1}$.
The conditional detailed-balance input is the actual Statement of the
current batch-74 draft [[lem-tgr-thermal-contour-spectrum]], reproduced in
[L1] below. Its declared prerequisite [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]] is also
a draft. The current run's Step-1 records report `ready` for both items;
these are authoring-readiness records, not proof acceptance. The inertial
pair $(C_0,S_0)$ is the unconditioned comparison from
[[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]]. Both spectra are continuous and
globally Lipschitz. The conventions are $S=\mathcal F_-C$ with kernel
$e^{-i\nu s}$ and $C$ paired bilinearly with Schwartz tests.

Let $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ be nonzero, let the switching
duration $\mathsf T>0$ be measured in seconds, and put
$$\widehat h(z)=\int_{\mathbb R}h(u)e^{-izu}\,du,\qquad K_h=\frac{1}{2\pi\|h\|_2^2}\int_{\mathbb R}|z|\,|\widehat h(z)|^2\,dz.$$
For either stationary pair $(C,S)=(C_a,S_a)$ or $(C_0,S_0)$ define the
switched coefficient
$$R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)=\left\langle C(s),e^{-i\nu s} \int_{\mathbb R}h(t/\mathsf T)h((t-s)/\mathsf T)\,dt\right\rangle.$$
Then $K_h<\infty$ and, for every $\nu\in\mathbb R$,
$$R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)=\frac{\mathsf T^2}{2\pi} \int_{\mathbb R}S(\omega)|\widehat h(\mathsf T(\nu-\omega))|^2\,d\omega,$$
so $R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)\ge0$, and
$$\left|\frac{R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)}{\mathsf T\|h\|_2^2}-S(\nu)\right| \le\frac{\operatorname{Lip}(S)K_h}{\mathsf T},\qquad \operatorname{Lip}(S)=\sup_{x\ne y}\frac{|S(x)-S(y)|}{|x-y|}<\infty.$$
This proves the leading switched coefficient limit and its explicit error;
it is not a convergence theorem for an all-order detector transition
probability or an exact infinite-time probability.

There is also the following separately defined two-state continuous-time
Markov model. Choose an energy $E>0$ in joules, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds,
$k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and a coupling $\gamma_d>0$ in square metres
per square second. For the accelerated spectrum set
$$r_+=\gamma_d S_a(E/\hbar),\qquad r_-=\gamma_d S_a(-E/\hbar).$$
These are positive rates in seconds$^{-1}$. Let $p(t)$ be the probability
of the excited state in the two-state chain with ground-to-excited rate
$r_+$ and excited-to-ground rate $r_-$. For $t\ge0$ and any initial probability $p(0)\in[0,1]$, then
$$p(t)=p_*+(p(0)-p_*)e^{-(r_++r_-)t},\qquad p_* =\frac{1}{1+e^{2\pi cE/(a\hbar)}}.$$
If the effective thermometer temperature $T_{\rm eff}>0$ is defined by
$p_*/(1-p_*)=e^{-E/(k_BT_{\rm eff})}$, then
$$T_{\rm eff}=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}.$$
This is an exact result for the specified Markov chain. It is not a weak
coupling or point-detector thermalization theorem.

items.design_state: Explicit switched-coefficient estimate and inertial-rate comparison; accelerated limit is conditional through the A-page items on the two unaccepted batch-74 draft suppliers.
items.statement:
Assume the conditional mathematical spectra and switched-coefficient bound
of [[lem-tgr-spectral-thermometer]], with $a>0$, $c>0$, and a real nonzero
$h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$. For each proper switching duration
$\mathsf T>0$ and excitation frequency $\nu>0$, define the normalized
accelerated coefficient
$$Q_{\mathsf T}^{(a)}(\nu)= \frac{R_{\mathsf T}^{(C_a)}(\nu)}{\mathsf T\|h\|_2^2}.$$
With
$$K_h=\frac{1}{2\pi\|h\|_2^2}\int_{\mathbb R}|z|\,|\widehat h(z)|^2\,dz<\infty,$$
the exact leading-coefficient estimate is
$$|Q_{\mathsf T}^{(a)}(\nu)-S_a(\nu)| \le\frac{\operatorname{Lip}(S_a)K_h}{\mathsf T}.$$
For the inertial covariance, the same definition gives
$$0\le\frac{R_{\mathsf T}^{(C_0)}(\nu)}{\mathsf T\|h\|_2^2} \le\frac{K_h}{2\pi c^2\mathsf T},$$
because $S_0(\nu)=0$ for $\nu>0$ and
$\operatorname{Lip}(S_0)=1/(2\pi c^2)$. Thus the inertial excitation
coefficient divided by duration tends to zero, while the accelerated one
tends to its conditional spectrum. These are finite-switch coefficient
statements; they do not claim an all-order detector probability, strict
nonzero response for every finite switch, or a measured outcome.

items.title: Exponential mode sums for the periodic photon box
items.design_state: Batch 76 local intermediate result added after prerequisite inspection; its complete proof and contract are on the assigned A page.
items.statement:
Let $L,\beta,\hbar,c>0$ be real parameters, set $a=2\pi\hbar c/L$, and for
$n\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ define
$$\epsilon_n=a|n|,\qquad q_n=e^{-\beta\epsilon_n},$$
where $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm. For $j\ge1$, the integer max-norm shell
$$\{n\in\mathbb Z^3:|n|_\infty=j\}$$
has $24j^2+2$ points. Consequently
$$\sup_{n\ne0}q_n=e^{-\beta a}<1,\qquad \sum_{n\ne0}q_n<\infty,\qquad \sum_{n\ne0}\epsilon_n^p q_n<\infty$$
for every integer $p\ge0$. In particular, the positive mode-energy sum
$$\sum_{n\ne0}\frac{\epsilon_n}{e^{\beta\epsilon_n}-1}$$
is finite. Repeating each mode twice for two polarization labels preserves all
these conclusions.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333 Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 20, photon-gas section

items.strategy: 1.1 The number of integer vectors with $|n|_\infty=j$ is $(2j+1)^3-(2j-1)^3=24j^2+2$. On this shell $j\le |n|\le\sqrt3j$, so $q_n\le e^{-\beta a j}$ and $\epsilon_n^p q_n\le (a\sqrt3)^p j^p e^{-\beta a j}$. The shell contributions are bounded by $C_p j^{p+2}e^{-\beta a j}$ for a finite constant $C_p$; the ratio of consecutive terms tends to $e^{-\beta a}<1$, so their series converges. [given, A1, algebra]

items.title: Planck integrals from Fourier Parseval
items.design_state: Batch 76 local intermediate result added after prerequisite inspection; its complete proof and contract are on the assigned A page.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The following improper integrals
converge and have the exact values
$$\int_0^\infty\frac{x^3}{e^x-1}\,dx=\frac{\pi^4}{15},\qquad \int_0^\infty x^2[-\log(1-e^{-x})]\,dx=\frac{\pi^4}{45}.$$

references.title: University of Mississippi PHY 727 course notes, Lecture 18: The Photon Gas
Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333 Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 20, photon-gas section

items.strategy: 1.1 On $[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]$ define the continuous periodic representative $F(y)=(2\pi y)^2$. Its normalized Fourier coefficients are $c_n=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}x^2e^{-inx}\,dx$ after the change $x=2\pi y$. Direct integration gives $c_0=\pi^2/3$; for $n\ne0$, two integrations by parts give $c_n=2(-1)^n/n^2$ because the first boundary term cancels at $x=\pm\pi$ and $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}e^{-inx}\,dx=0$. [given, algebra]

items.title: Photon-box energy and singular entropy Riemann limits
items.design_state: Batch 76 local intermediate result added after prerequisite inspection; its complete proof and contract are on the assigned A page.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. For $r>0$ define $f(r)=r/(e^r-1)$ and $g(r)=f(r)-\log(1-e^{-r})$, with $f(0)=1$. Let $|n|$ be the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb Z^3$. Then, as the dimensionless mesh $d\downarrow0$,
$$d^3\sum_{n\ne0}f(d|n|)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(|x|)\,d^3x,$$
$$d^3\sum_{n\ne0}g(d|n|)\longrightarrow\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(|x|)\,d^3x<\infty.$$
Both sums converge absolutely for each $d>0$. In addition, for every continuous compactly supported $\psi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$,
$$d^3\sum_{n\ne0}\psi(d|n|)\longrightarrow4\pi\int_0^\infty r^2\psi(r)\,dr.$$

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333 Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 20, photon-gas section
University of Mississippi PHY 727 course notes, Lecture 18: The Photon Gas

items.strategy: 1.1 For a continuous compactly supported $h:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$, the cubes $Q_{n,d}=dn+[-d/2,d/2]^3$ tile $\mathbb R^3$ up to boundaries of volume zero. Uniform continuity of $h$ bounds $|d^3\sum_nh(dn)-\int h|$ by the volume of one fixed enlarged support box times the modulus of continuity at $\sqrt3d/2$, which tends to zero. Taking $h(x)=\psi(|x|)$ proves the compactly supported radial limit; applying [F2] and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ from [F3] rewrites its integral as $4\pi\int_0^\infty r^2\psi(r)\,dr$. Omitting $n=0$ changes the sum by $d^3\psi(0)\to0$. [given, F2, F3, algebra]

items.title: Actual photon box trace and Planck energy/entropy flux
items.design_state: Batch 76 assigned inventory item; complete conditional argument and proof contract are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Fix $L,T,\hbar,c,k_B>0$ with SI units respectively metre, kelvin, joule-second, metre per second, and joule per kelvin. Let $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in inverse joules. The mathematical periodic-box mode set is $I=(\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\})\times\{1,2\}$, with two polarization labels and the enumeration by increasing max-norm shells and then lexicographic order; within each shell use lexicographic order on $(n,s)$. For $i=(n,s)$ set $\epsilon_i=\hbar c(2\pi/L)|n|$ in joules and $\omega_n=2\pi c|n|/L$ in inverse seconds. The zero wavevector is excluded and no zero-point energy is included.

Let $\Omega_B$ be the finite-support maps $m:I\to\mathbb N_0$, set $E(m)=\sum_{i\in I}\epsilon_i m_i$, and let $\mathcal H_B=\ell^2(\Omega_B,\mathbb C)$ with its occupation basis. Define the nonnegative diagonal multiplier $H$ by $(Ha)_m=E(m)a_m$ on $D(H)=\{a\in\ell^2(\Omega_B,\mathbb C):\sum_m E(m)^2|a_m|^2<\infty\}$, so $H|m\rangle=E(m)|m\rangle$. For each $\gamma>0$ in inverse joules define the bounded positive diagonal multiplier $e^{-\gamma H}$ by $e^{-\gamma H}|m\rangle=e^{-\gamma E(m)}|m\rangle$, and set $Z_L(\gamma)=\sum_{m\in\Omega_B}e^{-\gamma E(m)}$; the proof shows this sum is finite and equals the operator trace $\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\gamma H})$. Set $q_n=e^{-\beta\epsilon_{(n,1)}}$, $Z_L=Z_L(\beta)$, $\rho_L=Z_L^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$, and $p_m=e^{-\beta E(m)}/Z_L$. Define the diagonal-state entropy by $S_L=-k_B\sum_{m\in\Omega_B}p_m\log p_m$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

The finite-box trace, energy and entropy are actual diagonal sums, not continuum mode integrals. The partition function $Z_L$ and occupations $q_n$ are dimensionless, $\rho_L$ has trace one, energy and $U_L$ have units joules, and $S_L$ has units joules per kelvin. The sums satisfy $Z_L=\prod_{n\ne0}(1-q_n)^{-2}<\infty$, $\rho_L$ is a positive trace-one trace-class operator, and every nonnegative integer energy moment under $\rho_L$ is finite. Define the everywhere-defined diagonal operator $B_L$ by
$(B_La)_m=p_mE(m)a_m$ for $a\in\mathcal H_B$. The proof shows that it
is bounded, positive and trace class, agrees with $\rho_LH$ on $D(H)$,
and equals $H\rho_L$ on all of $\mathcal H_B$. The notation
$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_LH)$ means $\operatorname{Tr}(B_L)$, the trace
of that unique bounded extension. Moreover,
$$U_L=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_LH)=2\sum_{n\ne0}\frac{\epsilon_{(n,1)}}{e^{\beta\epsilon_{(n,1)}}-1}<\infty.$$
The entropy is
$$S_L=k_B(\log Z_L+\beta U_L)=2k_B\sum_{n\ne0}\left[-\log(1-q_n)+\frac{\beta\epsilon_{(n,1)}q_n}{1-q_n}\right]<\infty.$$

With $u_L=U_L/L^3$ and $s_L=S_L/L^3$ in joules per cubic metre and joules per kelvin per cubic metre, respectively, their thermodynamic-volume limits at fixed $T$ exist. For every continuous compactly supported $\psi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$, the limiting spectral energy measure is
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{2}{L^3}\sum_{n\ne0}\frac{\hbar\omega_n}{e^{\beta\hbar\omega_n}-1}\psi(\omega_n)=\frac{\hbar}{\pi^2c^3}\int_0^\infty\frac{\omega^3\psi(\omega)}{e^{\beta\hbar\omega}-1}\,d\omega.$$
The integrated limits are
$$u=\lim_{L\to\infty}u_L=\frac{\pi^2k_B^4T^4}{15\hbar^3c^3},\qquad s=\lim_{L\to\infty}s_L=\frac{4u}{3T}.$$

In a separately specified isotropic freely streaming ray model, directions have uniform angular density $u/(4\pi)$ for energy and $s/(4\pi)$ for this coarse mode entropy on the unit sphere; each ray has velocity $c\hat n$. Define one-sided flux through a plane by integrating the outward normal velocity component over the outward hemisphere. Then $F=cu/4=\sigma T^4$ and $F_S=cs/4=(4/3)F/T$, where $F$ is in watts per square metre, $F_S$ in joules per kelvin per square metre per second, and $\sigma=\pi^2k_B^4/(60\hbar^3c^2)$ in watts per square metre per kelvin to the fourth power. This is a mathematical model deduction; it does not assert an observed blackbody, an equilibration mechanism, or a horizon-emission law.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333 Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 20, photon-gas section
University of Mississippi PHY 727 course notes, Lecture 18: The Photon Gas

items.strategy: 1.1 For $i=(n,s)$ with $n\ne0$, $|n|\ge1$, so $\epsilon_i\ge2\pi\hbar c/L>0$. Thus $q_i\le e^{-2\pi\beta\hbar c/L}<1$, and [F3] gives $\sum_{i\in I}q_i<\infty$ with the required strict supremum bound. [given, F3, algebra]

items.title: Exact ideal emitter mass ODE and entropy accounting
items.design_state: Batch 76 assigned inventory item; complete conditional argument and proof contract are recorded in batch evidence.
items.statement:
Assume the exact Planck energy and coarse entropy flux formulas of [[thm-tgr-photon-planck-flux]]. Fix model constants $G,c,\hbar,k_B>0$ in SI units, with units respectively $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Fix a normalization of the asymptotic time and energy reference, a dimensionless fraction $0<\eta\le1$, an initial mass $M_0>0$ in kilograms, a cutoff $0<M_{\min}<M_0$, and an entropy offset $S_0\in\mathbb R$ in joules per kelvin. Let $M(t)>0$ be a $C^1$ mass function on an interval containing $0$ and its first cutoff time, with $M(0)=M_0$. For each $M>0$ define the model quantities
$$r_H=\frac{2GM}{c^2},\qquad A_H=4\pi r_H^2,\qquad \kappa=\frac{c^2}{4GM},\qquad T_\infty=\frac{\hbar c\kappa}{2\pi k_B},\qquad S_B(M)=\frac{k_Bc^3A_H}{4G\hbar}+S_0.$$
Here $r_H$ is in metres, $A_H$ in square metres, $\kappa$ is the fixed-reference inverse-length parameter in inverse metres, $T_\infty$ is in kelvins, and $S_0$ is a fixed entropy offset in joules per kelvin. Adopt an effective far-field emitter with area $A_{\rm eff}=\eta A_H$ and power $P=A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_\infty^4$ in watts, where $\sigma$ is the coefficient in [[thm-tgr-photon-planck-flux]]. Adopt the mass-balance equation $c^2M'(t)=-P(t)$, with $t$ in seconds measured by the fixed asymptotic time parameter; terminate the model at the first time $M(t)=M_{\min}$. Then the exact solution until that cutoff is
$$M(t)=(M_0^3-3\alpha t)^{1/3},\qquad \alpha=\frac{\eta\hbar c^4}{15360\pi G^2},\qquad \tau=\frac{M_0^3-M_{\min}^3}{3\alpha}.$$
The parameter $\alpha$ has units $\mathrm{kg^3\,s^{-1}}$. The model exports energy $c^2(M_0-M_{\min})$ in joules through cutoff. Define its coarse exported entropy by $S_{\rm rad}(t)=\int_0^t(4/3)P(t')/T_\infty(t')\,dt'$, in joules per kelvin. Then
$$S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})>0.$$
$$S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=\frac43[S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})].$$
$$\Delta(S_B+S_{\rm rad})=\frac13[S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})]\ge0,$$
where $\Delta(S_B+S_{\rm rad})=S_B(M_{\min})+S_{\rm rad}(\tau)-S_B(M_0)$ and $S_{\rm rad}(0)=0$. This is an exact conditional calculation in the fixed-reference effective-area model. It is not a theorem about a material patch of a null horizon, an exact time-dependent Einstein solution, quantum backreaction, reference-independent Stefan emission, or a universal generalized second law.

$$S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_0/2)=\frac{3\pi k_BG M_0^2}{\hbar c},\quad S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=\frac{4\pi k_BG M_0^2}{\hbar c},\quad \Delta(S_B+S_{\rm rad})=\frac{\pi k_BG M_0^2}{\hbar c}.$$
The entropy offset cancels. This calculation stops at positive mass and asserts no endpoint at $M=0$ or physical generalized second law.

items.title: Restricted smooth horizon Einstein/NEC adoption
items.design_state: Authored draft; the planned scope and exact dependencies are recorded in batch-77 notes and cross-batch evidence.
items.statement:
Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N,o)$
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. The manifold
orientation is independent of the time orientation. On an open set $U\subseteq
M$, let $F$ be a smooth real two-form and use the SI constants and
length-coordinate convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. This adoption is
parameterized by any complete explicitly supplied named smooth classical
matter-model instance
$$\mathcal M=(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m)$$
of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]]. The model data are inputs, not
unspecified functions to be inferred from the field equation. They specify
the actual matter-field bundles and smooth configuration fields $\Psi$ in
$\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ on $U$, the exact equations and constraints
$\mathcal E_m[g,F;\Psi]=0$, all constitutive functions and parameters, and
the explicit current and symmetric-stress maps $\mathsf J_m$ and
$\mathsf T_m$. Any further domain, boundary or initial-data hypotheses of
that selected model are retained. A specialization must give these actual
equations and maps together with the model's name; providing only the symbols
$\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m$ or arbitrary smooth $j,T^m$ is not
such a specification.

For the supplied model, take an admitted smooth configuration
$\Psi\in\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ satisfying all of its equations and constraints,
and set
$$j:=\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi],\qquad T^m:=\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi].$$
Thus $j$ is a smooth vector field and $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant
two-tensor on the same domain. The postulate and the restricted area deduction
are uniform in these fully specified model data; they do not select one
constitutive law or restrict the range to source-free matter or dust. The
named zero-matter instance, when selected, is precisely $\mathcal M_0$ of
the equation-based supplier. No matter action or circle-representation
hypothesis is required for this model input.

Define
$$T_{ab}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab},\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),$$
where raised indices use $g^{-1}$ and $\mu_0>0$. Define
$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$ with the curvature
convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Adopt the smooth Maxwell equations
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, together with the equation-based
gravitational field law of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] on $U$:
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}T_{ab},$$
with constant $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $G_N>0$, and $c>0$.

For a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $H\subset U$ and a smooth
nowhere-zero future-directed null generator field $k$ along $H$, adopt the
null energy condition on this generator:
$$T_{ab}k^ak^b\ge0\qquad\text{at every point of }H.$$
Here $H$, $k$, and the screen variables are defined by
[[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]]; the displayed inequality is a physical
restriction on the selected classical stress and congruence. It is not a
consequence of the field equation and is not asserted for every quantum state.
For the restricted area result on this page, the chosen generator must also
have the smooth future flow and persistent compact spacelike cuts stated in
[[thm-tgr-smooth-null-area]]. This adoption neither constructs such a flow or
horizon nor asserts that every event horizon has those regularity and
completeness properties. No matter action, singular source, observational
claim, or thermodynamic entropy is included.
items.physical_scope: A restricted smooth classical Einstein–Maxwell model with the equation-based field law and the null energy condition for the specified future null generator. It does not construct matter or a horizon, and the energy condition is not asserted for every classical or quantum state.

items.title: Conditional restricted classical area increase
items.design_state: Authored draft; the planned scope and exact dependencies are recorded in batch-77 notes and cross-batch evidence.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and let $U\subseteq M$ be open. For any
complete explicitly supplied named smooth classical matter-model instance
$\mathcal M=(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m)$ of
[[post-tgr-smooth-horizon-energy-condition]], retain its specified matter-field
bundles, configuration fields, exact equations and constraints, constitutive
inputs, regularity, and additional domain or data hypotheses. Take a smooth
admitted configuration $\Psi\in\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ satisfying
$\mathcal E_m[g,F;\Psi]=0$ on $U$, and use the same source maps
$j=\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and $T^m=\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$. Assume the
equation-based Einstein–Maxwell equations and restricted total-stress null
energy condition of that postulate for this model and configuration. The
claim is uniform over these supplied named models, without requiring a
matter action or choosing a particular matter closure. Let $H\subset U$ be a
smooth embedded null hypersurface with a smooth nowhere-zero future null
generator field $k$ satisfying $\nabla_k k=0$. In the definitions of
[[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]], $k$ is affine and its screen expansion is
$\theta=\operatorname{tr}_{\bar g}B$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$S_0\subset H$ be a compact smooth embedded spacelike two-dimensional
submanifold transverse to $k$, and let $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$. Suppose a
smooth map
$$\Phi:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times S_0\to H$$
satisfies $\Phi(\lambda_0,x)=x$ and
$\partial_\lambda\Phi(\lambda,x)=k_{\Phi(\lambda,x)}$, with each
$\Phi_\lambda:=\Phi(\lambda,\cdot)$ an embedding whose image $S_\lambda$ is
compact and spacelike. Thus the same affine parameter runs for every future
value and the cuts persist without a caustic or endpoint on this domain. Define
the induced Riemannian metric $q_\lambda:=\Phi_\lambda^*g$ on $S_0$ and the
area
$$A_H(\lambda):=\int_{S_0}\mu_{q_\lambda}.$$
Then $\theta\ge0$ on every future cut,
$$A_H'(\lambda)=\int_{S_0}\theta(\Phi(\lambda,x))\,\mu_{q_\lambda}(x)=\int_{S_\lambda}\theta\,dA\ge0\qquad(\lambda>\lambda_0),$$
and $A_H(\lambda_2)\ge A_H(\lambda_1)$ whenever
$\lambda_2\ge\lambda_1\ge\lambda_0$.

This is a conditional deduction for the stated smooth classical model and
future-complete congruence. It makes no assertion about an arbitrary event
horizon, a rough null hypersurface, quantum energy conditions, or a horizon
entropy.

items.title: Physical KN family work and constancy
items.design_state: Authored draft; the planned scope and exact dependencies are recorded in batch-77 notes and cross-batch evidence.
items.statement:
Fix $G_N,c,\mu_0>0$ and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Let
$m_*>0$ be the selected SI mass parameter, $J\in\mathbb R$ the selected
angular-momentum parameter, and $Q_e\in\mathbb R$ the selected electric
charge parameter, with zero magnetic flux. Define the geometric length
parameters and field normalization by
$$m:=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad a:=\frac{J}{m_*c},\qquad q:=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad \alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}}.$$
Assume the strict subextremal condition $m^2>a^2+q^2$. Set
$$s:=\sqrt{m^2-a^2-q^2},\qquad r_+:=m+s,\qquad D:=r_+^2+a^2,\qquad A_H:=4\pi D.$$
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined in [[def-countable-choice]], the
choice convention inherited by the selected geometric flux parametrization;
no full Axiom of Choice is used.
In the selected smooth ingoing KN model, the outer Killing horizon has
generator
$$\chi:=\partial_v+\frac aD\Psi,$$
where $v$ is a length coordinate and $\Psi=X\partial_Y-Y\partial_X$ is
the smooth rotation field of the unit two-sphere. Normalize time by
$t=v/c$, and define
$$\Omega_{\rm SI}:=\frac{ca}{D},\qquad \kappa_{\rm acc}:=\frac{c^2s}{D},\qquad \Phi_{\rm SI}:=\frac{cq r_+}{\alpha D}.$$
Thus $c\chi=\partial_t+\Omega_{\rm SI}\Psi$; $\kappa_{\rm acc}$ is the
acceleration-unit surface gravity; and $\Phi_{\rm SI}$ is the voltage in
the displayed gauge, constant on the horizon cross-section and vanishing at
spatial infinity. The quantities $\Omega_{\rm SI}$,
$\kappa_{\rm acc}$, and $\Phi_{\rm SI}$ are constant on each fixed
cross-section because the selected horizon formulas depend only on the family
parameters. Let $E_{\rm par}:=m_*c^2$ be the energy-valued parameter
derived from the selected mass input. For ordinary differentials on the
strict physical parameter domain, with $G_N,c,\mu_0$ fixed, the exact family
identities are
$$dE_{\rm par}=\frac{\kappa_{\rm acc}c^2}{8\pi G_N}\,dA_H+\Omega_{\rm SI}\,dJ+\Phi_{\rm SI}\,dQ_e,$$
and
$$E_{\rm par}=\frac{\kappa_{\rm acc}c^2}{4\pi G_N}A_H+2\Omega_{\rm SI}J+\Phi_{\rm SI}Q_e.$$
The quantities have units $[E_{\rm par}]={\rm J}$,
$[A_H]={\rm m^2}$, $[\kappa_{\rm acc}]={\rm m\,s^{-2}}$,
$[\Omega_{\rm SI}]={\rm s^{-1}}$, and $[\Phi_{\rm SI}]={\rm V}$.
The joint Schwarzschild point $J=Q_e=0$ is included by the separate exact
Schwarzschild horizon-data supplier; the generic physical horizon theorem
itself states a nonzero-rotation-or-charge hypothesis.

These identities concern the selected stationary family and its stated
normalizations. They are not a dynamical-process first law, and
$E_{\rm par}$ is not identified here with ADM or Komar gravitational energy.
No operational temperature, physical entropy, Hawking calibration, or
extremal-boundary claim follows from this calculation.

items.physical_scope: Two selected effective models only: a one-dimensional exponential-coordinate chiral current and a massless Minkowski scalar sampled along a uniformly accelerated timelike curve. The adopted two-state rates are model inputs; this is not a general horizon, KMS, detector-transition, or empirical thermometer claim.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the mathematical context for the tested-current, Fourier and temporally smeared field constructions used below.

Use the length-coordinate, unit, and reference conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Adopt two distinct model branches.

**Reduced exponential-current branch.** Choose a constant $\kappa>0$ in inverse metres and a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on a declared domain in the TGR framework. The real parameter $u$, measured in metres, is the selected flow parameter for $\xi$; the reference event and normalization of this flow are fixed as part of the model. Set the exponential coordinate $U_\kappa(u)=-\kappa^{-1}e^{-\kappa u}$. Adopt the positive-chiral-current vacuum and tested current $j_\kappa$ constructed in [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Its mathematical two-point covariance is the tested boundary $C_\kappa$ there; use its angular-frequency spectrum $S_\kappa$ and detailed-balance convention exactly as stated in [[lem-tgr-thermal-contour-spectrum]]. The exponential ray map and the choice of $\kappa$ are model inputs. If $\xi$ and $\kappa$ are identified with a generator and geometric surface gravity of a particular horizon, that identification is an additional physical assumption; no collapse geometry, four-dimensional horizon restriction, scattering factor, or backreaction is derived here.

**Massless acceleration branch.** Adopt the massless scalar and Minkowski vacuum of [[post-qft-free-field-model]]. Use the actually defined temporal smearing along the smooth proper-time hyperbola and its tested covariance from [[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]]. The curve-smeared field is not a sharp-point field. Its accelerated spectrum and finite-switch coefficient are used only with the conditional hypotheses recorded in that lemma and in [[lem-tgr-spectral-thermometer]].

For either branch, select an energy gap $E>0$ joules and define a two-state, continuous-time rate model with ground state $g$, excited state $e$, and model-time parameter $t\ge0$ measured in seconds. In the reduced branch, no identification of $t$ with proper time along a spacetime curve is assumed. In the acceleration branch, take $t=\tau\ge0$ along the proper-time hyperbola supplied by [[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]]. In the reduced branch let $\gamma_{\rm red}>0$ have units metres per second and set $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(E/(\hbar c))$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(-E/(\hbar c))$. In the acceleration branch let $\gamma_{\rm acc}>0$ have units square metres per square second and set $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(E/\hbar)$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(-E/\hbar)$. Here $c>0$ is metres per second, $\hbar>0$ is joule-seconds, and the frequency arguments have units inverse metres and inverse seconds, respectively. These choices make both rates inverse seconds. The adopted population $p(t)$ of state $e$ is the solution of $p'(t)=r_\uparrow(1-p(t))-r_\downarrow p(t)$ with supplied $p(0)\in[0,1]$. This differential equation is the entire effective two-state model; the rates are adopted inputs, not exact QFT transition probabilities.

Only when a selected construction also supplies a density state and a normalized finite measurement instrument may an outcome be read using [[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]]. No such state, instrument, detector apparatus, or observed outcome is supplied here. The postulate asserts no general thermalization, exact all-order transition probability, KMS state, or experimental temperature reading.

items.physical_scope: Reference temperature calibration in the selected reduced exponential-current and two-state Markov model. A local stationary temperature formula applies only after the stated equilibrium assumption and reference match; no general Hawking or KMS theorem is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the reduced branch of [[post-tgr-exponential-current-and-spectral-thermometer]] with $\kappa>0$ in inverse metres. Let $E>0$ be an energy in joules, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $c>0$ in metres per second, $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and $\gamma_{\rm red}>0$ in metres per second. Put $\nu=E/(\hbar c)$ and use the adopted rates $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(\nu)$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(-\nu)$ in that postulate's two-state model. The unique stationary excited-state probability and its ratio are

$$p_* = \frac{1}{1+e^{2\pi E/(\hbar c\kappa)}},\qquad \frac{p_*}{1-p_*}=e^{-2\pi E/(\hbar c\kappa)}.$$

Define the model's effective reference temperature $T_{\rm red}>0$ by $p_*/(1-p_*)=e^{-E/(k_BT_{\rm red})}$. Then

$$T_{\rm red}=\frac{\hbar c\kappa}{2\pi k_B}.$$

Let $\xi$ be the same selected reference Killing field and $u$ its length flow parameter from [[post-tgr-exponential-current-and-spectral-thermometer]]. For the horizon interpretation, additionally supply a smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H$ in the domain of $\xi$, require $\chi:=\xi|_{\mathcal H}$ to be a nonzero tangent null generator with the same length-flow normalization, and assume $\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa\chi$ on $\mathcal H$ in the sense of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Under these additional identifications of both generator and constant geometric surface gravity, $T_{\rm red}$ is the reference temperature of that reduced horizon model. If, in addition, $\xi$ is future timelike on a connected open domain $O$, a selected stationary equilibrium of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] is adopted there with this same $\xi$, a reference event $x_{\rm ref}\in O$ has Killing lapse $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, and its local reference temperature is identified with $T_{\rm red}$, then its local proper-temperature field obeys $T(x)=T_{\rm red}/N_\xi(x)$ on $O$. These are conditional model deductions; the theorem establishes no horizon formation, general Hawking radiation, KMS state, detector thermalization, or empirical reading.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the massless acceleration branch of [[post-tgr-exponential-current-and-spectral-thermometer]] with proper acceleration $a>0$ in metres per square second, gap $E>0$ in joules, $c>0$ in metres per second, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and $\gamma_{\rm acc}>0$ in square metres per square second. The adopted rates are $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(E/\hbar)$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(-E/\hbar)$. The unique stationary excited-state probability of the defined two-state model and its effective temperature are

$$p_* = \frac{1}{1+e^{2\pi cE/(a\hbar)}},\qquad T_{\rm eff}=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}.$$

For any nonzero real $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ and switching duration $\mathsf T>0$ seconds, let $Q_{\mathsf T}^{(a)}(\nu)=R_{\mathsf T}^{(C_a)}(\nu)/(\mathsf T\|h\|_2^2)$ and $K_h=(2\pi\|h\|_2^2)^{-1}\int_\mathbb R|z||\widehat h(z)|^2dz$, with the definitions in [[lem-tgr-spectral-thermometer]]. For every $\nu\in\mathbb R$, the leading switched coefficient obeys $|Q_{\mathsf T}^{(a)}(\nu)-S_a(\nu)|\le\operatorname{Lip}(S_a)K_h/\mathsf T$. This is a coefficient estimate and does not assert an all-order transition probability.

On the Minkowski right Rindler wedge $W_R=\{(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):x^1>|x^0|\}$, use length coordinates $x^0=ct$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\rho=\sqrt{(x^1)^2-(x^0)^2}>0$, and the boost Killing field $\chi_\kappa=\kappa(x^1\partial_{x^0}+x^0\partial_{x^1})$ with $\kappa>0$ in inverse metres. Its lapse is $N=\sqrt{-\eta(\chi_\kappa,\chi_\kappa)}=\kappa\rho$. The orbit at fixed $\rho$ has proper acceleration $a(\rho)=c^2/\rho$, so the effective model temperature there is $T_U(\rho)=\hbar c/(2\pi k_B\rho)$. With reference event on $\rho_0=\kappa^{-1}$, $N(\rho_0)=1$ and $T_K^{\rm acc}:=T_U(\rho_0)=\hbar c\kappa/(2\pi k_B)$, hence $T_U(\rho)=T_K^{\rm acc}/N(\rho)$. On the future Rindler horizon $x^0=x^1>0$, direct differentiation gives $\nabla_{\chi_\kappa}\chi_\kappa=\kappa\chi_\kappa$, so the generator's $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ is $\kappa$ under the definition of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Rescaling $\chi_\kappa$ by $b>0$ rescales $N$ and $T_K^{\rm acc}$ by $b$ while leaving the proper model temperature unchanged.

If a selected stationary bath of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] is additionally adopted on $W_R$ with its selected Killing field identified with this same $\chi_\kappa$, and its reference proper temperature is identified with $T_U(\rho_0)$, then the bath's local proper temperature agrees with $T_U(\rho)$ by [[pthm-tgr-tolman-ehrenfest]]. Both identifications are extra model assumptions. No general Unruh-state, KMS, horizon-formation, Hawking-radiation, or empirical thermometer claim follows.

items.title: Restricted reversible horizon entropy identification
items.design_state: Draft authored for the reserved TGR-PHS03 inventory; current page requirements follow plan-spec.json, and exact supplier interfaces, dependency levels, and readiness blockers are recorded in batch-79 notes.
items.physical_scope: An additional reversible heat and entropy-state-function identification on the selected connected, strictly subextremal, zero-magnetic-flux stationary Kerr–Newman family, conditional on matching each member's reduced exponential-current branch parameter and Killing flow at each family point to that member's positive geometric surface gravity and generator normalization. It asserts no entropy microstate count, general Hawking or KMS result, dynamical-process law, or empirical reading.
items.statement:
Use the connected strict subextremal parameter domain
$\mathcal P:=\{(m,a,q)\in\mathbb R^3:m>0,\ m^2>a^2+q^2\},$
with its physical Kerr–Newman family and SI conversion as in [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]]. Fix positive constants $G_N$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $c$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and $k_B$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Write $E_{\rm par}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm J$, $A_H:\mathcal P\to\mathrm{m^2}$, $J_{\rm SI}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$, $Q_e:\mathcal P\to\mathrm C$, $\Omega_{\rm SI}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, and $\Phi_{\rm SI}:\mathcal P\to\mathrm V$ for the smooth parameter functions supplied by [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]].

Define the work-subtracted reversible heat one-form on $\mathcal P$ by
$$\delta Q_{\rm rev}:=dE_{\rm par}-\Omega_{\rm SI}\,dJ_{\rm SI}-\Phi_{\rm SI}\,dQ_e.$$
Here a one-form assigns a linear functional to each tangent direction in the family parameter domain; each term has units of joules. Let $S_H:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R$ be a $C^1$ function with values measured in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. It is a state function here in the explicit sense that its value is assigned to each family parameter point and does not depend on a path used to reach that point.

Assume the mathematical premise $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] required by the selected spectral supplier. This is not a physical postulate.

For $x=(m,a,q)\in\mathcal P$, define
$$s(x):=\sqrt{m^2-a^2-q^2},\qquad r_+(x):=m+s(x),\qquad D(x):=r_+(x)^2+a^2.$$
On the selected smooth ingoing Kerr–Newman spacetime belonging to the family member $x$, write $\chi_x$ for the selected horizon generator with the length-flow parameter and reference normalization of [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]]. Let $\nabla^{(x)}$ denote the Levi-Civita connection of that member's metric. By that supplier and the conditional geometric definition in [[def-tgr-framework-units]],
$$\nabla^{(x)}_{\chi_x}\chi_x=\kappa_{\rm geom}(x)\chi_x,\qquad \kappa_{\rm geom}:\mathcal P\to(0,\infty),\qquad \kappa_{\rm geom}(x):=\frac{s(x)}{D(x)},$$
where the connection is taken on the spacetime indexed by the family point, not on the parameter domain $\mathcal P$.
This is a smooth positive family map with values in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Put $\kappa_{\rm acc}(x):=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}(x)$, in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, as in the SI family theorem.

For each fixed $x\in\mathcal P$, use a reduced exponential-current branch instance of [[pthm-tgr-reduced-horizon-temperature]] whose Killing flow field is identified with $\chi_x$ and whose length-flow normalization is the family member's. The reference event is fixed within that instance as required by the PHS02 branch model. The branch instance satisfies the supplier's positive energy-gap, positive $\gamma_{\rm red}$, and two-state-rate hypotheses; its scalar inverse-length parameter is held constant at $\kappa=\kappa_{\rm geom}(x)$. Let $T_{\rm red}(x)$ denote that instance's effective reference temperature. The supplier gives
$$T_{\rm red}(x)=\frac{\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}(x)}{2\pi k_B}.$$
Adopt the additional reference-temperature identification $T_K:\mathcal P\to(0,\infty)$, $T_K(x):=T_{\rm red}(x)$, so
$$T_K(x)=\frac{\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}(x)}{2\pi k_B}=\frac{\hbar\kappa_{\rm acc}(x)}{2\pi c k_B}.$$
Thus $T_K$ is a smooth family map with values in kelvins. At a fixed family point $x$, the unparameterized symbol $T_K$ denotes the value $T_K(x)$. It names only the selected reference scale in the reversible relation; it is not a local proper-temperature field and does not assert a stationary bath, a KMS state, or an observed detector reading.

Adopt the reversible thermodynamic identification
$$\delta Q_{\rm rev}=T_K\,dS_H$$
as an equality of one-forms on $\mathcal P$: at each $x\in\mathcal P$ and $v\in T_x\mathcal P$, it means $\delta Q_{\rm rev}(x)[v]=T_K(x)\,dS_H(x)[v]$. This physical identification is an additional assumption. The geometric family identity and the reduced effective-temperature model do not by themselves assert it. No global entropy zero or identification with a quantum-gravity microstate count or an unrenormalized outside-state entropy is adopted.

Thus $t_{\mathrm{cross}}$ has units of seconds and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}$ is dimensionless. This is a diagnostic defined from the adopted mass ODE and the chosen length scale $r_H/c$; it is not a measured crossing time, an estimate of error against a time-dependent Einstein solution, or a proof that the ideal model approximates such a solution.

items.title: Exact quasistatic and finite-interval mass-change bounds
items.design_state: Added on the assigned A page because the PHS09 scope requires the exact diagnostic and finite-interval mass-change bound; this complete argument uses mathematical dependencies only.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $G,c,\hbar,\eta,M_0,M_{\min}>0$ be the relevant constants and initial/cutoff data of [[prop-tgr-ideal-evaporation-accounting]], with $0<\eta\leq1$ and $0<M_{\min}<M_0$. Let
$$
M(t_\infty)=(M_0^3-3\alpha t_\infty)^{1/3}, \qquad \alpha=\frac{\eta\hbar c^4}{15360\pi G^2}, \qquad \tau=\frac{M_0^3-M_{\min}^3}{3\alpha}
$$
be the positive solution and cutoff supplied by that proposition.
Use the diagnostic of [[def-tgr-emitter-quasistatic-diagnostic]]. Then
$$
\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}(t_\infty)=\frac{2G\alpha}{c^3M(t_\infty)^2} \leq\frac{2G\alpha}{c^3M_{\min}^2}.
$$
For any $\epsilon_0>0$, the condition $M_{\min}^2\geq2G\alpha/(c^3\epsilon_0)$ therefore implies $\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}(t_\infty)\leq\epsilon_0$ throughout $[0,\tau]$.

There is also an exact finite-interval bound. If $0\leq t_\infty\leq t_\infty+\Delta t\leq\tau$ and
$$
\delta:=\frac{3\alpha\Delta t}{M(t_\infty)^3}\leq\frac12,
$$
then
$$
\frac{M(t_\infty+\Delta t)}{M(t_\infty)}=(1-\delta)^{1/3}, \qquad \left|\frac{M(t_\infty+\Delta t)}{M(t_\infty)}-1\right| \leq\frac{2^{2/3}}{3}\,\delta.
$$
Both bounds are exact internal consequences of the adopted ODE. They give no error bound between that ODE and an unconstructed Einstein–quantum backreaction solution.

items.statement:
Use SI constants $G_N>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\hbar>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. In [[prop-tgr-ideal-evaporation-accounting]], the mathematical constant $G$ is identified with this same $G_N$.

For each fixed mass $M>0$ in kilograms, take the zero-angular-momentum, zero-charge member of the selected Kerr–Newman stationary family [[pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics]], with geometric mass length $m=G_NM/c^2$ in metres. In the Schwarzschild exterior use coordinates $(x^0,r,\vartheta,\varphi)$, $x^0=ct_\infty$ in metres, $r>2m$, and metric
$$
ds^2=-\left(1-\frac{2m}{r}\right)(dx^0)^2+ \left(1-\frac{2m}{r}\right)^{-1}dr^2+r^2d\Omega_2^2,
$$
where $d\Omega_2^2$ is the unit-sphere metric. The asymptotic generator is $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$, with $g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ at infinity. The selected stationary-family radius, area, and geometric surface gravity are
$$
r_H(M)=2m=\frac{2G_NM}{c^2},\qquad A_H(M)=4\pi r_H(M)^2,\qquad \kappa_{\rm geom}(M)=\frac{1}{4m}=\frac{c^2}{4G_NM}.
$$
Thus $r_H$ is in metres, $A_H$ in $\mathrm{m^2}$, and $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, using the length-normalized generator convention of [[def-tgr-framework-units]].

Adopt the selected reduced-model reference temperature from [[post-tgr-thermodynamic-horizon-identification]] on this Schwarzschild subfamily:
$$
T_\infty(M):=T_K=T_{\rm red} =\frac{\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}(M)}{2\pi k_B} =\frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi G_NMk_B}>0.
$$
This is an adopted model identification for one fixed asymptotic reference. It is not a local proper-temperature field and does not assert a general Hawking state. The reversible entropy state $S_H$ is the value of the stationary-family state function on each Schwarzschild member; evaluating that family function along a changing parameter $M(t_\infty)$ is bookkeeping in this model, not a claim that the changing family is an exact spacetime solution.

Adopt the zero-mode-excluded, zero-point-subtracted, two-polarization photon Gibbs model and isotropic freely streaming ray convention of [[thm-tgr-photon-planck-flux]], under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]]. Its energy density $u$, coarse diagonal-mode entropy density $s$, and one-sided fluxes are those of that theorem. This identification is an ideal reservoir assumption; no photon-wall equilibration theorem or physical preparation is asserted.

Fix $0<\eta\leq1$, a constant dimensionless active-area fraction, an initial mass $M_0>0$, and a positive cutoff $0<M_{\min}<M_0$. Let $M(t_\infty)>0$ be $C^1$ on an interval containing its first cutoff time $\tau$, with $M(0)=M_0$, and let $t_\infty$ be measured in seconds by the fixed asymptotic time parameter. Define $E_\infty(t_\infty)=M(t_\infty)c^2$ in joules and the effective far-field emitting area
$$
A_{\rm eff}(M):=\eta A_H(M).
$$
Adopt zero incoming flux, the power law $P_\infty=A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_\infty^4$ in watts, the balance equation
$$
\frac{dE_\infty}{dt_\infty}=c^2M'(t_\infty)=-P_\infty(t_\infty),
$$
and the coarse exported entropy rate $S_{\rm rad}'=(4/3)P_\infty/T_\infty$, with $S_{\rm rad}(0)=0$. Here $S_{\rm rad}$ is the entropy carried by the ideal Gibbs/ray model, not an outside von Neumann entropy. The effective area is not a material patch of the null horizon and $\eta$ is not a frequency-independent greybody factor applied separately to entropy.

The model holds only for the fixed normalization $\xi$. Under $\xi\mapsto b\xi$, $b>0$, the model conventions scale $E_\xi\mapsto bE_\xi$, $t_\xi\mapsto t_\xi/b$, $\kappa_{\rm geom}\mapsto b\kappa_{\rm geom}$, and leave $A_H$ unchanged. The Stefan closure above is therefore not stipulated as a reference-independent luminosity law. items.title: Conditional ideal Planck emission and entropy accounting
items.design_state: Authored from the exact TGR-PHS04 reservation and PHS09 route; the MHS04 results and PHS03 area-entropy interface are used conditionally with AC_omega explicit.
items.statement:
Assume the ideal model and fixed asymptotic normalization of [[post-tgr-photon-emitter-and-quasistatic-balance]], and explicitly assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. Use $G=G_N$ between the mathematical ODE input and the physical Schwarzschild family. Also assume the conditional family-entropy interface stated by [[pthm-tgr-area-entropy-calibration]] with its actual hypotheses. Let $S_H(M)$ denote that state-function value at the stationary Schwarzschild member of mass $M$, and put
$$
\Delta S_H:=S_H(M_0)-S_H(M_{\min}).
$$
For the fixed-reference effective-area model,
$$
P_\infty(M)=\frac{\eta\hbar c^6}{15360\pi G_N^2M^2}, \qquad \alpha=\frac{\eta\hbar c^4}{15360\pi G_N^2}, \qquad M(t_\infty)=(M_0^3-3\alpha t_\infty)^{1/3}, \qquad \tau=\frac{M_0^3-M_{\min}^3}{3\alpha}.
$$
The model exports energy $c^2(M_0-M_{\min})$ joules, and its coarse photon entropy satisfies
$$
S_H(M)=\frac{4\pi k_BG_NM^2}{\hbar c}+s_*, \qquad s_*\in\mathbb R\ \text{constant on the stationary family},
$$
$$
S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=\frac43\Delta S_H>0, \qquad \Delta(S_H+S_{\rm rad})=\frac13\Delta S_H>0.
$$
The absolute entropy offsets in the mathematical ODE model and the stationary-family state function need not be identified; their differences agree because both have the same area coefficient on this branch.

For the diagnostic of [[def-tgr-emitter-quasistatic-diagnostic]],
$$
\epsilon_{\rm qs}(t_\infty)=\frac{2G_N\alpha}{c^3M(t_\infty)^2}, \qquad \sup_{0\leq t_\infty\leq\tau}\epsilon_{\rm qs} =\frac{2G_N\alpha}{c^3M_{\min}^2}.
$$
Thus $M_{\min}^2\geq2G_N\alpha/(c^3\epsilon_0)$ implies $\epsilon_{\rm qs}\leq\epsilon_0$ for any $\epsilon_0>0$. The finite-interval bound in [[lem-tgr-emitter-quasistatic-bounds]] also applies whenever its stated $\delta\leq1/2$ condition holds.

The Stefan closure is tied to the fixed reference: under $\xi\mapsto b\xi$, power scales as $b^2$, while $T_\xi^4$ scales as $b^4$ and area is unchanged. This is an exact conditional model calculation, not a Hawking-radiation theorem, a time-dependent Einstein solution, a backreaction error estimate, an observed evaporation history, or a universal generalized second law.

items.title: Ideal active-area half-mass cutoff interval
items.design_state: Authored from the exact TGR-PHS04 B reservation as a conditional half-mass cutoff calculation, with no empirical observation.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the conditional model conclusion of [[pthm-tgr-ideal-photon-emission]]. Choose $\eta=1$ and $M_{\min}=M_0/2$ for $M_0>0$, with $G_N,c,\hbar,k_B$ as in that theorem. Define the model's algebraic zero-mass time scale
$$
t_*:=\frac{M_0^3}{3\alpha} =\frac{5120\pi G_N^2M_0^3}{\hbar c^4}.
$$
The stipulated model stops earlier, at
$$
\tau=\frac78t_*=\frac{4480\pi G_N^2M_0^3}{\hbar c^4},
$$
when its mass parameter first reaches $M_0/2>0$. It exports energy $c^2M_0/2$ joules. Its stationary-family entropy drop, coarse photon entropy export, and total coarse entropy gain are respectively
$$
\Delta S_H=\frac{3\pi k_BG_NM_0^2}{\hbar c},\qquad S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=\frac{4\pi k_BG_NM_0^2}{\hbar c},\qquad \Delta(S_H+S_{\rm rad})=\frac{\pi k_BG_NM_0^2}{\hbar c}.
$$
For any $\epsilon_0>0$, if $M_0^2\geq\hbar c/(1920\pi G_N\epsilon_0)$, then the model's maximum diagnostic on the closed interval $[0,\tau]$, including its positive cutoff endpoint, satisfies $\epsilon_{\rm qs}\leq\epsilon_0$. This is an exact ideal-model calculation, not a measured evaporation time or an error estimate for a gravitational backreaction solution.
